parameters.name: workspace_ids
parameters.description:
Comma-separated workspace ids to include (UUIDs). Applies to every `kind`
(LLM / MCP / web) via the shared `gateway_audit.workspace_id`. Omit for
all workspaces.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description:
Exact-match filter on `gateway_audit.request_id`. Used by deep-links
from the tool-calls / mcp-tool-calls feeds (`/audit?request_id=…`) so
a single row can be focused and auto-expanded. Applies to every `kind`.

parameters.name: jti
parameters.description:
Exact-match filter on `gateway_audit.key_id` interpreted as a spec-OAuth
`jti`. The proxy stamps the JWT's `jti` straight into `key_id` for
OAuth-authenticated MCP requests (see `proxy/mcp/spec_oauth.rs`), so an
operator deep-linking from the Tokens view (`/audit?kind=mcp&jti=…`)
lands on exactly that token's traffic. Only meaningful on `kind=mcp`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
Row family to return. Default `llm`; `mcp` returns MCP gateway rows;
`all` interleaves both by timestamp.

parameters.name: methods
parameters.description:
MCP-side method filter (comma-separated). Whitelisted at the handler
level. The Tool Calls feed (`/tool-calls`) sends
`methods=tools/call,resources/read,prompts/get` to narrow `kind=mcp`
to the three caller-addressable methods. Empty / unset means no
filter. Ignored on the LLM side.

parameters.name: tool_id
parameters.description:
MCP-side: filter to a single canonical `tool_id` (from the field-
profile registry). Used by Top-Tools deep-links from the dashboards.

parameters.name: resource_uri
parameters.description: MCP-side: filter to a single resource URI. Substring match.

parameters.name: prompt_id
parameters.description: MCP-side: filter to a single prompt id. Exact match.

parameters.name: virtual_server_id
parameters.description:
MCP-side: filter to one virtual server (mount slug → UUID via
`mcp_virtual_servers.id`). Used by Top-Endpoints deep-links.

parameters.name: upstream_server_id
parameters.description:
MCP-side: filter to one upstream server (`mcp_upstream_servers.id`).
Used by Top-Upstreams deep-links.

parameters.name: upstream_server
parameters.description:
LLM-side: filter to one upstream server by name (joined via
`upstream_servers.name`). Used by the LLM dashboard Top-Servers
deep-link.

parameters.name: api_version
parameters.description:
LLM-side: filter to one wire protocol (`chat_completions` /
`responses` / `anthropic_messages` / `google_gemini`). Bound on
`llm_audit.api_version`. Used by Proxy dashboard per-protocol
drill-downs.

parameters.name: has_blocked
parameters.description:
LLM-side: when true, restrict to rows whose `llm_audit.badges` carry a
response-phase `tool_blocked` event — i.e. tool calls the policy engine
suppressed. Powers the Dashboard Overview's "Blocked tools" attention
tile click-through. Ignored on MCP / web kinds.

parameters.name: has_guardrail
parameters.description:
When true, restrict to rows whose `badges` carry a `guardrail` event —
the inline injection guardrail flagged untrusted web content. Applies to
the `llm` kind (content folded back into a model on the substitution
loop) and the `web` kind (direct `/mcp/web` observe scan); ignored on
`mcp`. Powers the Dashboard Overview's "Web guardrail" attention tile
click-through.

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: Web-side: filter to one dispatch surface. Whitelisted at the handler.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: Web-side: filter to one operation kind. Whitelisted at the handler.

parameters.name: agent_slug
parameters.description:
A2A-side: filter to one registered agent by its **slug** — the agent's
public identifier everywhere else in the product (the `/a2a/<slug>` mount,
the `a2a_agent_filter` policy pivot, the dashboard's by-agent key), so a
deep-link from any of those surfaces lands here unchanged.

parameters.name: task_state
parameters.description:
A2A-side: filter to one `TASK_STATE_*`. Whitelisted at the handler, so an
unknown value can't reach the inline SQL literal.

post.summary:
Render a draft profile against the validation placeholder dictionary,
without saving it.
post.description:
Deliberately the same code path as save-time validation — including the
delivery rules — so a preview that comes back clean IS a save that will
pass, and a preview that 400s names exactly what a save would reject.

400.description: A body or companion failed to render

post.summary:
Restore every builtin profile from disk, forced over any prior operator
edit and clearing every soft-deletion.
post.description:
This is the one path that reclaims a user-edited builtin — seed-sync
deliberately leaves `is_builtin = false` rows alone — and the only route the
UI has back to a builtin the operator deleted, since a suppressed row is
filtered out of every read and so has no row to act on (the per-id reset
still restores one, addressing the seed id rather than the stored row).

A user-created profile is preserved UNLESS it occupies a seed key, which the
restore force-writes; `custom_preserved` counts only the rows that survive,
so the impact never reports a row both restored and kept.

get.summary:

what the API will actually accept.

post.summary: End every console session for the calling account.
post.description:
Deleting the cookie is the browser's half and the gateway cannot see it; this
is the half that makes the token stop working. Without it a session someone
copied outlives sign-out by up to `JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS`, and the only remedy is
disabling the account.

The grain is the account within its tenant, not the one browser that asked —
so signing out on a shared machine also ends the session on the laptop that
was left logged in, which is the behaviour someone reaching for "sign out"
after losing a device needs. Other tenants' sessions for the same person live
in their own `admin_accounts` rows and are untouched.

Requires a live session: `validate_session_token` refuses a token that a
previous sign-out already revoked, so a repeat call answers 401 rather than
re-stamping the watermark. That refusal is the point — a re-stamp moves the
watermark forward and would take out any session established since, turning
a copied token into a way to keep someone signed out. The browser tier
ignores the status: its cookies go either way.

This endpoint takes an identity on a caller's word: the bearer secret proves

path no longer uses it — it verifies the provider's signature in-process —
so it is off unless an operator turns it on for a deployment that drives

post.summary: The subject refused the grant (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 `access_denied`).
post.description:
A denial is an authorization *response*, so this server builds it — the same
function that builds every other error redirect, carrying the same
byte-exact RFC 9207 `iss` an approval would. Assembling it in the browser
tier instead meant a second implementation of one wire format, kept in step
by nothing, and the consent page needing to be told this server's identity
so it could quote it back.

The full parameter bundle is re-validated first, and that is not ceremony:
without it an attacker could craft an authorize URL naming a real client
with an attacker-controlled `redirect_uri`, bait a Deny click, and bounce the
visitor anywhere from a page wearing the tenant's own branding. No token
leaks — but the bounce itself is the phishing primitive. A bundle that fails
to validate is refused inline rather than redirected.

get.summary: The public half of this tenant's MCP token-signing keys (RFC 7517).
get.description:
Unauthenticated by design — this is a *public* key set, and a client that
has to authenticate to fetch one gains nothing from local verification.

The document is derived, never stored: the keys come from the same ring that
signs, so there is no state that could drift out of step with the tokens in
circulation, and rotating `AUTH_SECRET` changes what is published here on
the next request with no migration or key-distribution step.

RFC 7009 §2.2: revocation answers 200 even for a token that is invalid,
expired, already revoked, or belongs to someone else. Reporting the
difference would turn this endpoint into an oracle for whether a token is
live, and the caller's goal — "this token must not work" — is satisfied
either way.

Header-mode portal login: exchanges X-Auth-Request-* headers for a portal JWT.
Auto-provisions or links user accounts. Triggers OIDC group sync.
get.description:
SECURITY: reachable only under the deployment-wide `AUTH_MODE=header`, or —
when `ALLOW_OIDC_CLAIM_EXCHANGE` is on — to a caller presenting
`INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET`. Anything else gets a 404, so an exposed admin-api
port cannot be driven by forged headers.

The secret is *caller* authentication everywhere else in this deployment; on
this endpoint it is also *identity* proof, because past it the caller names
the user and the tenant and gets a session for them. That is the same
authority the admin plane's `oidc_exchange` grants, so it stands behind the
same operator opt-in and is likewise absent by default. Header mode is
unaffected: there the reverse proxy is the authentication and no secret is
involved.

200.description: Header-mode login successful, returns JWT and user info

404.description: Not available in standard auth mode

get.summary:
OAuth provider redirects here after user consent. The handler:
  1. validates the `state` (binds to the requesting user + upstream),
  2. exchanges the `code` at the IdP token endpoint with the PKCE verifier,
  3. encrypts + UPSERTs into `mcp_user_credentials`,
  4. deletes the pending row,
  5. redirects the browser to `/portal/t/<slug>/mcp/connections?connected=...`.
get.description:
On any failure, the user is redirected to the connections page with
`?error=<short-code>` so the portal UI can show a toast.

parameters.name: iss
parameters.description:
RFC 9207 authorization-server issuer identifier.

Optional on the wire because not every authorization server sends it,
but when one does it MUST be checked before the code is redeemed —
that check is what closes the mix-up attack the parameter exists for.
An attacker-controlled authorization server otherwise hands us a code
we carry to an honest server's token endpoint, redeeming its
credential on the attacker's behalf.

agent_card.description:
Cached upstream agent card (raw). Feeds the admin UI's card preview +
skill catalog; the proxy rewrites it before serving to A2A clients.

A2aArtifactView.description: One artifact an A2A agent produced, projected into canonical blocks.

A2aAuditLogEntry.description:
A2A-side audit row exposed at `/audit?kind=a2a`. Per-call shape with the
joined agent slug/name + user email so the audit UI renders rows without
a fan-out fetch. Operators correlate calls in the same A2A conversation
by the raw `a2a_context_id` (and one unit of remote work by `a2a_task_id`).

a2a_context_id.description: Raw wire `contextId` — the per-protocol conversation correlator.

badges.description: Typed audit badges — same `AuditBadge` enum as LLM/MCP rows.

error_category.description:
Gateway-level error class shared with the LLM/MCP rows (`upstream`,
`rpc_error`, `cancelled`, …) — what the error dashboards aggregate on.

error_detail.description:
Why the call failed, in prose. On a streamed call this is where a
mid-stream break, a malformed event, or the byte cap is recorded.

params.description:
JSON-RPC `params` payload as the client sent it (polymorphic per
method — `SendMessage` carries the message envelope, task ops the id).

result.description:
JSON-RPC `result` payload from the agent (Task | Message | card —
polymorphic per method). NULL on error replies.

session_id.description:
Hashed session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — cross-protocol
correlation with LLM/MCP rows sharing the client's `X-Session-Id`.

stream_events.description:
Streaming calls: accumulated `StreamResponse` envelopes. NULL for
non-streaming methods.

oneOf.description: What the policy engine and the inline guardrail did to this call.

A2aBreakdownItem.description: One row of an A2A breakdown panel.

filter_id.description:
The value a deep-link filters on, when it differs from the displayed
`key`. The user pivot displays a name but filters by `user_id`; every
other pivot's key IS its filter value (an agent's slug, a method, a task
state) and leaves this `None`. A panel row must never link on a label —
a display name is not a filter, and the audit list would come back empty.

key.description:
Pivot value — an agent slug, a method, a task state, or a user's display
name. Always TEXT so one component renders every panel.

total_calls.description:
Calls across every group, before the top-N cut — the denominator the UI
renders shares against.

agents.description: Distinct agents addressed in the window.

blocked.description: Calls tool policy refused before they reached the agent.

errors.description: HTTP 4xx/5xx or a JSON-RPC error code.

guardrail_flagged.description: Calls carrying at least one inline-guardrail finding (either direction).

tasks.description: Distinct remote tasks the calls created or addressed.

A2aPolicyFinding.description: One policy rule that fired on an agent call, and where.

phase.description: `request` (the message the caller sent) or `response` (the agent's reply).

A2aTransformDiff.description:
`a2a_audit.transform_diff` — what the gateway did to an agent call.

Both lists, because both phases can fire on one call: a rule may rewrite the
outbound message *and* another rewrite the reply, and an operator looking at a
modified call has to see both.

guardrail_steps.description:
Inline-guardrail findings on this call — the caller's message (request
phase) and the agent's reply (response phase) each produce their own.

ActionImpact.description:
What a side-effecting action did, reported in [`ActionResponse::impact`].
One type for every action, so the spec states the shape; an action sets
only the fields it reports and the rest are absent from the body.

builtins_restored.description: Reset to seed: builtins written back.

custom_preserved.description: Reset to seed: custom rows kept.

deleted_builtins_cleared.description: Reset to seed: deleted builtins brought back.

downstreams.description: Model or server delete: the downstream providers that lost a route.

items_restored.description: Profile reset: content items the profile holds again.

keys_moved.description: QoS class delete: keys moved to the replacement class.

keys_revoked.description:
Member removal: the member's keys in the workspace that were revoked.
Server delete: the keys bound to its pass-through, revoked.

models_unlinked.description:
Catalog delete: upstream models whose explicit link named the entry,
unlinked so they auto-match again.

orphaned_routes.description: Model or server delete: curated downstream routes left without a model.

overrides_removed.description: Server delete: the model overrides of its pass-through, deleted.

program_id.description: Suggestion approval: the transform program it installed.

route_targets_moved.description: QoS class delete: route targets moved to the replacement class.

routes_uncached.description: Cache preset delete: routes that now serve uncached.

workspaces_moved.description: QoS class delete: workspaces moved to the replacement class.

workspaces_ungranted.description: Server delete: the workspace grants of its pass-through, removed.

oneOf.description: What the action did, as counts. Each action sets only the fields it reports.

AdaptiveLive.description: A learned in-flight limit across the replicas that report it.

auto_itl_target_ms.description:
What an automatic token-latency target holds this engine to:
`AUTO_ITL_TARGET_RATIO` times `low_load_itl_ms` — the figure each
replica applies is its own, and this one the slowest. `null` until
learned: an automatic target holds nothing until then. Reported
whatever the server's setting.

limit.description:
The limits the replicas apply now, summed — `null` while any of them
applies none (its engine unheard and no ceiling set).

low_load_itl_ms.description:
The engine's time between tokens while it ran one or two requests per
rank, in milliseconds: the slowest figure any replica learned. `null`
until one has.

state.description: The most pressing state any replica reports (`AdaptiveState::pressure`).

AdaptiveState.description:
What the window did on the latest reading, as an operator reads it.

It rides the heartbeat and is stored as text, so a state this build does
not know reads as `Unknown` rather than failing the whole report.

actor_key_id.description:
The `ak-` key id when `actor_kind='admin_key'`; `null` for humans.
Answers "which automation did this?" independently of the owning account.

change_diff.description:
Structured before/after snapshot stamped by handlers that pre-load
the row they're about to mutate. Shape: `{ "before": <row>, "after":
<row> }`, or `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n> }` when it was too
large to keep. NULL for handlers that haven't opted in (most creates /
deletes) or when nothing actually changed.

request_body.description:
Redacted request body. `null` when the inbound body was empty or
non-JSON. The middleware redacts known secret-shaped keys (password,
api_key, token, …) before insert.

response_error.description:
Typed error body (`{code, message}`) the handler returned on a non-2xx
status. NULL on success. Lets the log show WHY a call failed, not just
its status_code.

AdoptCatalogEntry.description: Request body for adopting a catalog entry.

credential.description:
Shared bearer token — required when the entry's `auth_mode` is
`service_account`. Encrypted at rest.

oauth_client_id.description: OAuth client id/secret to register on the upstream (per_user_oauth).

slug.description:
Slug for the new `/mcp/<slug>` endpoint. Defaults to a slugified name;
a numeric suffix is appended on collision.

workspace_ids.description: Workspaces to grant the new endpoint to.

oneOf.description:
What the agent's own calls cost over the window, and in which currency.
`null` when the window straddles a change of the tenant's accounting
currency.

AgentModelEntry.description:
One judge-model option: an alias, which is the value an expert profile's
`model` (or an expert's override) stores and the agent sends, with every
enabled route it resolves to whose model can answer the judge (not an image,
audio, video, embedding or rerank model). An alias appears once however many
routes carry it (an alias may load-balance across presets on one provider,
or be carried by several providers).

granted_to_agent.description:
Whether the Agent workspace holds a live grant on a provider carrying
the alias. `false` means the gateway refuses the agent's analysis
calls on it until a provider is granted to the Agent workspace.

targets.description: The distinct (server, upstream model) pairs behind the alias, never empty.

AgentModelTarget.description: One upstream model a judge-model alias resolves to, and the server serving it.

granted_to_agent.description:
Whether the Agent workspace holds a live grant on a provider routing the
alias to this target. Only such a target can serve the agent's calls.

key_id.description:
`Some` once the tenant's agent key has been provisioned (it lives in the
Agent workspace and reaches the providers granted to it). `None` before then.

models.description:
One entry per alias with at least one such route, ordered by alias —
the judge-model options for an expert profile's `model` (and
per-expert overrides).

AlertLevel.description:
Severity of an agent-emitted session alert.

`Info` is the default emission floor — a neutral annotation that doesn't
demand operator action. `Minor` requires specific evidence; `Major` is
reserved for active exploitation or destructive operations.

AliasCollision.description:
An alias that resolves to more than one distinct upstream model across more
than one provider — a silent load-balance that's usually a misconfiguration.

analyzed_through.description:
How far the profile's enabled experts have analyzed: the oldest of their
cursors. `null` while any of them has no position yet.

furthest_through.description:
The newest of those cursors. A restart earlier than this analyzes again
what at least one expert already analyzed.

restartable.description:
False when a restart would move nothing: the profile runs no enabled
expert that reads sessions, or no workspace uses it.

workspaces.description:
The workspaces a restart moves: analysis keeps one cursor per expert and
profile, so it moves for every workspace using this profile. The Default
also covers sessions attributed to no workspace.

AnalysisStartWorkspace.description: A workspace an expert profile's analysis covers.

ApiErrorBody.description: Error details within an API error response.

ApiErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable error code enum. Ships in OpenAPI so clients can branch on
a stable identifier instead of parsing error messages. **Append-only: never
rename a variant** — mint a new one and let the old one fall out of use.
Every error body outside the RFC-shaped OAuth endpoints is an
`ApiErrorResponse` carrying one of these; a client branches on the code,
never on the message.

ApiErrorResponse.description: Structured error response body matching the proxy's `ErrorResponse` format.

ApiVersion.description: API version detected from request path.

AppInfo.description: Metadata for a known AI coding client.

builtin.description: Whether this entry is built-in (true) or user-defined (false).

prompt_patterns.description:
Substrings of the opening of the system prompt (case-insensitive), tried
only when no header named the app. Each is at least
`MIN_PROMPT_PATTERN_CHARS` characters: it is tried against every
unclassified request, so a short one would claim other clients' traffic.

referer_patterns.description: Referer domain substrings used for detection (case-insensitive).

level.description: `none`, `soft` or `hard`; `unknown` when the disk cannot be read.

ApplianceEvent.description:
One entry of the daemon's event journal: what happened to the appliance, as
the daemon (and its health gate) wrote it — a job started, ended or lost, a
reboot scheduled or cancelled, a boot started or judged, the install
finished or failed. One shape for every kind; a field a kind does not carry
is absent.

by.description: The job that scheduled the reboot; absent when it was asked for directly.

job.description: The job, by its start (the job's `started`).

kept.description: Why a boot found unhealthy keeps running.

kind.description:
`job.started`, `job.ended`, `job.lost`, `reboot.scheduled`,
`reboot.cancelled`, `boot.started`, `boot.judged`, `install.finished`,
`install.failed`, `backup.config` (a backup setting this console
changed); a kind a newer daemon adds passes through.

on_trial.description: A judged boot ran an upgrade's new system on trial.

reason.description:
Why: a job lost, a reboot cancelled, a boot judged, an install failed;
for `backup.config`, the settings this console changed.

oneOf.description:
A job that ended done: the reboot (or power-off) it scheduled, journaled
before it runs; absent when the job schedules none.

result.description: What a job that ended done found (the backup test's verdict).

seq.description: Its number, increasing for the journal's life.

ApplianceEventReboot.description: The reboot a job scheduled as its last step.

ApplianceEvents.description:
The journal's entries after a number — a cursor feed, not a page: the
client asks again after `next`.

events.description: Oldest first; at most a few hundred.

last.description:
The journal's last entry. An answer is capped: ask again after `next`,
not after this.

next.description:
The number to ask after next: past every entry answered (one this side
cannot read included), or the floor of a truncated answer.

truncated.description:
The journal no longer holds the entry after `after` — entries were
dropped, or the journal started again below it; `next` already accounts
for it, and the entries still held after it are in `events`.

ApplianceFailedBoot.description: The last boot the health gate found unhealthy.

kept.description:
Set when the gate kept the failed system because going back was refused;
the reason it was refused.

ApplianceJob.description: The daemon's last job (an upgrade, a rollback, a backup).

log_total.description: Lines the job logged in all.

result.description: What a job that is done found (the backup test's verdict).

started.description:
When the job started: its identity, telling two jobs of one kind and
target apart. Absent when none ran.

state.description: `idle` (none ran since the daemon started), `running`, `done` or `failed`.

oneOf.description:
The network given at install, which **Reset to install settings**
returns to; absent on an appliance whose install did not record it.
The override set here; absent when none is.

ApplianceNetworkConfig.description:
Network settings. `address` (IPv4, with its prefix, `192.168.1.50/24`) and
`gateway` are static only; `ipv6` turns IPv6 on in either mode (off, the
link has none), with an optional static `address6` beside the advertised
ones and its `gateway6`; `dns` replaces the lease's resolvers.

ApplianceNetworkLive.description:
The network the appliance runs, as the kernel and the resolver report it —
never read from a config file.

addresses.description: The interface's global IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, with their prefix.

gateways6.description: The IPv6 default routes' gateways, static or advertised (a router each).

ApplianceNetworkPending.description:
A change awaiting confirmation: past `deadline`, `previous` comes back
(absent: the install-time settings).

ApplianceNetworkUpdate.description:
The new settings. Optional fields are omitted on the wire when absent: the
daemon decodes strictly, and an omitted `revert_secs` takes its default.

address.description: Static only. The IPv4 address with its prefix: `192.168.1.50/24`.

address6.description:
A static IPv6 address with its prefix, beside the advertised ones;
needs `ipv6`.

dns.description: Resolvers, in preference order; empty keeps the lease's own.

gateway.description: Static only. Inside the address's own subnet.

gateway6.description:
The IPv6 gateway (link-local, or in `address6`'s subnet); needs
`address6`.

ipv6.description:
IPv6 on, in either mode: router advertisements (and DHCPv6 with
`dhcp`) address the link. Off, the appliance has no IPv6. Required: a
change states IPv6 whole, so a body without it is refused rather than
read as off.

revert_secs.description:
Seconds an addressing change has to be confirmed in before it is undone:
default 90, `0` for none, else 30 to 3600. A resolver-only change arms
nothing.

ApplianceRollbackPlan.description:
What going back would do: the release running now, and the one the fallback
system carries.

ApplianceStatus.description:
The appliance at a glance — the page header, its Software card and the
storage tiles.

boot.description: The system that booted: `active`, `passive` (the fallback) or `recovery`.

boot_id.description: The kernel's id of this boot: it changes with every reboot.

channel.description: The release channel the appliance follows.

events.description:
The event journal's last entry (0 before the first): a client reads the
status, then follows `…/events?after=` from here. Absent when the journal
cannot be read — never a made-up 0, which would replay it all.

events_error.description: Why the journal cannot be read, when it cannot.

fallback.description:
The appliance runs its fallback system: the last upgrade's boot failed its
health gate, or a rollback chose it.

install_failed.description: Why the boot's install failed, as the daemon says it.

oneOf.description: The release the install runs; absent before the first install finished.

installing.description:
The boot's install runs: its services are coming up, or a first install
finishes.

on_trial.description:
The boot runs an upgrade's new system, which the health gate has not
judged yet: healthy, it is kept; not, the appliance goes back (or keeps
it, as `failed_boot` then says).

os.description: The release the running OS carries.

reboot_pending.description: A reboot or power-off is scheduled.

ApplianceUpdates.description: The release an upgrade would install.

available.description: The target comes after the running release and may be installed.

left_by_rollback.description: The appliance went back from the target, and does not upgrade to it again.

ApproveSuggestionRequest.description:
The content a reviewer approves: the suggestion's `content_hash` as the
list showed it. Required on every approve body — an agent re-proposal
rewrites a pending row in place, so the hash is what ties the installed
content to the content that was reviewed.

content_hash.description: `content_hash` of the suggestion as the reviewer saw it.
`content_hash` of the suggestion as the reviewer saw it.

profile_id.description:
The tool profile the promoted rule lands in. Omit (or `null`) to use
the tenant default profile.

AssignedProfile.description:
A workspace's **explicit** profile choice for one `kind`. Present only when
the workspace has a row for that kind (an absent kind inherits the tenant
default). `profile_id`/`name` are `None` when the kind is explicitly **off**
(`mode = "off"`); a specific profile carries both (`mode = "profile"`). The
UI maps `{off}` / `{profile,id}` / absent → its three-state picker.

AttachedDestinationList.description: An attachment as shown, with the list's name.

top_rule_id.description:
Most-frequent rule id across the blocked-tool events in window. Empty
`None` when no blocks. Used by the UI as a one-line subtitle.

approaching.description: Scopes between 80% and 100% of cap (approaching the ceiling).

breached.description:
Scopes (organisation ceiling, workspace pool, member limit, or per-key cap) at or over
their daily/monthly budget cap in the current window.

worst_ratio.description:
Worst offender's spend as a fraction of its cap (≥0). `None` when no cap
is configured or no spend recorded. Surfaces as the tile's subtitle.

worst_scope_kind.description:
Worst offender's scope (`"tenant"` | `"workspace"` | `"user"` (a
member) | `"key"`) for the deep-link.

worst_workspace_id.description:
The workspace the worst offender belongs to — where a member's limit is
set (its Limits tab). `None` for the organisation ceiling.

top_error_category.description:
Most-frequent `gateway_audit.error_category` value in the window
(e.g. `"auth"`, `"upstream"`, `"timeout"`, `"rate_limit"`). `None`
when there are no errors. Surfaces as the tile's subtitle.

expired.description: Rows whose `expires_at` is already in the past (not yet revoked).

lt_24h.description: Rows whose `expires_at` falls within the next 24 hours.

lt_7d.description:
Rows whose `expires_at` falls within the configured expiry window
(default 7 days). Inclusive of `lt_24h` and `expired`.

blocked.description:
Subset of `total` whose guardrail badge carries `action: "block"` — the
enforce-mode stripped subset (observe-mode flags are excluded). Only the
substitution loop strips, so this is an LLM-side count.

total.description:
Rows in the window whose badges carry a `guardrail` finding — the inline
injection guardrail flagged untrusted web content. Spans both surfaces:
`llm_audit` (content folded back into a model on the substitution loop)
and `web_audit` (the direct `/mcp/web` observe scan). Counts both observe
(flag) and enforce (block) verdicts.

window_days.description: Echoed window so the UI can label "in last Nd" without re-computing.

AttentionUpstreams.description:
Whether the tenant's LLM upstream servers can serve traffic now, and whether
capacity ran out in the window.

degraded.description: Servers with some — not all — of their enabled endpoints out of rotation.

down.description: Servers with every enabled endpoint out of rotation.

down_server_id.description: The server that is down, when exactly one is, so the tile can open it.

engines_silent.description:
Endpoints whose engine gauges the gateway reads and which have gone
quiet — their queue bound is not being applied.

refused.description:
Refusals the dispatch gate gave for want of capacity in the window —
including each one a request then moved on from to a fallback.

oneOf.description:
Request or response content was rewritten by a transform.
Emitted once when at least one `injection_block` exists.

Policy produced a rewrite that was NOT applied on the wire: the caller
(an inline-AI enforcement point analyzing out-of-band) declared itself
verdict-only, or the block was a thinking block the provider signed and
refuses back altered. The original content went forward unmodified. The
distinct code keeps the audit truthful — `modified` means the wire
changed; this means it *would have*.
Context-window compression engaged.
Upstream returned malformed JSON; gateway repaired it.

Tool policy blocked one or more tool calls.
`phase=request` for name-match blocks, `phase=response` for argument-match blocks.

Tool block fail-closed because the buffered event count exceeded the analysis window.
Operator should investigate.

A streaming text/thinking block was dropped (fail-closed) because it
exceeded the buffered-event cap during script analysis.

Rhai script chain failed in fail-closed mode.
Tooltip lists the offending program names.

Cross-protocol translation happened. `not_carried` names each part of
the request the target protocol or model has no channel for — a hosted
tool, a provider-specific tool choice, a reasoning request to a model
that does not reason — so a translation that dropped something says what.

The request needed a capability the alias's chosen upstream does not
declare, so the gateway forwarded it to the next target in the chain
that does. `from` is the displaced model and `reason` the capability
that displaced it; the row's `model_used` records the model that
actually served the request. Without this the substitution would be
invisible — the alias's priority / load-balancing order silently did
not decide this request.
Request hit the catch-all proxy (unmatched route).
Tool names were sanitized before forwarding upstream. Only emitted when `count > 0`.

Tool names emitted by the *upstream model* in a response (streaming
or non-streaming) were sanitized before being delivered to the
client. Parallel to [`Self::SanitizedToolNames`] but on the response
path. Only emitted when `count > 0`. Operators inspecting the audit
detail can see the original→sanitized mapping in
`transform_diff.injection_blocks` entries with
`transform: "response_sanitize_tool_names"`.

One expert's alert of one level. Never written by the current agent,
which raises its alerts on the session (`SessionAlert`).

MCP request returned a JSON-RPC error. `code` is the JSON-RPC error
code (`-32xxx`) — `-32429` rate limited, `-32500` upstream credential
unavailable, `-32506` blocked by policy, etc. Tooltip resolves the
code to a human-readable label in the UI registry.

MCP upstream is using the legacy `text/event-stream` GET transport
instead of Streamable HTTP. Operator-visible signal that the upstream
hasn't migrated to spec 2025-03-26+.

MCP `sampling/createMessage` was intercepted by the gateway and
served via a synthetic LLM call instead of being forwarded to the
connected agent. Badged on the `mcp_audit` row. The linked
`llm_audit` row carries the matching [`AuditBadge::LlmSyntheticSampling`].

LLM call was synthesized by the gateway in response to an MCP
`sampling/createMessage` interception (not initiated by an
upstream client). Badged on the `llm_audit` row.

Tool call with canonical id `web_search` or `web_fetch` was blocked
by tool policy. Lands on the `mcp_audit` row alongside the generic
`ToolBlocked` chip so the UI can show a per-domain icon without
re-parsing the tool name. Fires on the canonical `tool_id`, not the
wire name — so it covers `/mcp/web` direct calls (canonical id
resolved via the `builtin-web` field profile) and any future MCP
upstream that exposes a tool resolving to the same canonical id.

At least one URL in the call was denied by the URL-filter chain
(allow / deny domains, future external HTTP filters). For search,
counts hits removed; for fetch, the target URL itself was denied.

Search returned hits but the URL-filter chain dropped every one of
them — the model received an empty result.
Upstream provider returned 429 (or equivalent quota exceeded).

Fetched content was stripped from `audit_media_blobs` storage
because it exceeded `media_blob_max_size_mb` or because
`media_blob_storage_enabled = false`.

The gateway could not deliver this audit record whole — it was too
large (`oversized`) or nested too deep (`too_deep`) for the edge's
sync to admin-api — so its structured payload fields (params, results,
diffs) were left out, and long text possibly replaced by a size note;
its identity, status and counters were recorded.

A body this record names — a conversation message, a tool set, the
system prompt or a media blob — is not held by admin-api: the gateway
could not deliver it, or the database refused to store it. The record
is stored and its turn renders without that body.

Fetch refused because the target host resolved to an internal /
loopback / link-local / IMDS address.
Fetch refused because the URL scheme was not http/https.

A server-side server-tool the client requested (Anthropic
`web_search_20250305`, OpenAI Responses `web_search_preview`, Gemini
`google_search`) was emulated by the gateway via the substitution
loop. Badged on the orchestrating `llm_audit` row; the executor's
`web_audit` rows carry `surface='substitution'` and
`parent_request_id` linking back. Wiring lands in a follow-up PR.

A client-side function-tool a known client declared (Claude Code
`WebFetch`/`WebSearch`, opencode `webfetch`/`websearch`) was
intercepted and routed through `WebService` instead of being
echoed to the client. Badged on the orchestrating `llm_audit` row.
The substituted `tool_use` is invisible to the client. Wiring lands
in a follow-up PR.

The substitution loop hit `web.substitution_max_iterations`
without the upstream emitting a final non-tool-use response. The
last upstream response was forwarded to the client as-is.

One of the executor calls inside the substitution loop failed; the
loop surfaced the error to the upstream as a tool-execution error
and continued.

Substitution agent loop ran for a round whose upstream stream
terminated without a `Done` event (idle timeout / decode error /
half-close) while pending intercepted calls were queued. The loop
forwarded the round's last bytes as-is and DROPPED the pending
intercepts (no executor ran). Appends the dropped tool names so
operators can attribute the loss.

One upstream turn emitted both real and intercepted tool_use
blocks. The buffered-discard path forwarded the real blocks as-is
and DROPPED the intercepted ones (no executor ran). Decision #4
requires splicing both — full implementation pending PR-3. The
badge surfaces the partial behaviour for now.

Re-issuing the upstream call after a substitution round failed
(HTTP error, transport error, retry exhaustion). The agent loop
stopped and yielded an empty response to the client (with a
synthetic error marker).

Re-serializing the cumulative `DomainRequest` for the next round
failed (translation / encoding error). Same client effect as
`WebSubstitutionForwardFailed`.

A request matched a substitution rule but the agent loop is
streaming-only — the upstream `tool_use` echo flowed back to the
client unchanged. Visible-mode + non-streaming substitution land
in a follow-up release.

Cumulative `DomainRequest` body re-sent upstream across substitution
rounds exceeded `web.substitution_history_max_bytes`. The
agent loop dropped the oldest splice (assistant tool_use + contiguous
tool_result messages) one or more times and re-translated; if the
body is still over cap after the bounded truncation pass, the loop
surfaces this badge and aborts via the serialize-failed path. Each
truncation also emits an `injection_block` with `field="history"`
and `action="truncate_oldest"`.

The substitution agent loop was cancelled mid-flight — typically
the client SSE response was dropped before the loop reached its
terminal round. The cancellation token threaded through
`WebContext` short-circuits the in-flight executor calls and
upstream re-issue so the gateway stops wasting upstream egress on a
conversation the client has abandoned. Pending intercepted calls
surface as `injection_blocks[]` with `reason="cancelled"`.

One or more parked mixed-pending entries from a prior request in the
same session were spliced into the inbound conversation as
synthesised `assistant tool_use → user tool_result` pairs before the
request was forwarded upstream. Pairs with the
`WebSubstitutionMixedPending` badge on the *prior* request
(which dispatched and parked the result); this badge surfaces on
the *next* request, completing the audit trail for the
cross-request strict-Decision-#4 splice. `count` is the number of
parked entries actually folded in.

Inbound mixed-pending splice was attempted but failed mid-flight —
either the `DomainRequest` → wire translation errored, or the
re-parse of the translated bytes errored. The cache entries had
already been drained, so `count` parked dispatched results were
dropped without reaching the model. The "Nothing is silently
discarded" invariant: every dropped parked entry shows up on this
row's `injection_blocks[]` with `transform="mixed_pending_splice"`
and `action="drop_on_translation_failure"` so operators can see
what was lost.

The inline injection guardrail scanned untrusted fetched/searched
content and flagged at least one item. `action=flag` in observe mode
(content untouched, the would-have-blocked signal); `action=block` in
enforce (content stripped to a placeholder). `categories` lists the
distinct finding categories; `max_confidence` is the highest positive
score across the flagged items. Aggregated on the orchestrating
`llm_audit` row (substitution path) or stamped on the `web_audit` row
(direct `/mcp/web`).

The guardrail detector errored (timeout / transport / parse) and the
tenant's `fail_mode` decided the request's fate. Surfaced so a fetch
that went unscored is never silently invisible.

The answer came from the gateway's response cache — no upstream call was
made. `avoided_cost` prices the cached response's stored token usage
at the alias's current rates: what this request would have cost. The row
itself is charged `$0`. `age_seconds` is how long the entry had been
resident when it was served; `similarity` is present only for a
semantic-mode hit.

A cache preset in `observe` mode matched an entry that *would* have been
served. The request still went upstream and was billed normally — this
records the would-be hit so an admin can measure before enforcing.

A cache-enabled alias produced a response that was NOT stored, and why
(`tool_calls`, `error_status`, `zero_completion`, `entry_too_large`,
`cache_full`, `client_bypass`). Only ever appears on an alias with
caching enabled, so a cache that never fills is diagnosable instead of
silently inert.

A cache preset asked for semantic matching, and the gateway could not do
it for this request (`no_embedding_alias`, `embedding_alias_unresolved`,
`embedding_failed`, `embedding_timeout`). The request was served
normally and exact matching still applied — but an alias that quietly
stops matching semantically looks identical to one nobody is repeating
prompts on, so the reason is recorded instead of inferred.

The request waited for upstream capacity before it was dispatched, and
for how long. It says the model was saturated and this caller's turn came
after others — the one thing that explains a slow request the upstream
itself served quickly.

The request was served by a replica other than the one it was routed to,
because that one had no room at the moment it asked.

The row already names the replica that answered; what this adds is that
the request MOVED, which nothing else records. It is the readable form
of a fleet running hot on one replica — and, for a session pinned to a
replica for its prompt cache, the reason a turn was slower than the ones
around it.

No price is known for the model this request used, so its recorded cost is
a floor of zero rather than a real figure.

This is NOT the same as a free model, and the distinction is the point: a
zero cost skips budget accrual entirely, so an enforcing budget over an
unpriced model never fires. Without the badge that failure is invisible —
the cap looks configured and simply does nothing. Resolve it by pricing the
model on its upstream, or by linking it to a catalog entry.

The request was conformed to an upstream whose API reads the target
protocol differently (`dialect`: `mistral`, `openai_compatible`, or
`anthropic` for what Anthropic verifies). `adapted` names each
rewrite that kept the meaning (a renamed parameter, a narrowed tool
choice), `not_carried` each part the upstream has no channel for, which
was removed. Recorded with or without a protocol translation: a request
forwarded in its own protocol is conformed too, and the row renders the
request as the client sent it.

The agent raised an alert on this LLM audit row's session: its most
severe level and every expert that raised one. Derived by the audit list
at read time from the session's alert columns — never stored on the row
(audit rows are never rewritten).

AuditBadge.description:
A typed audit badge. Wire format is `{ "code": "<snake_case>", ...payload }`.

One variant per user-facing chip on the audit log.

AuditKind.description:
Discriminator for the `/audit` endpoint's row families. Defaults to
[`AuditKind::Llm`] so callers that haven't migrated keep the existing
shape; native MCP clients pass `kind=mcp`; `kind=web` returns
rows from the `web_audit` partition (one per dispatched call,
including substitution-loop children); `kind=all` runs every query
server-side and merges by `timestamp DESC`.

badges.description:
Typed audit badges (`streamscope_core::audit::AuditBadge`, codes
append-only): the LLM row's own, plus a `session_alert` read from its session's
current alert (the agent writes the alert on the session, never on the
audit row).

billed_units.description:
Per-unit decomposition of `cost`: what was charged for each thing the
request consumed. Counts are what was CHARGED — a provider's reported
count less anything that partitions out of it, each of which carries its
own line — so the lines sum to `cost` less `embedding_cost`.

catchall_path.description:
Path/method of the catch-all hit (only populated when the request fell
to the catch-all handler).

chat_media_summary.description:
Extracted media references for chat requests. Typed shape mirrors
`streamscope_core::audit::ChatMediaSummaryEntry`.

client_ip.description:
Forwarded end-client identity, present only for Inline AI traffic where a
trusted inline key relayed it (`X-Client-IP` / `X-Authenticated-User` /
`X-Authenticated-Groups`). Absent/empty for direct clients.

conversation_session_id.description:
Content-derived conversation id from `conversation_turns.session_id`.
`None` when no `conversation_turns` row exists for this request
(MCP/web audit rows, LLM rows captured before content
logging was on). Use this — not `session_id` — for any UI link to
`/sessions/{id}`.

cost.description:
The row's total, in `cost_currency` — the tenant's accounting currency
as it was when the row was written, not as it is now. Stamped per row so
changing the setting cannot restate spend that was already reported.

embedding_cost.description:
Portion of `cost` spent on the response cache's own embedding call,
with the tokens it consumed. Non-zero only on a Semantic-cached alias.
Present so the row's total still decomposes: without it `cost`
exceeds the completion's own cost with nothing to explain the gap.

endpoint_url.description:
The replica endpoint of the server that answered, as its URL was when
it did. Null on a row with no upstream call, or from a release before
endpoints.

latency_total_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the moment the gateway started forwarding — after its
own checks and transforms — to the end of the answer: any hold for
capacity (`queue_wait_ms`) and any earlier attempt it moved on from
included.

latency_ttft_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the moment the gateway started forwarding — after its
own checks and transforms — to the first token: any hold for capacity
(`queue_wait_ms`) and any earlier attempt it moved on from included.

limit_bucket.description:
On a limit refusal: which limit refused it — `organisation`,
`workspace`, `member` or `key`. The UI explains a refusal from this.

oneOf.description:
Canonical media RPC shape — source of truth for embeddings / audio /
images / video endpoint turns. `None` for chat/text routes.

pipeline_path.description:
Internal pipeline-path tag (`fastpath` | `buffered`). Analytics-only,
not user-facing.

qos_class_id.description:
The QoS class the request ran as. The name is resolved by the reader
against the tenant's class list — an audit row must not hold a class
back from being renamed or deleted.

queue_wait_ms.description:
Milliseconds the request waited for upstream capacity before it was
dispatched. Part of `latency_ttft_ms` and `latency_total_ms`: the time
the upstream that answered took is the latency less this and less any
earlier attempt it moved on from.

session_id.description:
Raw client-facing session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — the
hashed X-Session-Id value used for cross-stream correlation in the
session detection layer. This is NOT the conversation id used by
the session-detail UI: that's the separate content-derived
`conversation_session_id` below, populated only when there's an
LLM turn linked via `conversation_turns.session_id`. UI callers
building "View Session" links MUST use `conversation_session_id`,
not this field — the two diverge for any session that didn't go
through the LLM pipeline (MCP-only, web-only, etc).

source_cost.description:
What the provider charges, in the currency it quotes, and the multiplier
that took one to the other. Equal to `cost` with an `fx_rate` of 1 when
the model is priced in the accounting currency.

oneOf.description:
Transform diff captured on `conversation_turns` — mirrors the shape in

transforms applied with `capture_diffs` enabled. `None` otherwise (e.g.,
media requests, non-text requests, or transforms without diff capture).

allOf.description:

joined virtual-server slug + user email + protocol_version so the audit
UI can render rows without an extra fan-out fetch. Operators correlate
across calls in the same JSON-RPC session by pasting `mcp_session_id`
into the audit list `search` box (substring match).

app_id.description:
Three-tier app id resolved by `extract_attribution` from `X-App-Id` /
`Referer` / `User-Agent` (mirrors LLM rows). `None` when no pattern
matched. Stored on `gateway_audit.app_id`.

badges.description:
Typed audit badges — same `AuditBadge` enum as LLM rows. Codes are
append-only; UI consumer is the shared `BADGE_REGISTRY`. DB column
is `NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` so this is always present.

mcp_session_id.description:
Raw `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the call. Distinct from
`session_id` above (which is hashed).

params.description:
JSON-RPC `params` payload as the agent sent it (for `tools/call`
this is the `{name, arguments}` envelope; for `resources/read` the
`{uri}`; for `prompts/get` the `{name, arguments}`). Mirrors the
LLM trace's `messages` field — surfaced so the audit drawer + the
session-view MCP bubble can render the actual request body
without an extra fetch.

protocol_version.description:
MCP protocol version negotiated at `initialize` and pinned for the
remainder of the session. `None` for the rare row that lands before
`initialize` completes (`mcp_sessions.protocol_version` defaults to
`"unknown"`).

result.description:
JSON-RPC `result` payload returned by the upstream (success path
only — error responses populate `error_code` / `error_message`).

session_id.description:
Hashed session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — same shape the
LLM `AuditLogEntry` carries. Cross-protocol correlation pivots on
this when an MCP `sampling/createMessage` was intercepted by the
gateway and answered through the LLM pipeline (the synthetic
`llm_audit` row shares this id).

oneOf.description:
Typed diff payload stamped by the MCP policy engine + multiplex pump.
Each field corresponds to a key the proxy may stamp on a given row.
Empty struct (`{}`) when nothing fired.

allOf.description:
Web audit row exposed at `/audit?kind=web`. One row per
dispatched call (both direct `/mcp/web` traffic with `surface='mcp'` and
substitution-loop children with `surface='substitution'`). `parent_request_id`
links substitution rows back to the orchestrating LLM `gateway_audit`
row; the dedicated `GET /api/v1/admin/audit/{request_id}/web`
endpoint queries by it.

fetch_content_summary.description: For fetch operations: blob hashes/MIMEs into audit_media_blobs.

filter_chain.description: Ordered filter ids that ran in the chain.

parent_request_id.description:
Orchestrating LLM `request_id` when `surface == "substitution"`;
`None` for direct MCP traffic.

oneOf.description:
Provider's raw response, typed as the cap-aware
[`streamscope_core::web::audit::WebProviderResponse`]
enum. UI branches on the `Stripped` variant for the oversized
callout.

response_summary.description: Response shape returned to the caller.

result_count.description: search → hits returned to caller (post-filter); fetch → 1 on success.

oneOf.description: Per-rule diff payload (same shape the LLM/MCP rows carry).

url_results.description: Per-URL filter verdicts on every search hit / fetch target.

allOf.description:
A2A-side audit row exposed at `/audit?kind=a2a`. Per-call shape with the
joined agent slug/name + user email so the audit UI renders rows without
a fan-out fetch. Operators correlate calls in the same A2A conversation
by the raw `a2a_context_id` (and one unit of remote work by `a2a_task_id`).

a2a_context_id.description: Raw wire `contextId` — the per-protocol conversation correlator.

badges.description: Typed audit badges — same `AuditBadge` enum as LLM/MCP rows.

error_category.description:
Gateway-level error class shared with the LLM/MCP rows (`upstream`,
`rpc_error`, `cancelled`, …) — what the error dashboards aggregate on.

error_detail.description:
Why the call failed, in prose. On a streamed call this is where a
mid-stream break, a malformed event, or the byte cap is recorded.

params.description:
JSON-RPC `params` payload as the client sent it (polymorphic per
method — `SendMessage` carries the message envelope, task ops the id).

result.description:
JSON-RPC `result` payload from the agent (Task | Message | card —
polymorphic per method). NULL on error replies.

session_id.description:
Hashed session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — cross-protocol
correlation with LLM/MCP rows sharing the client's `X-Session-Id`.

stream_events.description:
Streaming calls: accumulated `StreamResponse` envelopes. NULL for
non-streaming methods.

oneOf.description: What the policy engine and the inline guardrail did to this call.

AuditLogRow.description:
Row family discriminated by `kind`. UI consumers branch on `row.kind`
rather than sniffing fields. All variants are boxed because
`AuditLogEntry` is wide (~1.5 KB) and the size mismatch with the MCP /
web shapes would otherwise blow up the heap allocation per row.

admin_group.description: IdP group whose members get console role `Admin` (OIDC mode).

mcp_oauth_cimd_enabled.description:
Whether this tenant accepts CIMD (Client ID Metadata Document) clients —
an OAuth client that publishes its metadata at an HTTPS URL and presents
that URL as its `client_id`, with no registration step.

Defaults to `true`. Turning it off makes the tenant's RFC 8414 document
advertise `client_id_metadata_document_supported: false`, refuses a
URL-shaped `client_id` at `/authorize`, and refuses a
`client_id_metadata_url` at `/register` — closing the one path on which
an unauthenticated caller can name a URL this deployment will fetch.

mcp_oauth_delegate_to_oidc.description:
When true, the spec-OAuth `/authorize` endpoint delegates
user authentication to the tenant's OIDC IdP (reuses
`oidc_issuer_url` / `oidc_client_id` / `encrypted_oidc_client_secret`
for the consent step) instead of relying on a portal session JWT.
The proxy still mints the access token; the IdP only proves identity.
Defaults to `false`. The admin UI exposes a toggle on the auth-config
page when `auth_mode = oidc`.

oidc_allow_unverified_email.description:
Accept an address the provider made no verification statement about.
Never overrides an explicit `email_verified: false`. Only a claim other
than `email` is always unstated — the provider's `email_verified`
describes `email` alone. Default `false`.

oidc_client_secret_masked.description:
A fixed `****` when a secret is stored, `None` when none is — a
presence flag, never any part of the value.

oidc_email_claim.description:
The ID-token claim the account is keyed on — it must hold exactly one
address. Default `email`; `upn` for a directory without mailboxes.

oidc_groups_claim.description:
The ID-token claim whose values are matched against `admin_group` /
`readonly_group`. A single string or a list, whichever the provider
sends. Default `groups`; AD FS names it `group`.

oidc_response_mode.description:
How the provider returns the authorization code: `query` (default) or
`form_post`. AD FS puts the claims its rules issue into the ID token only
for a `form_post` authorization.

readonly_group.description:
IdP group whose members get console role `ReadOnly` (OIDC mode).
`admin_group` wins if a user is in both.

api_origin.description:
Streamscope extension (CLI surface only): the public origin of the
canonical admin-API, where the token/portal endpoints live. Possibly
distinct from the browser-facing origin serving
`authorization_endpoint` — admin-UI and admin-API are separate vhosts
on every production deploy shape, and the discovery document itself
may be fetched through the UI origin's GET-only passthrough. The
`ssai` CLI directs every API call here after discovery.

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description:
RFC 9207 §3. **Load-bearing when true**: the parameter defaults to
`false` when the field is absent, and a conformant client keys its
validation on this flag — so a server that emits `iss` without
advertising it has built a protection nobody checks.

client_id_metadata_document_supported.description:
Whether the authorization server accepts URL-formatted `client_id`
values that resolve to a JSON metadata document
([draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00]). Per MCP 2025-11-25
§ Authorization, clients SHOULD prefer CIMD over Dynamic Client
Registration when this flag is `true` — so it must never be advertised
unless the authorization endpoint really does accept a URL, or a
conforming client picks the path that fails.

device_authorization_endpoint.description:
RFC 8628 device-authorization endpoint. Present only on surfaces that
support the device grant (the CLI provisioning surface — headless
logins); the MCP surface omits it.

issuer.description:
Issuer identifier — the URL that prefixes our /authorize and /token
endpoints, and the exact string our authorization responses echo back as
the RFC 9207 `iss` parameter. Clients compare the two byte for byte.

jwks_uri.description:
RFC 8414 `jwks_uri` — where this authorization server publishes the
public keys that verify the tokens it issues.

Present only on surfaces whose tokens are asymmetrically signed, which
today is the MCP surface alone. Advertising it elsewhere would promise a
verification path that does not exist: the CLI surface's access tokens
are HS256 and are only ever presented back to us.

registration_endpoint.description:
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration endpoint. Optional in the spec but
always present here so MCP clients that prefer DCR over manual
registration can discover it without out-of-band setup.

resource_parameter_supported.description:
Whether we support the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter on /authorize and
/token. Always `true`.

revocation_endpoint.description:
RFC 7009 token-revocation endpoint. Both first-party surfaces publish
one; the field stays optional because the type describes the wire
format, not our deployment.

oneOf.description: The request validated. Render the "X wants to access Y" copy.

The request is invalid, but the client and its redirect URI are
registered — so the error belongs at that URI, not on our page.

redirect_to.description:
The fully-built error redirect, so the encoding and the byte-exact
RFC 9207 `iss` stay owned by the server that has to match its own
metadata.

AuthorizePreviewResponse.description:
Payload returned by `POST /authorize/preview`.

Two dispositions, because RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 gives an invalid authorization
request two different destinations: the consent page renders `ok`, and
hands `redirect` straight back to the client. The consent page cannot make
that call itself — only the server knows whether the redirect URI was
vouched for by a registration — so the decision is carried, not inferred.

AuthorizeRequest.description: Query (or body) shape used by `preview` and `approve`.

resource.description:
RFC 8707 `resource` parameter — the canonical URI of the virtual server
the client wants to access. We bind the issued JWT's `aud` to this.

AutoSyncStatus.description:
The last autosync run's outcome as the API reports it: `ok` with the
counts on success, `ok: false` with `reason` and `at` on failure. Read from
the stored `upstream_servers.last_auto_sync_status`; every field but `ok` is
optional because each outcome writes a different subset.

at.description: When the failure was recorded (database clock).

BackupConfig.description: The backup settings, the rclone config's secrets left out.

configured.description: Settings were saved; otherwise the rest are the defaults.

destination.description: Where backups go: an rclone remote and a path in it.

locked.description:
The operator locked the settings over SSH: a save, or a test of settings
other than the saved ones, is refused (403 `appliance_operator_only`);
they are still read, tested as saved and run. A daemon that does not
lock them omits it: false.

profile.description: The profile a scheduled backup takes.

oneOf.description: Who saved it; absent when none is saved.

rclone_config_set.description: An rclone config is saved. It is never returned.

recipients.description: The age public keys a backup is encrypted to.

retention_days.description: A backup older than this is deleted after a backup; 0 keeps every one.

schedule.description: The schedule, as a systemd calendar event.

BackupConfigUpdate.description:
Backup settings to save, or to test, over the saved rclone config. That
config (the remotes and their credentials) is the operator's, set over SSH:
rclone runs programs its options name, as root on the host, so the daemon
refuses one from the console. A field this body does not name, an
`rclone_config` included, is refused (422), never dropped: a credential
change must not answer as saved.

destination.description: `remote:path`, the remote one the operator's rclone config defines.

recipients.description: age public keys to encrypt to; any one's private key decrypts a backup.

error.description: Why it failed; absent when it succeeded.

prune_error.description: Why pruning older backups failed, after a backup that succeeded.

profile.description: The profile to take; absent takes the settings' profile.

oneOf.description: The last backup, whether it succeeded or not.

next.description: The schedule's next run, as systemd prints it.

from_discovery.description:
True when these values were read from the provider's own discovery (the
sync-review apply), false when an operator typed them (the default).

It decides whether the inheritable fields are **pinned**: a value the
operator supplied is theirs and must survive every later refresh, while a
discovered one must keep tracking the provider. Both meanings arrive on
this one endpoint, and they are indistinguishable from the payload alone.
The default is the safe direction — an unmarked caller pins, which
preserves a value rather than silently overwriting it later.

plane.description: Which plane the user is signing in to: `admin` or `portal`.

prompt.description:
Standard OIDC `prompt`. Only `login` and `select_account` are honoured;
anything else is ignored, which yields the default silent SSO.

redirect_uri.description:
The URL the provider will redirect back to. Must be one the provider has
registered for this client; it is pinned into the flow so the token
exchange presents exactly the value the authorization request carried.

return_to.description:
Where to land after a successful portal login. Honoured only when it is
a same-origin path under `/portal/`.

tenant_slug.description: Tenant whose identity provider should authenticate this login.

flow_token.description:
Opaque. Hand it back to `/callback` unchanged; it cannot be read or
altered outside this process.

plane.description:
The plane this login will authenticate, after a `return_to` has been
taken into account. Returned so the caller can route a failure to the
right login page; the authoritative copy is sealed inside `flow_token`.

BilledUnit.description:
One line of a priced request: how much of a unit was charged, and for how
much.

cost.description: What that count cost, in the enclosing [`Cost`]'s currency.

count.description:
Units charged — the count reported by the provider **less** anything
that partitions out of it, since those are charged on their own line.

BlobContent.description: A media blob, keyed by `(content_hash, blob_type)` within the tenant.

data_base64.description: The bytes, standard base64 (decoded by the database on insert).

BlobType.description:
Discriminator for a row in `audit_media_blobs` and its `blob_ref` references.

Wire form is the `snake_case` of the variant — the strings stored in the DB
`blob_type` column, embedded in `blob_ref` JSON, and accepted by the
`?blob_type=` query param of the media-serving endpoint.

BlockKind.description: Block kind for `BlockOverflow` (response stream block dropped fail-closed).

BlockedToolInfo.description: Info about a tool blocked by policy.

arguments.description:
Arguments the model attempted. Only populated for response-phase blocks
(the LLM emitted a real call); request-phase blocks strip the tool
before the LLM runs, so there is nothing to capture.

rule_id.description: Stable identifier (e.g. `ASI02-06`) of the rule that blocked the tool.

tool_use_id.description:
Id of the specific tool_use call that was blocked. Populated for
response-phase blocks (the model emits an id on every tool_call);
`None` for request-phase blocks (no call existed to have an id).
Used by the admin event builder to attach the block banner to the
exact `ConversationEvent::ToolCall` the model tried to make, so
same-tool-twice turns attribute the banner correctly.

BreakdownBy.description:
The dimension a usage breakdown groups by. `server_model` and
`workspace_model` group by model within each server / workspace (the
server / workspace is the entry's `parent_key`).

server_id.description:
The upstream server's id when `by=server` (the entry) or
`by=server_model` (its parent), so a row can open that server's
dashboard, which is addressed by id.

oneOf.description:
What this entry spent, decomposed per pricing unit.

`null` when the entry's rows straddle a change of the tenant's
accounting currency: they are then stated in different denominations,
and a single figure would be in neither. Render that as unavailable —
the window's own components are on the overview.

user_email.description:
User email when `by=user` and the user has one on file. Lets the UI
build a `?user_email=…` deep-link that the audit / sessions backends
match exactly, instead of relying on the rendered display-name `key`.

user_id.description:
User UUID when `by=user`. Fallback identifier the UI uses when
`user_email` is absent — pairs with `AuditQuery::user_id` /
`SessionListQuery::user_id` so deep-links still resolve for users
without an email on file.

BudgetWindow.description:
Which budget window a warning or a figure is about: the UTC day, or the
fixed 30-day period.

ids.description: If provided, only update these model IDs (overrides server_id).

server_id.description: Scope to a single server. If omitted, applies to ALL servers.

BundleKey.description:
The gateway key the bundle embeds (sans plaintext — that rides once in
`minted_secrets` when freshly minted).

CacheAliasSavings.description: One alias's money figures over the window, all in `currency`.

embedding_cost.description: The alias's embedding spend, whatever its mode.

net_saved.description:
`gross_avoided` less the embedding spend of an enforcing alias; an
`observe` alias's embeddings are measurement and not charged here.

alias.description: The alias the client asked for.

mode.description:
Cache mode in force: `exact`, `semantic`, or `observe`. An alias whose
preset changed mid-window appears once per mode it ran under.

oneOf.description:
`null` when this alias's window straddles a change of the accounting
currency.

semantic_skips.description:
Why semantic matching could not run, commonest first. Always empty on an
`exact`-mode row, which never attempts it — reasons are attributed to the
mode that was in force, so an alias that ran both modes in the window
carries each reason on the row that produced it.

store_skips.description: Why this alias's responses were not stored, commonest first.

CacheAnalyticsResponse.description:
What the response cache did, and what it was worth, over the window.

Every figure covers only requests that went through an alias with a cache
preset bound — an uncached gateway reports zeroes throughout.

aliases.description:
Per-alias breakdown, ranked by net savings under the shared spend rule
(see `TopUserEntry`): by the net saved in today's accounting currency,
richest first, then aliases with nothing in it.

bypassed.description:
Requests where the client sent `Cache-Control: no-cache`/`no-store`.
Kept out of `lookups` so a client opting out cannot depress the hit rate.

hit_rate.description:
`hits / lookups`. Zero for an `observe`-only tenant by construction:
observe never serves.

hits.description: Requests answered from the cache, with no upstream call.

lookups.description: Requests the cache was consulted for. Excludes `bypassed`.

observe_hits.description:
Requests that matched under `observe` and were still sent upstream.
These saved nothing — they are the tuning signal for whether to enforce.

oneOf.description:
What the cache saved and cost, in one currency. `null` when the window
straddles a change of the tenant's accounting currency: its figures are
then in more than one denomination and no single one states them.

semantic_skips.description:
Why semantic matching could not run, tenant-wide, commonest first. A
semantic alias silently degraded to exact (`embedding_timeout`,
`embedding_failed`) is indistinguishable from one nobody repeats
prompts on unless this is reported.

store_skips.description:
Why responses were not stored, tenant-wide, commonest first. A cache
with a low hit rate and a full `tool_calls` bucket is not underused —
it is being asked to cache something it never can.

CacheControl.description:
Anthropic's cache breakpoint as the client sent it: `{"type": "ephemeral",
"ttl"?: "5m" | "1h"}`.

route_count.description: How many aliases reference this preset. Drives the delete-impact warning.

threshold.description: Cosine-similarity floor for a semantic hit. Ignored in the other modes.

CacheSavings.description: The response cache's money figures over the window, all in `currency`.

embedding_cost.description:
Embedding spend on enforcing (`exact`/`semantic`) aliases. Charged
against savings — it is the cost of running the cache.

gross_avoided.description: What the upstream calls the hits replaced would have cost.

net_saved.description:
`gross_avoided - embedding_cost`. Can be negative — a semantic
alias nobody repeats prompts on pays for embeddings and saves nothing.

tuning_cost.description:
Embedding spend on `observe` aliases. Reported separately and NOT
charged against savings: observe is a measurement run, so folding its
cost in would make a tenant evaluating the cache read as losing money.

would_avoid.description: What enforcing would additionally have saved, from the observe matches.

CacheSettings.description:
Tenant-wide response-cache settings — typed projection of the
`system_settings.cache` key. Lives on `TenantConfig.cache`.

Per-alias policy is *not* here: mode, TTL, threshold and sharing scope live
on the named cache preset a route references. What belongs here is what the
tenant decides once, across every alias.

embedding_alias.description:
Alias the gateway calls to turn a prompt into a vector, for `semantic`
mode. It is an ordinary embeddings alias from the tenant's own catalog,
so no separate credential exists — the tenant's routing resolves it like
any other model.

Unset means semantic matching is unavailable: a `semantic` preset still
serves exact hits, and each request says so on its audit row rather than
quietly behaving as `exact`.

embedding_timeout_ms.description:
Hard ceiling on the embedding round-trip. Exceeding it abandons the
semantic lookup and takes the miss — a cache is an optimization, so it
must never become the slowest part of a request.

enabled.description:
Tenant-wide master switch. `false` makes every alias behave as uncached
regardless of the preset it references — the one-flip incident lever, so
an admin never has to edit N presets to stop serving cached answers.

max_entry_kb.description:
Largest single response the tenant will cache, in KB. A response over
this is served normally and left uncached, with an audit marker — big
answers would evict many small ones for one rare reuse.

CacheSkipStat.description: One reason a cache step did not run, and how often.

reason.description:
Machine-readable reason, straight off the audit badge — e.g.
`tool_calls`, `entry_too_large`, `cache_full`, `client_bypass`,
`embedding_timeout`, `no_embedding_alias`.

id_token.description: The provider's ID token, for use as `id_token_hint` at logout.

redirect_to.description: Where to send the browser now.

token.description: The session JWT for the resolved plane.

models_unlinked.description:
Upstream models whose explicit link named a removed entry, unlinked so
they auto-match again.

rates.description:
Price per billing unit, plus the currency those prices are quoted in.
Rates are in each unit's natural scale — per million for token units, per
single unit otherwise.

An empty map means no price is on file: the request is billed at a floor
of zero **and** badged, which stays distinct from a rate of `0`, meaning
the model is genuinely free. A catalog entry that carries only
capabilities (context window, modality support) legitimately has one.

CatalogInput.description:
Input for create: `provider` and `model` are required; everything else is
optional. An update takes [`UpdateCatalogEntry`].

oneOf.description:
The whole price list, replaced as one atom — the prices and the currency
they are quoted in are one provider's quote and are never merged
field-by-field. Absent means no price is known, which the gateway badges
rather than reporting as free.

server_id.description: NULL = global entry for this model (applies to all servers).

ChangelogResponse.description: Changelog response with markdown content and current version.

content.description: Markdown content of the full changelog.

ChatMediaSummaryEntry.description: Summary entry for `chat_media_summary` stored on llm_audit.

CimdClientRow.description:
One CIMD client observed holding tokens in this tenant.

A client that identifies itself by a published metadata URL never registers,
so it has **no `mcp_oauth_clients` row** — it is absent from the OAuth-client
list and out of reach of that list's revoke. This inventory is derived from
the tokens themselves, which is the only record such a client leaves.

client_id.description: The metadata-document URL the client presented as its `client_id`.

grants.description:
Distinct grants — one per consent, however many rotations it has been
through.

Counted by login chain rather than by user **deliberately**: a token row
outlives its subject (`user_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so a revocation
survives the account), and counting users would silently drop exactly
the orphaned rows an operator most needs to see here.

tokens_active.description: Tokens that would still be honoured right now.

tokens_issued.description: Every token ever minted for this client, revoked and expired included.

ClassHeldLive.description: Requests held for a server, of one class.

qos_class_id.description: `null` for a tenant with no classes.

ClassHeldSeries.description:
Requests held at the gateway for one class, per bucket: summed across
replicas within each 60 s window, as `EndpointGaugeSeries::in_flight` is —
the highest window (`held`), and the mean over the bucket's windows
(`held_mean`). A bucket with no beat is `null`.

qos_class_id.description: `null` for a tenant with no classes.

ClassTrafficSeries.description: One class's attempts at this server, per bucket.

qos_class_id.description: `null` for requests of a tenant with no classes.

series.description:
Aligned with `bucket_starts`; a bucket with no attempt of the class is
all zeros.

ClassifierProtocol.description:
Wire protocol the configured classifier endpoint speaks. Lets one
`classifier_url` target the classifier extension **or** another service
without per-vendor code.

oneOf.description:
The request validated. Render the "Streamscope CLI on X wants to
provision" copy.

user_email.description: The authenticated portal user the grant would bind to.

oneOf.description:
The request is invalid, but the client and its loopback redirect URI
check out — so the error belongs at that URI.

CliAuthorizePreviewResponse.description:
Payload returned by `POST /authorize/preview`.

Two dispositions for the RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 split — see the MCP surface's
twin for why the server, not the consent page, decides which one applies.

device_name.description:
Self-reported device label ("laptop hostname") shown on the consent
page and stored on the issued tokens.

token.description:
The refresh token to revoke. Its paired access token (`original_jti`)
is revoked with it.

CliSessionRow.description:
One `ssai login` — the machine, not the token.

A login is a **chain** of token rows: each pair is access + refresh, and
every refresh rotation retires the pair and mints another onto the same
chain. This row aggregates one chain, which is why its id is the chain and
not a jti — the operator revokes a machine, and the tokens are an
implementation detail of how that machine holds its access.

device_name.description:
Self-reported by the CLI at login (device-grant logins name the host).
Absent for a login that reported none — never treat it as an identifier.

expires_at.description: How long the machine can keep refreshing before it must sign in again.

id.description: The login chain. Also the revoke handle.

last_used_at.description:
When the machine last called, across the whole chain — a rotation mints
a new generation, but the last call belongs to the machine rather than
