to whichever generation was holding its access at the time.

`None` means it has not called yet. It is stamped at
roughly one write a minute, so read it as "active around then", never
as an exact last-request time.

revoked_at.description:
When the machine was deliberately cut off — by an operator here, or by
its own `ssai logout`. Read from the chain's NEWEST generation,
never from "some row is revoked": rotation revokes the generation it
replaces, so the latter would report every rotated-then-expired chain as
revoked, stamped with the time of a rotation.

signed_in_at.description:
When the machine signed in, from the oldest generation still on record.
The sweeper eventually purges long-expired generations, so on a chain
older than the retention window this walks forward rather than pinning
the original login.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the binary, hex — `ssai update` and the installer
script verify the download against it.

target.description: Target triple shorthand the download route accepts (e.g. `linux-x86_64`).

version.description:
Application version this gateway ships (the CLI binary is built from
the same release).

ClientAccessClient.description: One client profile as the Clients section shows it.

is_new.description:
Not offered, and added after the profile was created — a client a later
release shipped, waiting for an admin to enable it.

clients.description: Every live client profile, offered or not.

ClientProfile.description:
A client-config profile loaded from `seeds/client_profiles/<id>.json`.
One profile per client app (Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, …); each
carries one or more `templates` covering different downstream protocols
or use modes (LLM-only / MCP-only / combined / GUI instructions).

builtin.description:
Set by the loader (`true` when read from disk) and by the seed-sync
(`false` when an admin overrides the profile on a tenant).

homepage.description:
Link to the upstream project's docs — surfaced in the UI as a "Why
these settings?" link.

launch_command.description:
Command that launches the tool once provisioned (e.g. `claude`,
`opencode`). `None` for GUI clients (Cursor, Zed) that the user restarts
instead — the CLI then prints a "Restart <label>" hint.

compatible.description:
`true` iff this profile has at least one template the user can render
given their accessible downstream providers / MCP virtual servers.

incompatibility_reason.description:
User-actionable reason why `compatible = false`, naming the specific
gap (e.g. *no compatible LLM provider in your workspaces* or *no MCP
virtual servers your workspaces can reach*). `None` when `compatible`
is `true` — the UI shows this string as the disabled-card tooltip.

ClientProfileTemplate.description:
One copy-paste config template within a `ClientProfile`. The body is a
raw template string with `{{ident}}` placeholders and optional one-level
`{{#if ident}} … {{/if}}` conditional sections (line-stripped on
tag-only lines). See the render engine module for substitution semantics.

companions.description:
Files this template's configuration needs beside its body. Omitted from
the wire when empty, so a profile that declares none carries no extra
key.

filename.description:
Where the user should put the body. `None` for instructions / shell
snippets that aren't a file (e.g. curl one-liners, env exports).

instructions.description: Short user-facing prose rendered above the snippet. Optional.

key_delivery.description:
How the user gets the gateway key into this client. `Environment` is
the only exemption from the key-deliverability check — see
[`KeyDelivery`].

keyed_arrays.description:
Arrays of the body that the CLI merges ENTRY BY ENTRY instead of
replacing whole: a JSON pointer into the rendered document (`/models`,
or `/providers` for a TOML `[[providers]]`) → the field that identifies
an entry (`name`). Provisioning then writes, updates and removes only
the entries it rendered, and keeps the ones the user added beside them;
an array not listed here is still replaced whole. Every rendered entry
must be an object carrying a scalar identity (or, with a composite
field `a+b`, a scalar in each named field), unique within its array —
or, with the field [`STRING_ENTRIES`], a string identified by
[`string_entry_identity`] (`set-env: ["NAME=value"]`) in JSON or YAML.
Checked when the profile is saved. Omitted from the wire when empty.

mcp_auth_mode.description:
Only meaningful on `kind = mcp` and `kind = combined` templates;
ignored otherwise. Defaults to `static`.

project_filename.description:
Project-local destination, RELATIVE to the project root, used when
provisioned with `--local`/`--dir` (e.g. `.claude/settings.json`).
`None` ⇒ the client has no project-local form; in a project run it is
written to its global `filename` (the global scope) instead.

protocol.description:
Client-facing protocol the rendered snippet will hit (e.g.
`"responses"` for a snippet that posts to `/v1/responses`). Selects
the `{{base_url_*}}` placeholder variant. It does NOT constrain
which upstream the rendered snippet can be paired with — the proxy
translates between any client protocol and any upstream protocol.

route_tag.description:
Optional route-tag filter for the quickstart renderer. When set, the
renderer's `routes` block is restricted to downstream routes whose
`tags` array contains this value (e.g. `"opencode"`, `"claude-code"`),
and the top-level `{{model_alias}}` resolves to a route whose
`default_for_tags` contains it. Falls back to all enabled routes when
no route under the provider is tagged this way — keeps the renderer
usable on tenants that haven't tagged anything yet.

ClientSlot.description:
A client model slot besides the default: `fast` for a client's
background work (titles, search, commit messages), `plan` for its planning
model. One route per slot in a provider, and one route may fill both; a
client config whose slot no route fills uses the default route there.

CollisionTarget.description: One upstream target an alias resolves to within a colliding alias group.

CompanionTemplate.description:
A part of a template's configuration that is not its body: a credential
the tool reads from its own secrets or `.env` file, a part of the config
the tool reads from a file of its own (Claude Code's project MCP servers),
or a snippet the user runs because no file can carry it (Claude Code's
user-scope MCP servers live in a file the tool keeps its own state in, so
they are added with its own command). This is the
DECLARED form — `body` and `instructions` are Handlebars templates rendered
with the same placeholder map and the same sentinel contract as the owning
template's body. `path` is a literal and is deliberately NOT rendered, so
the set of files a profile can write stays reviewable in a seed diff.

instructions.description: Why this file exists, rendered above the snippet.

path.description:
Destination path, `~/`-anchored. The CLI writes here; the quickstart
shows it as the snippet's filename. `None` ⇒ no file outside a
project: with a `project_path`, the companion exists only under a
project scope; without one, it is a snippet shown and never written.

project_path.description:
Where the file goes under a project scope, relative to the project
root. `None` ⇒ the `~/` path re-anchored at the project root.

title.description: User-facing title for the snippet header.

Content.description:
Content-addressed rows records point at. Written `DO NOTHING` on their key:
content repeats freely across shares.

ContentKey.description: Names one content-addressed body: its store and its key within the tenant.

raw.description: The message this event renders, in its client protocol's wire shape (raw view only).

guardrails.description:
Inbound-prompt guardrail findings (P1/P2) that flagged this message —
the user's own prose (direct injection / jailbreak), an inbound PII
detection, or a tool-result the client folded into the turn (indirect
injection) — before it reached the model. One message can trip
several detectors at once (e.g. an injection step AND a PII step on
the same prose), so every finding is carried and rendered as its own
shield banner. Empty when the message was clean.

is_from_history.description:
True when this assistant message came from the client's request
history rather than from a proxy-captured response. Lets the UI
flag client-sent history echoes that didn't originate from any
captured upstream call — e.g. fabricated assistant turns. Always
false for user / tool / system events.

raw.description: The message this event renders, in its client protocol's wire shape (raw view only).

arguments.description: The call's arguments as the model sent them — whatever the tool's schema allows.

oneOf.description:
Populated when a policy rule rejected this tool call. The call is
still rendered (name + effective args) so operators see what the
model attempted, with a rule-identity banner attached. Boxed: this is
the rare block path, so keeping it out-of-line keeps the common
`ToolCall` variant small.

Populated when a substitution rule intercepted this call and ran it
server-side (web-executor). The call is rendered with an
"intercepted by policy" banner; the server-side execution + guardrail
surface on the following `web_call` event. Boxed for the same reason
as `blocked` — a cold-path payload kept out-of-line.

modifications.description:
Per-argument rewrites applied by policy rules or Rhai transforms.
The proxy does not populate this today — the field exists so the
UI can render transform-driven arg diffs once the pipeline captures
them. Empty / absent means the arguments are unchanged.

raw.description: The message this event renders, in its client protocol's wire shape (raw view only).

guardrails.description:
Inline-guardrail findings that flagged this folded tool-result — a
web tool-result carrying a prompt-injection attempt, an inbound PII
detection, or both at once — before it was folded back into the
model. Every finding is carried and rendered as its own shield
banner. Empty when the result was clean or not web-sourced.

raw.description: The message this event renders, in its client protocol's wire shape (raw view only).

oneOf.description:
Populated when a request-phase `redact_result` rule rewrote or
dropped this tool_result before it was forwarded to the model.
The content shown is the effective (redacted) payload; this slot
carries the original, the rule identity, and the reason so the UI
can surface a banner with a diff toggle — matching the treatment
`ToolCallBlock` gives to blocked tool calls. `None` when the
result passed through untouched.

Emitted when the client rebuilt the message array without reducing its size
(e.g., different system prompt, reorganized messages). The conversation
baseline was reset but no compaction occurred.

Emitted whenever the effective tool set differs from what the model
"saw" on the previous turn (`BetweenTurns`) or what the client sent on
this turn was modified by tool policy (`PolicyModified`). The UI
renders a compact "tools changed" banner with an expand-to-diff
affordance, dereferencing each hash via the lazy
`/audit/tool-definitions/{hash}` endpoint.
Media attachment (image, document, audio) extracted from a message.
The stored blob's kind — set whenever `content_hash` is.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 content hash for blob retrieval (set for blob_ref media)

data.description: Base64 data (inline for small media, omitted for large or stripped)

request_id.description:
The request that carried the stored blob — the turn's own request,
when it sent the bytes itself. Absent when the turn only names the
blob (a part the client wrote, or history it did not resend): the
portal's media route requires it, so such a blob is not served
there.

url.description:
The client's own reference to the media: an external URL or a
provider file id. Never a gateway URL — a stored blob is named by
`content_hash` + `blob_type` (+ `request_id` when the turn carried
it), from which each plane builds its own media route (the
console's and the portal's differ, and the portal's needs the
request to prove ownership).

oneOf.description:
Standalone media API call (embeddings, audio, images, video) linked to a session.

Carries the canonical [`DomainMediaCall`] as the single source of truth —
UI reads endpoint / model / input-output blocks / params / job status
directly from `media_call`. Blob hashes are embedded as `BlobRef` blocks
inside `media_call.input` / `media_call.output`. Boxed so the variant
doesn't bloat every other `ConversationEvent` variant on the wire.

Framework-injected volatile block (e.g. `<system-reminder>…`,
`<available-deferred-tools>…`, `<local-command-*>…`,
`<command-*>…`) that was embedded inline inside a user or
assistant text block. The event builder splits prose from these
blocks so the session UI can render the prose as a normal bubble
and the reminder as a collapsed card — matches the Anthropic-
style collapse seen in other LLM consoles.

`content` carries the full raw block including opening and
closing tags so the UI shows exactly what the framework injected.
`raw`, when present, is attached to the first emitted event for
the parent message (same single-shot rule as `ConversationEvent::Message`).

raw.description: The message this event renders, in its client protocol's wire shape (raw view only).

oneOf.description:
MCP gateway call interleaved into the LLM session timeline. The
proxy stamps `gateway_audit.session_id` with the same hashed value
the LLM path uses, so all of an agent's MCP traffic correlates
back to the LLM session by id. Rendered between turns at its
actual timestamp — matches the agentic workflow (LLM proposes a
tool → MCP gateway dispatches → result → next assistant turn).

params.description:
JSON-RPC request `params` payload (e.g. `{name, arguments}` for
`tools/call`, `{uri}` for `resources/read`). Surfaced so the
session-view bubble can render the actual call body inline.

result.description: JSON-RPC `result` payload returned by the upstream on success.

timestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp — used by the UI to position the bubble.

oneOf.description:
Typed diff payload stamped by the MCP policy engine + multiplex
pump. Same shape as `McpAuditLogEntry.transform_diff` so the
session-view bubble and the audit detail render through the
same UI primitives.

turn.description:
LLM turn this call sits between (the turn whose timestamp
most recently preceded this MCP call). `0` when the MCP call
fires before any LLM turn.

oneOf.description:
Single web (search or fetch) call dispatched against the built-in Web
virtual MCP server. Mirrors `McpCall`'s shape — backend-built so the
session-replay bubble and the audit-detail drawer render through
the same `WebCallEvent` component without reconstructing the event
shape client-side.

badges.description: Stamped audit badges for this call.

error_category.description: Typed error category when the call failed.

guardrails.description:
Inline-guardrail findings on the content this call fetched, surfaced
on the web operation itself (server-side). For `substitution` they are
the turn's `guardrail_steps` entries matched by `tool_use_id` (a
single fetch can trip several detectors at once); for `mcp` they are
normalized from the row's guardrail badges. Empty when clean.

result_count.description: search → hits returned post-filter; fetch → 1 on success.

timestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp — used by the UI to position the bubble.

turn.description:
LLM turn this call sits between (matches the `McpCall.turn`
semantics).

oneOf.description:
A2A gateway call — one agent invoking another — interleaved into the
session timeline beside the LLM turns and MCP calls that surround it.

This is the event that makes the orchestrator pattern legible: an LLM turn
emits a `tool_use` whose implementation is an outbound `SendMessage` to a
remote agent, and with the same `X-Session-Id` the decision and the
agent-to-agent exchange it caused sit in one timeline.

Content is carried as canonical [`DomainContentBlock`]s — the same block
vocabulary the LLM protocols normalize into — so a text part, an image an
agent returned, and a structured payload all render through the existing
block components rather than an A2A-specific renderer.

artifacts.description: Artifacts the agent produced — an A2A task's typed output.

oneOf.description:
Populated when a policy rule refused the call. The call is still
rendered — the caller really did attempt it — with a rule-identity
banner, exactly as a blocked tool call is.

caller_kind.description:
`"user"` or `"app"` — selects the caller glyph on the client; absent
when the principal is unknown (keyless / pre-auth error).

caller_label.description:
Who initiated the call — the authenticated gateway principal (the
user's email, else the client app id). This is the direction the
whole surface turns on: this caller is talking TO `agent_slug`, and
naming it is what makes an A2A row legible ("frank → research-desk").

guardrails.description:
Guardrail findings on the message or on the reply. Each renders its
own shield banner.

request_blocks.description: The message the caller sent, as it was sent (pre-screening).

response_blocks.description: The agent's reply — its message plus its task status message.

timestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp — used by the UI to position the bubble.

turn.description: LLM turn this call sits between (same semantics as `McpCall.turn`).

client_ip.description:
Forwarded end-client identity for the whole session, present only for Inline AI
traffic where a trusted inline key relayed it (`X-Client-IP` /
`X-Authenticated-User` / `X-Authenticated-Groups`) — gateway-asserted, NOT
authenticated here (distinct from `user_email`, the internal account).

detected_spawn_points.description:
Subagent spawn points detected in THIS session's own stream (the parent
side): each `Agent`/`Task`-style tool call, with the turn, id and a prompt
preview. Computed on read from the built events. The cluster judge confirms
a child↔spawn link from it, and the UI anchors child cards + content-matches
header-linked children that carry no stored anchor.

linkage_spawn_tool_call_id.description:
This session's own spawn anchor as a CHILD — the tool-call id in its parent.
Present only when a spawn call was confirmed; the parent's stream anchors the
child card on `(linkage_spawn_turn, linkage_spawn_tool_call_id)`.

turn_params.description: Canonical request-level parameters per turn. Keyed by turn number.

oneOf.description:
What the conversation cost, and in which currency. `null` when its
turns straddle a change of the tenant's accounting currency — they are
then stated in different denominations and no single figure states them.

card_url.description:
The upstream card URL (typically
`https://<agent-host>/.well-known/agent-card.json`). Fetched
server-side at create time.

credential.description:
Upstream credential plaintext (service_account only) — encrypted at
rest, never returned.

credential_header.description:
Header carrying the credential upstream. Unset = `Authorization:
Bearer <credential>`.

slug.description:
Mount handle: the agent becomes reachable at `/a2a/<slug>`. Globally
unique across tenants (the card endpoint is pre-auth).

display_name.description: Optional display name (kept in sync with a sibling gateway user row).

role.description:
Console role: `admin` (default) or `read_only`. Ignored on the SYSTEM
tenant, where admins are always full super-admins.

mode.description:
Defaults to `observe` — a new preset records before it serves, which is
the tuning path the admin flow is built around.

weight.description: Relative share of new sessions (≥ 1). Default 1.

merge_enabled.description:
Pool into merged analysis calls with shape-compatible experts (default
true); `false` = always a solo call.

CreateFieldProfile.description:
Body of POST /tool-field-profiles. Mirrors `tool_rules::FieldProfile` minus
server-managed `is_builtin` (always false on user create).

app_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the request `app_id`. Mutually
exclusive with `mcp_server`.

mcp_server.description:
Optional MCP server identifier (matches `mcp__<server>__<tool>`).
Mutually exclusive with `app_filter`.

server_type.description:
Optional server-tool discriminator (Anthropic `web_search_20250305`,
OpenAI Responses `web_search_preview`, Gemini `google_search`, or any
future provider's wire tag). Mutually exclusive with `app_filter` and
`mcp_server`. The matching `ServerType` tier outranks `mcp_server`,
`app_filter`, and generic in canonical-id resolution.

tool_id.description:
Canonical concept identifier the wire tool maps to (`shell_exec`,
`read_file`, `db_query`, etc.). Free-form string; `tool_ids.json`
documents the shipped taxonomy but new ids are first-class.

wire_field.description:
Optional actual arg key on the wire — used when the client emits a
different name than the canonical `field`. Defaults to `field`.

emergency.description: Emergency recovery invite — resets tenant auth_mode to internal.

oneOf.description: Optional per-key budget ceiling (omitted ⇒ no per-key cap).

downstream_provider_id.description:
For a BYOK (`forward_auth`) key, the BYOK downstream it is bound to.
Unconfigured models pass through to that downstream's upstream with the
client's own forwarded credential; routes inside the downstream override
individual models. Must be a `byok` downstream granted to `workspace_id`.
Ignored for `sk-` keys.

forward_auth.description:
When true, generate a `vk-` prefix key for BYOK (forward client auth on
`/fwd/{key}/...`). Otherwise a proxy-issued `sk-` key.

qos_class_id.description:
The key's priority class under load. Omitted means the workspace's own
class; a class more important than the workspace's is an elevation, and
only a tenant admin may make one.

workspace_id.description:
Workspace the key is bound to. The user must be a member; the workspace
allowlist gates which providers / MCP servers the key can reach.

key.description: The plaintext key — returned ONCE, never again.

proxy_base_url.description:
The tenant's configured gateway public origin (no trailing slash), for
rendering the BYOK connection URL (`{proxy_base_url}/fwd/{key}`). `None`
when `proxy_public_url` is unset — the UI falls back to a relative hint.

CreateMcpCatalogEntry.description: Request body for creating a custom catalog entry.

source_name.description: Seed-sync dedupe key. Defaults to `name` (uniquified per tenant).

auth_mode.description:
Defaults to `"no_auth"`. All four modes (`"no_auth"`,
`"service_account"`, `"per_user_oauth"`, `"byot"`) are honored.

credential.description:
Bearer token plaintext. Required when `auth_mode =
"service_account"`; rejected when any other auth_mode is set. Encrypted
at rest with AES-256-GCM (`ENCRYPTION_KEY` HKDF-derived). Never echoed
in responses — `has_credential: bool` surfaces presence.

oauth_client_secret.description:
Plaintext client secret (encrypted at rest, never echoed in responses).
Required when `auth_mode = "per_user_oauth"`; forbidden otherwise.

prefix.description:
Empty string allowed — only on a virtual server's first route; prefixed
routes may be added beside it.

sampling_credential.description:
LLM-family bearer pasted by the operator. Encrypted at rest with the
process `ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Write-only — the API never returns it.

website_url.description: MCP 2025-11-25 `serverInfo.websiteUrl` — must be a valid `http(s)://` URL.

catalog_model_id.description: Explicit catalog entry to inherit from. NULL = auto-match by canonical name.

healing_enabled.description: Per-model self-healing override. NULL = inherit the tenant `healing_enabled`.

oneOf.description:
Price override, replacing the catalog's map WHOLE (omitted = inherit it).
All-or-nothing by design: a price list is one provider's quote in one
currency, so taking half of it from the catalog is the borrowed-price
hazard the provider-matched ladder exists to prevent. An empty map is an
operator saying "no price", and does not fall through to the catalog.

client_id_metadata_url.description:
When set, also register a CIMD URL for follow-up resolution. Stored
at registration but not fetched here — CIMD resolution happens in the
`/authorize` flow.

redirect_uris.description:
At least one redirect URI required. Each must be `http://localhost*`,
`http://127.0.0.1*`, `https://...`, or an RFC 8252 private-use scheme
for a native app (`com.example.app:/cb`).

downstream_provider_id.description:
For a BYOK (`forward_auth`) key, the BYOK downstream it is bound to.
Unconfigured models pass through to that downstream's upstream with the
client's own forwarded credential; routes inside the downstream override
individual models. Must be a `byok` downstream granted to `workspace_id`.
Optional (a `vk-` key is also valid for MCP bring-your-own-token with no
LLM binding); ignored for `sk-` keys.

forward_auth.description: When true, generate a `vk-` prefix key for BYOK (forward client auth).

qos_class_id.description:
The key's priority class under load. Omitted takes the workspace's own
default for a person's tool; a class MORE important than the workspace's
is refused — only a tenant admin can grant one.

workspace_id.description: Workspace the key is bound to. The caller must be a member.

proxy_base_url.description:
The tenant's configured gateway public origin (no trailing slash), for
rendering the BYOK connection URL (`{proxy_base_url}/fwd/{key}`). `None`
when `proxy_public_url` is unset — the UI falls back to a relative hint.

settings.description:
Native partial request body. Validated against the model's resolved
protocol + capability ceiling. Defaults to `{}` (passthrough).

start_from.description:
How the new profile relates to the Default and what it starts from
(defaults to Layered + Blank — inherits the Default with no own content).

profile_id.description:
Transform profile scope. Omitted/`null` → **shared** (runs for every
profile's effective set — the baseline). A profile id → **specific** to
that transform profile.

trigger_regex.description:
Optional fast-find trigger regex. When set, the program runs only if the
in-scope content matches. Empty/omitted ⇒ always run.

upstream_server_id.description:
**Create-only** — ignored on update. The link to an upstream server is a
structural relationship set when the provider is created (a mirror's
source, or a BYOK pass-through target); `update_provider` deliberately
leaves it untouched so a name/description/icon edit can never re-point or
unlink it. This body type is shared by the PUT route, where the field is
accepted but silently unused.

cache_preset_id.description: Response-cache policy to bind. Absent / null = the alias is uncached.

client_context_window.description:
Client-facing advertised window (token-scaling). The one alias-scoped
client knob; never sent upstream.

default_for_tags.description:
Subset of `tags` marking this route as the canonical default for the
named tag — the renderer's top-level `{{model_alias}}` resolves to a
route whose `default_for_tags` contains the template's tag.

preset_id.description:
Invocation preset to bind. Absent / null = the model's **default** preset.
The preset MUST belong to `model_id`. The route is a pure pointer — it does
not redefine the upstream's capabilities/window/protocol/healing (those are
model truth) nor its invocation beyond selecting a preset.

reassign_default_tags.description:
When a `default_for_tags` entry is already claimed by another route in
this provider, move the default to this route (clearing it from the
others) instead of rejecting. Absent / false ⇒ reject with
`RouteDefaultTagConflict` so the caller can confirm first.

tags.description:
Operator-supplied client tags (e.g. `["opencode", "claude-code"]`)
used by the portal quickstart renderer to filter routes per client.
Empty / absent = visible to every client.

auto_sync_enabled.description:
Toggle autosync for this server (omitted = on). Autosync is the single
switch that owns the mirror: when on, adding the server discovers its
models and maintains a same-named mirror downstream; when off, the server
is manual (no discovery, no mirror — build a custom downstream instead).

byok.description:
Create a **BYOK pass-through** provider: a keyless upstream (the client
forwards its own credential; `api_key` is ignored) plus an empty `byok`
downstream of the same name. Unconfigured models pass through to
`upstream_url`; add routes inside the downstream to override individual
models. No discovery / mirror (keyless), so `auto_sync_enabled` is forced
off. Default false. **Create-only** — ignored on update, where BYOK is
derived from the linked downstream (set-once at create).

chat_endpoint_path.description:
Override for the appended chat-completions endpoint path when this
provider's OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint is not `{upstream_url}/v1/chat/completions`
(e.g. `/chat` for Writer, `/chat/completions` with no `/v1` for DeepInfra).
Omitted = the provider seed default (else the canonical `/v1/chat/completions`).
Applies only to the `chat_completions` protocol.

transport.description:
How the gateway carries requests to this server, orthogonal to the
protocol it speaks. `default` is a plain bearer-auth endpoint on
canonical `/v1/...` paths. `azure_openai` addresses an Azure OpenAI in
Microsoft Foundry resource on its v1 API (`{url}/openai/v1/...`) with the
key in an `api-key` header; `azure_openai_entra` is the same surface with
a Microsoft Entra ID token minted from a client-credentials document
supplied as `api_key`. `aws_bedrock` addresses Amazon Bedrock's
OpenAI-compatible surface (`{url}/openai/v1/...`) with a Bedrock API key
as the bearer token. `google_vertex` addresses Google Vertex AI from a
project/location URL, with an access token minted from a service-account
JSON key supplied as `api_key`. Omitted = the provider seed's transport,
else `default`.

upstream_url.description:
The server's URL, stored as its first (primary) endpoint. Omitted = the
provider seed's endpoint; a provider without one requires it.

email.description:
Stable login-less identity. When omitted, auto-derived as
`svc-<slug>@<tenant>.service`. Must be unique within the tenant.

CreateToolRule.description:
Body of POST /tool-rules. Mirrors `tool_rules::Rule` minus server-managed
`is_builtin` (always false on user create — settable only via reset/seed).

a2a_agent_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the A2A upstream agent slug. Scopes the
rule to specific agents; only meaningful on the `agent_calls` scope.

app_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the request `app_id`. Scopes the
rule to specific clients.

forked_from.description:
Copy-on-write link: when set (with `profile_id = Some(P)`), this rule is a
per-profile fork of the shared rule with this id — it overrides that shared
rule inside P. Used by the "Customize here" action.

id.description: Optional stable identifier. When omitted, the server mints a UUID.

mcp_server_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the MCP upstream server name. Scopes
the rule to specific upstreams; only meaningful for
`(request, resource_reads | prompt_invocations)` and MCP-gateway
`(response, tool_calls)` paths.

profile_id.description:
Profile scope. Omit (or `null`) → **shared** (applies to every profile —
the baseline). A UUID scopes the rule to that one profile.

email.description:
Stable login-less identity. Auto-derived from the name + workspace when
omitted. Must be unique within the tenant.

CreatedModels.description: The models a batch create added.

CrossSessionIssue.description:
One cross-session issue — a cluster/anomaly finding that spans several
sessions, linking to each via `source_session_ids`. The first-class home that
replaced stamping a multi-session finding onto one arbitrary session's alert.

DashboardSortBy.description:
Sort dimension for top-N panels. `count` is the default (busiest); `p95`
flips to slowest-by-P95-latency. Honored on every panel — answers "which
X is slowest" for tools, resources, prompts, endpoints, upstreams, users,
apps, and methods alike.

DeletionResponse.description:
Unified response for destructive endpoints.
Dry-run returns `dry_run: true` with impact preview.
Execute returns `dry_run: false` with mutation result.

affected_oauth_sessions.description:
Live OAuth grants the deletion ends — MCP client authorizations and
signed-in CLI machines. Distinct from `affected_keys`, which counts
`sk-` keys: a user can hold none of one and several of the other, and a
preview that mentioned only keys read as "nothing else to lose".

DeploymentMs.description: A deployment setting as the gateways run it.

low_ms.description:
The lowest and highest value among the connected gateways, in
milliseconds — equal when they agree.

reported.description:
`true` when read from what connected gateways report running; `false`
when none has reported yet, and the value is what they start with.

DestinationAttachment.description: One destination list the sandbox attaches.

is_builtin.description: `true` while a seeded list is as the seed ships it.

seed_key.description: The seed's handle for a seeded list; `null` on a list an admin created.

seeded.description: The list came from the seed (a reset can restore it).

DestinationListUse.description: One place a list is attached.

profile_id.description: The client-access profile attaching it (`sandbox` only).

DestinationMode.description: How a consumer reads an attached list.

DetectedSpawnPoint.description:
A subagent-spawning tool call detected in a parent conversation. The judge
references it by its position in the per-session list (`[P0]`, `[P1]`, …); the
UI anchors a child card to the composite `(turn_number, tool_call_id)` because
`tool_call_id` alone is only turn-unique (Gemini/legacy shapes synthesize a
per-turn `call_0`).

prompt_preview.description:
First ~200 chars of the child prompt/description the call carried, so the
judge can match it to a child session's first user message.

tool_call_id.description: Tool-call id of the spawn call (turn-unique, not session-unique).

turn_number.description: Parent turn the spawn call was made in.

device_name.description:
Self-reported device label ("laptop hostname") shown on the approval
page and stored on the issued tokens.

device_code.description:
The device's polling secret — presented to `/token` with the device
grant. Never shown to the user.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the device code expires.

interval.description: Minimum seconds the device must wait between `/token` polls.

user_code.description: The short code the user types on the approval page.

verification_uri_complete.description: The approval page with the user code pre-filled.

DeviceConsentPreviewResponse.description:
Payload returned by `POST /device/preview` so the approval page can render
the "device X wants to provision as you" copy.

user_code.description: Canonical `XXXX-XXXX` form of the code — the page submits this.

user_email.description: The authenticated portal user the grant would bind to.

user_code.description:
The code shown on the device — case, the dash, and whitespace are
normalised away.

url.description: The URL to ask, with this server's credential.

issuer_url.description:
Optional explicit issuer URL. When supplied, the PRM step is skipped
and authorization-server metadata is discovered directly from it — for
servers that don't expose PRM but whose issuer the operator knows.

upstream_url.description:
The MCP upstream server URL (the same value as the upstream row's
`upstream_url`). Discovery POSTs an `initialize` here to learn the
protected-resource-metadata location.

default_scopes.description:
Scopes to request by default — the PRM `scopes_supported` when present,
else the authorization-server `scopes_supported`.

issuer_host_mismatch.description:
True when the discovered issuer's registrable domain differs from the
`upstream_url`'s. A conformant server's login lives on the same site;
a mismatch (e.g. a `tools.example.com` server pointing login at
`login.evil.com`) is the confused-deputy shape the MCP spec warns
about, so the UI surfaces it as a prominent "verify this" warning
before the operator saves.

pkce_s256_supported.description:
Whether the authorization server advertises PKCE S256
(`code_challenge_methods_supported` contains `S256`). The MCP spec
requires clients to refuse a server without it; surfaced so the UI can
warn rather than silently proceed.

registration_endpoint.description:
The RFC 7591 dynamic-client-registration endpoint, when the server
advertises one *and* it passes the same guard the endpoints above do.

`None` means the operator must create a client by hand — which is what
most servers require (GitHub among them). The UI reads this to decide
whether to offer registration at all, because the alternative is a
button whose only possible outcome is an error after a full discovery
round trip.

The URL rather than a bare capability flag: registration is where a
client secret is handed out, so which host would receive that request
is worth showing the operator next to `issuer_host_mismatch`.

DiscoveredField.description:
One discovered `(tool_name, field)` pair from recent audit traces, with
the count of distinct tool definitions that exposed it. Operators click
"Register profile" to seed a CRUD form pre-filled with this pair.

already_covered.description:
True when a profile already covers this `(tool_name, field)` —
surfaced so the UI can hide already-registered fields.

mcp_server.description:
MCP server identity if the tool name parses as `mcp__<server>__<local>`.
Surfaced so the UI can display "via MCP server foo" alongside the row.

occurrences.description:
How many distinct tool definitions in the lookback window included
this field. Higher = more confident the field is real, not a typo.

suggested_tool_id.description:
Suggested canonical `tool_id` for the row. Stage C ships only the
"registry hard-map" classifier (Layer 1): MCP-namespaced tools whose
server matches a shipped `mcp_server` profile get a high-confidence
suggestion. Other tools have `None` — operator picks manually.

suggestion_confidence.description: Confidence in `[0.0, 1.0]`. `1.0` for registry hard-map matches.

suggestion_source.description:
Where the suggestion came from: `"registry"` for MCP hard-map; `null`
otherwise. Future layers (`heuristic`, `llm`) are deferred.

parent.description: The base model of an adapter (vLLM `parent`).

oneOf.description:
Prices the provider published, one entry per billing unit it names, each
normalized to that unit's natural scale (per 1M for token units, per unit
otherwise). `None` = the provider published no price at all, so the model
inherits the catalog's map rather than overriding it with an empty one.

Reading the unit off the provider's own key is what keeps a transcription
model (billed per second of audio) from being filed as a token-priced one
and then billing nothing.

root.description:
What the engine says it serves under this name (vLLM `root`: the weights
path, or an adapter's path). Compared across a server's endpoints to flag
replicas that may serve different weights under one name; never routed on.

DiskPressureLevel.description:
How full the disk is, as the host daemon's disk watch classifies it. It
reports only the two levels that call for a purge.

input.description:
Parsed tool-call arguments. `Value::Null` when the wire string failed JSON parse —
consult `input_raw` for what the model actually emitted in that case.

input_raw.description:
Raw argument string as emitted on the wire (OpenAI `function.arguments`).
Populated by `from_chat_completions` / `from_responses` to preserve the original
bytes for malformed-JSON diagnostics. `None` after `from_anthropic` / `from_gemini`
(their wire formats carry arguments as an object, not a string).

On **cross-protocol outbound** (e.g. Anthropic-shaped `DomainRequest` →
`to_chat_completions`), `input_raw` is regenerated from `input` via
`serde_json::to_string`; the result is semantically equivalent but loses any
client-supplied formatting quirks (whitespace, key order). Same-protocol
round-trips for OpenAI Chat / Responses preserve the original bytes verbatim.

thought_signature.description:
The opaque `thoughtSignature` Gemini put on the call's part. Only
Gemini signs a call, so only a Gemini target is sent it back; every
other target leaves it behind, as it does another provider's
thinking signature.

content.description:
Nested blocks — a tool result carries content of its own. The schema
stops here rather than unfolding the union into itself forever.

citations.description: The document's citation settings as the client sent them, in its protocol's shape.

oneOf.description: Base64 audio input (OpenAI `input_audio` content part).
Opaque file reference — provider file IDs or URLs that can't be inlined.

Streamscope-synthesized reference to a stored media blob.

Produced post-capture by `strip_media_from_messages` when inline media
(image, audio, document, file) is extracted to `audit_media_blobs` and
replaced with `{type: "blob_ref", content_hash, media_type, size_bytes, blob_type}`
in stored message JSON, and built by the media capture for a media call's
uploaded and generated files. A `BlobRef` reaching `to_*` (a client that
sent such a part itself) is forwarded as its raw JSON, never resolved to
stored bytes. Parsed from a message only when `content_hash` is a SHA-256.

Streamscope-synthesized placeholder for media that was stripped without storing.

Produced post-capture by `strip_media_from_messages` when blob storage is disabled
or the payload exceeds `media_blob_max_size_mb`. Read-path-only; forward pipeline
should never encounter this block.

Unrecognized content block — preserved as raw JSON for lossless pass-through.

Invariant: parsers must produce `Unknown { value: raw_value }` for any unrecognized
`type` field. Never silently dropped. UI renders via the shared `<RawJsonBlock>`
component. `to_*` serializes back to the original JSON verbatim.

value.description: The unrecognised block exactly as it arrived.

DomainMediaCall.description:
Canonical representation of a media API call (embeddings / speech / transcription /
translation / image generation / image edit / image variation / video generation).

Media endpoints are single-shot RPC: one input → one output (or async job). Parallel
to `DomainRequest` for multi-turn chat. Input/output reuse `DomainContentBlock`
primitives so the rendering path shares block-level rendering with chat turns.

Persisted as the single `audit_log.media_call` JSONB column — source of truth for
every media RPC turn. Serde shape is the public wire format exposed to the UI.

input.description:
Request-side blocks: `Text` (prompt), `Image` / `BlobRef` (source image for edits),
`Audio` / `BlobRef` (uploaded audio for transcription).

oneOf.description: Async job metadata — populated for endpoints with queued-then-poll semantics (video).

output_structured.description:
Structured output for endpoints returning shapes that don't fit the block model —
e.g. transcription verbose_json `{language, duration, segments[]}`.

output_units.description:
Unit count for cost / analytics aggregation — number of embedding vectors,
generated images, audio clips, video clips. One per request by default;
populated at capture time. Kept as a typed field because the unit semantics
differ per endpoint and can't always be derived from `output.len()` (e.g.
embeddings summarize N vectors in a single Text block).

extra.description: Any remaining provider-specific params we haven't modeled yet.

DomainRequestMeta.description:
Read-only projection of request-level parameters (model, sampling, tool catalog,
request metadata). Built from stored `conversation_turns.request_params` plus the
JOIN-resolved tool blob from `tool_definitions` (referenced by
`conversation_turns.tools_available_hash`) by `domain_request_meta_from_stored`,
surfaced per-turn to admin-ui for the "Request parameters" and "Tools available"
side panels.

Not a wire shape — no `to_*` serialization. Forward serialization uses
`DomainRequest::to_*` directly.

metadata.description: The request's `metadata` object as the client sent it; free-form by every protocol's spec.

response_format.description: The request's response-format object as the client sent it, in its own protocol's shape.

tool_choice.description: The request's tool choice as the client sent it (a string or an object, by protocol).

DomainToolSummary.description: Thin projection of `DomainTool` for the UI side panel.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the tool's arguments (protocol-normalized).

drain_secs.description: Seconds the stack drains before the action fires, 0 to 600.

DroppedTelemetry.description:
One audit entry per piece of client telemetry that had no equivalent on
the outbound target. Surfaced on `TransformDiff.telemetry_dropped` and
rendered as a chip in the session UI.

client_id_metadata_url.description:
CIMD opt-in. When present, we ignore `redirect_uris` for storage,
stash the URL on the row, and resolve fresh on each /authorize call.
The URL is SSRF-validated immediately (rejects loopback/RFC1918/IMDS).

grant_types.description:
Spec fields we accept but don't act on yet — present to keep RFC 7591
compliant clients happy. `grant_types` MUST contain
`authorization_code` (the only grant we support) when present;
`response_types` MUST contain `code`.

redirect_uris.description:
Required. At least one URI; each must be `https://` or
`http://localhost*` per the existing redirect-URI policy.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description:
`client_secret` is omitted for public clients (RFC 7591 §3.2.1 lets
us return only the fields we set) — our token endpoint uses
`none` auth (PKCE-only).

EdgeCacheStats.description:
What one replica's response cache holds, as reported by heartbeat.

Gauges (`entries`, `bytes`, `semantic_*`) are point-in-time; the `*_total`
counters are CUMULATIVE since that process started, so a rate comes from
differencing successive reports — never from the raw value.

evictions_total.description:
Entries given up to make room. Rising against a flat `entries` means the
cache is too small for its traffic — answers are thrown out before they
can be hit, which from the audit side is indistinguishable from nobody
repeating a prompt.

expired_total.description:
Entries dropped for reaching their TTL — the cache working as configured,
deliberately counted apart from eviction.

max_bytes.description: The replica's global byte ceiling — the denominator for `bytes`.

semantic_vectors.description:
Indexed prompt vectors. Above `entries` means vectors are outliving the
answers they point at, which has no symptom other than memory.

instance_key.description: The instance's own id, as it states it on every request.

outbox_pending.description: Rows the instance still had buffered for ingest at its last sync.

synced.description:
What the instance's last request said it holds — once no answer is
in flight or unreported ([`settled_held`]) — carries the current digest
of every resource this replica serves, as its cache has it (at most one
`EDGE_SYNC_REFRESH_MS` behind the database; the tenant status reads
the database itself).

usage_merged_at.description:
When admin-api last merged every counter of a usage report from the
instance. The edge reports every counter it holds each usage interval,
so the second stamp after a moment covers every counter it had accrued
by then — not a request whose accrual was still to come (a stream's
audit task; wait for `outbox_pending` to drain first), nor a delta the
edge itself dropped while admin-api was unreachable.

EdgeNodeMetadata.description:
Typed metadata bag stored on each edge node. Populated from the proxy
heartbeat payload (`stats`, `runtime`) and a server-assigned timestamp.

oneOf.description:
Runtime-config state reported by the proxy (effective settings + the
central-override subset it booted with) — the *actual* half of the
desired-vs-actual runtime-config model.
Live runtime stats from the proxy (most recent heartbeat).

stats_updated_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp when the stats block was most recently written.

connected_instances.description:
Proxy replicas (edge instances) syncing recently: 1 for a single-proxy
VM appliance, N for a horizontally-scaled (e.g. Kubernetes) Deployment.

is_connected.description: Some proxy replica of this edge has synced recently.

last_sync_at.description: The most recent sync by any of its replicas.

status.description: `active` admits the edge's token; any other value refuses it.

synced.description:
Every live replica holds the current config, as the answering admin
replica's cache has it (at most one `EDGE_SYNC_REFRESH_MS` behind).

EdgeProxyStats.description: Per-replica runtime stats, as reported with the instance state.

cache.description:
Response-cache occupancy and lifetime counters for the replica that sent
this heartbeat.

cores.description: Effective Tokio worker-thread count (the replica's parallelism), not host cores.

cpu_percent.description:
CPU% (100% == one core) and working-set bytes from the replica's cgroup —
real pod/container usage, not host-wide.

memory_limit_bytes.description:
Denominator for the replica's memory-pressure reading: its cgroup ceiling
(`memory.max`) normally, or — on the single-host VM appliance — the host's
total RAM, paired with a host-wide `memory_rss_bytes` (the appliance
reports whole-VM pressure, not the proxy container's slice of its own cap).
`None` off-cgroup or when unconstrained.

overhead_buckets.description:
Proxy-overhead histogram — the platform's own auth + transform +
routing time, excluding upstream. CUMULATIVE per-bucket counts since
proxy start, positioned against the shared bounds
(`streamscope_core::metrics::OVERHEAD_BOUNDS_US`, last slot =
overflow); windowed percentiles come from differencing consecutive
samples, like `requests_total`.

overhead_sum_us.description: Cumulative sum of recorded overhead in µs (histogram `_sum`).

pending_audit_count.description:
Audit records buffered locally on this edge that haven't yet flushed
upstream. Non-zero means the edge is queueing (admin-api disconnected,
remote backpressure, or a sync_request in flight).

EdgeRuntimeReport.description: Runtime-config state an edge reports with its instance state.

effective.description: Token → effective running value for every core + proxy setting.

loaded_overrides.description:
The central-override subset the edge actually applied at startup.
Compared against the desired override set to detect "restart pending".

EdgeRuntimeStatus.description: One edge node's actual runtime-config state.

effective.description:
Token → actual running value reported by this edge (core + proxy).
Empty when the edge has not reported a runtime block yet.

reported_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the most recent heartbeat, if any.

restart_pending.description:
Overridable tokens whose desired override differs from what the edge
booted with — the edge must restart to converge.

EdgeStatsBucket.description:
One time bucket of an edge's operational telemetry. Cumulative counters are
reported as per-bucket deltas; gauges as the bucket mean.

avg_active_streams.description: Mean concurrent streams across samples in the bucket.

avg_cpu_percent.description: Mean CPU utilisation (percent) across samples in the bucket.

avg_memory_mb.description: Mean resident memory (MB) across samples in the bucket.

errors.description: Errors in this bucket (delta of the cumulative counter).

memory_limit_mb.description:
Memory ceiling (MB) the edge runs under — the cgroup `memory.max` the
working-set figure is measured against. `None` when no sample in the
bucket reported a limit (off-cgroup or unconstrained replicas). Near
constant per replica, so the bucket reports the max observed.

p50_overhead_ms.description:
Platform-induced latency percentiles in milliseconds — the proxy's own
auth + transform + routing time, excluding the upstream provider.

requests.description: Requests served in this bucket (delta of the cumulative counter).

instances.description: Every instance that has used the v2 sync, most recent first.

ready.description:
False until the answering replica has built its config cache (it starts
at boot); while false, no instance is reported synced — ask again.

untracked_tables.description:
Tables a config build on the answering replica read that carry no
change triggers — a change to one never reaches an edge. Empty is the
only correct value.

EffectiveLimitStack.description:
What actually limits one member inside one workspace: every bucket that
applies, widest first, with the one closest to its cap named.

oneOf.description:
The layer with the least headroom (highest use/cap across its metrics),
or `None` when nothing caps the member.

currency.description: The tenant's accounting currency the budgets are expressed in.

a2a.description: A2A upstream agents and their cards.

cimd.description:
OAuth client metadata documents a client advertises (CIMD) — reachable
from the unauthenticated registration endpoint.

extensions.description:
The extension endpoints a tenant sets: the web search backend and the
guardrail classifier.

llm.description:
LLM providers: gateway requests, liveness probes, model discovery,
replica endpoints, engine gauges.

mcp.description: MCP upstream servers and their OAuth discovery.

upstream_token.description: Upstream token endpoints a minting transport exchanges its credential at.

web.description: The built-in web tool's fetches (URLs an end user or a model supplies).

EmbeddingAliasOption.description: One selectable alias for the embedding picker.

verified.description: True once a probe has confirmed this alias produces vectors.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable outcome. The UI branches on this, never on
`message`.

dimensions.description: Vector width, when one came back.

id_token_hint.description:
The ID token from the login being ended, so the provider knows which
session to close.

url.description:
`None` when the provider publishes no `end_session_endpoint`, in which
case the caller clears its own cookies and stops there.

EndpointBeat.description:
The instance's live load on each replica endpoint and its stand on each
endpoint it routes to. Stated in full: an endpoint the beat does not name
is one the instance no longer routes to.

load.description: One `EndpointLoadReport` per replica endpoint (edge protocol only).

states.description: One `EndpointState` per endpoint the instance routes to (edge protocol only).

EndpointDiscoveryPreview.description: What an endpoint at a URL would contribute, asked before it is saved.

answered.description:
Whether the URL answered with a model list. When it did not, it would be
assumed to serve every model of the server.

not_listed.description: The server's models it did not list.

EndpointDiscoveryStatus.description: The last discovery attempt against an endpoint.

kept.description:
Why the models the answer did not name were kept rather than removed:
`first_answer`, `server_first_sync` or `short_answer`. Absent when the
answer was trusted to remove them.

listed.description: How many models the answer named.

ok.description: Whether the endpoint answered with a model list.

reason.description: Why the endpoint did not answer.

EndpointGaugeSeries.description:
One endpoint's gauges per bucket: each bucket's PEAK, and its mean beside
it. A replica reports, on each heartbeat, the instant and the highest value
since its previous beat; the mean of the instants dilutes a burst by the
length of the bucket — a minute at 100% KV reads under 2% over an hour —
and an instant misses a burst between two beats, while the peak keeps it.
`null` for a bucket with no reading.

engine_waiting.description:
The engine's own gauges: its highest reading in the bucket, from any
replica — they all read the same engine. `null` where it was not read.

engine_waiting_mean.description: The same gauges' mean over every reading in the bucket.

in_flight.description:
Requests in flight across the gateway replicas: summed across replicas
within each 60 s window (each holds one beat of every live replica, a
beat carrying its replica's highest count since the one before), and
the highest such window in the bucket — the fleet's peak. A pod and the
one replacing it are added only in the one window that can hold the
old pod's last beat and the new one's first, never across the bucket.

in_flight_mean.description: The same windows' sums, averaged over the bucket's windows.

learned_limit.description:
The learned in-flight limit: each replica's, summed across replicas per
window, averaged over the bucket — what the gateways together let through.
`null` where the limit is not learned.

EndpointHealth.description:
The breaker state each connected gateway reported for an endpoint.

Only reports from gateways connected now, made since their current process
began (`epoch_started_at`), count: an older report is from a process that
restarted with every breaker closed. A disabled endpoint takes no traffic,
so its breaker is not shown.

down_gateways.description: Connected gateways whose breaker for this endpoint is open.

down_since.description: When the earliest of those breakers opened.

reason.description: The most recent reason a breaker opened.

EndpointHealthStatus.description: Runtime health of an endpoint as the connected gateways report it.

EndpointLive.description: The live load of one endpoint.

oneOf.description: Where the learned in-flight limit stands, when the limit is learned.

The engine's own gauges, from the most recent reading any replica took.
`null` when it is not read, or no replica hears from it.

engine_read.description: Whether the gateway reads this engine's own gauges.

engine_silent_replicas.description:
Replicas that read this engine and have stopped hearing from it: each
is not applying its queue bound, whatever the others see.

gated.description:
Whether the gateway counts this endpoint's requests (it declares a
bound). `in_flight` and `capacity` mean nothing when it does not.

queue_bounded.description:
Whether a queue bound depends on that reading. A silent engine with
one is not applying it; without one, only its charts are missing.

adaptive_grew.description:
What the learned limits did in the bucket, summed over the replicas
(each runs its own): windows raised, stepped down for a round of token
latency above the target, and back-offs by cause. `null` where the
limit is not learned.

engine_computed_prompt_tokens_per_s.description:
Prompt tokens the engine computed — looked up in its prefix cache and
found neither there nor in its CPU tier — per second: a recomputed
history shows here, not in the prompt tokens served.

engine_itl_ms.description:
Mean time between two output tokens of one request, in milliseconds —
what a learned limit's token-latency target is held against.

engine_preemptions_per_min.description:
Requests the engine preempted (evicted from its KV cache to recompute
later), per minute.

engine_prefix_hit_rate.description:
Prompt tokens the engine did not recompute — found in its prefix cache,
or loaded back from its CPU tier — as a fraction of those looked up.

engine_prompt_tokens_per_s.description:
Derived from the engine's own cumulative counters: the change between
consecutive readings of one gateway replica (a fall is an engine
restart, counted from zero), averaged across the replicas that read it —
they all read the same engine. `null` where it was not read, or does not
publish the counter.

engine_queue_time_ms.description:
Mean time a request spent in the engine's own waiting queue, and to its
first token, in milliseconds.

engine_queueing_at.description:
The most the engine was seen running while it kept a queue of its own,
over the period. Not a capacity: an engine queues on its token budget
per step as well as on its memory or batch cap. `null` when it did not
queue in the period.

EndpointLoadSeries.description: One endpoint's live load over the window, per bucket.

EndpointMembership.description: What an endpoint is taken to serve.

EndpointRemovalResponse.description: What removing an endpoint did (or, on a dry run, would do).

models_removed.description: Retired models deleted outright (nothing curated referenced them).

retired_models.description: Models only this endpoint served, retired by the removal.

routes_deleted.description: Automatic routes of the retired models, deleted.

routes_disabled.description: Hand-built routes of the retired models, disabled and flagged.

max_in_flight.description:
This replica's own capacity, when it overrides its server's. `null` =
it uses the server's value.

mismatched_models.description:
Models this endpoint answered "model not found" for since its last
discovery answer — it was assumed or listed to serve them and does not.

primary.description: The first enabled endpoint, whose URL is the server's `upstream_url`.

EndpointSyncReport.description: What one endpoint contributed to a sync.

answered.description:
Whether it answered with a model list. An endpoint that did not answer
changed nothing: every model it served was kept.

kept.description:
Why the models its answer omitted were kept rather than removed:
`first_answer`, `server_first_sync` or `short_answer`. Absent when the
answer was trusted to remove them, or it did not answer.

listed.description: How many models its answer named.

kv_usage.description: KV-cache use, a fraction in `[0, 1]`; `null` when not published.

running.description: `null` when the engine does not publish the gauge — never a zero.

EngineProbe.description: What one endpoint's engine said when asked for its metrics just now.

answered.description: Whether a document with an engine's queue gauges came back.

credential_presented.description: Whether the server's credential was presented with the read.

kv_capacity_tokens.description: Tokens the engine's KV cache holds (blocks × block size), when it says.

metrics_url.description: Where the metrics were asked for: the endpoint's server root.

observed_peak_running.description:
The most this engine has run while requests waited behind it — seven
days of readings and this probe: what it sustained while queueing, not
a capacity. `null` until it has been seen queueing.

reason.description: Why not, in the terms an operator fixes.

running.description: `null` when the engine does not publish the gauge.

suggested_max_in_flight.description:
This engine's own per-gateway in-flight limit: its peak divided by the
gateway replicas — what to set on THIS endpoint when its engine differs
from its siblings (another GPU, other engine settings).

EngineProbeResponse.description:
An engine check for every endpoint of a server, and what the history says
its concurrency is.

gateway_replicas.description:
Gateway replicas connected now. The in-flight limit applies per gateway
replica, so an engine can receive this many times it.

observed_peak_running.description:
The SMALLEST of the engines' observed peaks: the limit applies to every
endpoint of the server, so the engine that fills first decides it.
`null` until EVERY enabled engine has been seen queueing.

suggested_max_in_flight.description:
A per-gateway in-flight limit that keeps the total at the observed
peak: the peak divided by the gateway replicas, at least 1.

Event.description: An event for the edge's tenants (an MCP user event today).

body.description: Polymorphic by event kind; the edge dispatches on its `type`.

expert_ids.description:
Expert ids enabled on this profile (its explicit membership rows). The
Default is seeded with all enabled experts but is editable like any profile.

is_default.description:
True for the tenant default expert profile (the shared base). Drives the
UI's "Reset to seed" affordance; no longer implies read-only.

merge_enabled.description:
Whether this expert pools into merged analysis calls with shape-compatible
experts; `false` = always analyzed by its own solo call.

FetchProvider.description: Where the `web_fetch` tool extracts content from.

FieldProfile.description:
Maps a raw `(tool_name, app_id|mcp_server)` to a canonical `tool_id`,
and per-arg `field` to the wire field + normaliser. Operators register
these per-client so a single rule (`tool_id = read_file`,
`arg.path glob /etc/*`) catches every client's variant of the same
conceptual tool, and so obfuscation tricks (whitespace, percent-encoding,
case) are defeated by the normaliser before matching.

Disambiguation: `server_type`, `mcp_server`, and `app_filter` are mutually
exclusive on a given profile. A profile sets exactly one (or none, for a
generic fallback). Lookup precedence is:
  1. `server_type` matches an inbound `DomainTool.server_type` (Anthropic
     `web_search_20250305`, OpenAI Responses `web_search_preview`, Gemini
     `google_search`, …)
  2. `mcp_server` matches the parsed MCP namespace
  3. `app_filter` matches the request's app_id
  4. Generic (none set)

Then by `priority` ASC, then by load position.

app_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the request's `app_id`. Mutually
exclusive with `mcp_server` — a profile is either app-scoped or
MCP-server-scoped, never both.

description.description: Human-readable description ("Claude Code Bash tool — shell command").

field.description:
Canonical arg field name (e.g. `command`, `url`, `path`). Rules
reference this in `arg.<field>` conditions. The engine maps this to
`wire_field` (or `field` when `wire_field` is unset) when fetching
the value from `arguments`.

id.description:
Stable operator-visible identifier (e.g. `TFP-claude-Bash-command`).
Surfaces in the discovery/registration UI and audit-style logs so
reviewers can trace why a field was canonicalised a specific way.

is_builtin.description:
Server-managed: `true` on initial seed, `false` after the first PATCH/PUT.
Mirrors [`Rule::is_builtin`]. Ignored on incoming client payloads.

mcp_server.description:
Optional MCP server identifier. When set, this profile only matches
when the wire tool name is `mcp__<server>__<local>` and `<server>`
equals (case-insensitively) this value, OR when the engine was given
an out-of-band `mcp_server` hint matching this value.

normalizer.description:
Which normaliser to apply. Hardcoded set; unknown values fail
deserialisation.

priority.description:
Lower wins on overlapping `(tool_pattern, field)` matches. Default 100.
Stable-sorted with array position as the tiebreaker so manual order
still controls equal-priority entries.

server_type.description:
Optional server-side server-tool discriminator. When set, this
profile matches only when the inbound `DomainTool.server_type`
equals this value (case-insensitively) — covers Anthropic
`web_search_20250305`, OpenAI Responses `web_search_preview`,
Gemini `google_search`, and any future native server-tool. The
`ServerType` precedence tier outranks `mcp_server`, `app_filter`,
and generic; consult `lookup_with_server_type` /
`resolve_tool_id_for_definition` to drive the lookup with a
`server_type` hint.

source.description:
Provenance tag, e.g. `"claude-code:builtin"`, `"mcp-registry:filesystem@1.0"`.
Display-only — the engine doesn't read it.

tool_id.description:
Canonical concept identifier (e.g. `shell_exec`, `read_file`). Rules
pivot on this id rather than tool-name globs. Free-form string —
`tool_ids.json` is documentation, not an enforced enum.

tool_pattern.description:
Pipe-separated case-insensitive glob over tool names. Same syntax as
`Rule.match[].value` for `glob` conditions. For MCP-namespaced tools
(`mcp__<server>__<tool>`), this matches the unprefixed local name —
`mcp_server` carries the server identity separately.

wire_field.description:
Optional actual arg key on the wire. Defaults to `field` when null.
Use this when the client emits a different name than the canonical:
`field: "path"`, `wire_field: "target_file"` for Cursor, etc.

FieldProfileSuggestionResponse.description:
A pending/reviewed field-profile suggestion proposed by the agent. Displayed
read-only; on approval the row is registered in `tool_field_profiles`.

content_hash.description:
Hash of every field an approval installs; send it back on approve so
the approval installs exactly what was reviewed.

FieldSource.description:
Where a resolved field value comes from, for the model editor's per-field
source badge. `User` = operator pinned it (in `user_overridden_fields`);
`Synced` = a provider discovery wrote it; `Catalog` = inherited from the
linked/matched catalog entry; `Default` = the built-in baseline.

GetSettingsResponse.description:
Wire shape for `GET /api/v1/admin/settings`. Bundles the writable per-tenant
`TenantSettings` with the read-only `inherited` block so the UI can show
"Currently inheriting `<X>`" chips without a follow-up call.

GlobalAdminAuditRow.description:
One row in `GET /api/v1/admin/global/admin-audit`. Same shape as the
tenant-scoped row plus `tenant_slug` for the UI's tenant column / filter.

change_diff.description: `{ "before": <row>, "after": <row> }` for the resource the call changed, or `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n> }` when it was too large to keep; `null` when nothing was captured or nothing changed.

request_body.description: Redacted request body (secret-shaped keys removed); `null` when the body was empty or not JSON; `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n>, …identity fields }` when it was too large to keep.

response_error.description: The error body the call answered with (`{code, message}` for a current release, any stored JSON for an older one); `null` on success.

GlobalEdgeStatsResponse.description: Response for the global per-edge stats endpoint.

edges.description: One series per edge node that reported samples in the window.

GlobalPortalAuditRow.description:
One row in `GET /api/v1/admin/global/portal-audit` — `PortalAuditRow` plus
`tenant_slug` for the UI's tenant column.

change_diff.description: `{ "before": <row>, "after": <row> }` for the resource the call changed, or `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n> }` when it was too large to keep; `null` when nothing was captured or nothing changed.

request_body.description: Redacted request body (secret-shaped keys removed); `null` when the body was empty or not JSON; `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n>, …identity fields }` when it was too large to keep.

response_error.description: The error body the call answered with (`{code, message}` for a current release, any stored JSON for an older one); `null` on success.

GlobalUsageSummary.description: Top-level response for the global usage analytics endpoint.

GrantedWorkspace.description: A workspace holding a grant on a provider.

GuardrailAction.description: What the inline injection guardrail did with a flagged verdict.

GuardrailBackendResponse.description:
Response for `GET /api/v1/admin/settings/guardrail`: the tenant-wide
classifier backend.

GuardrailBackendSettings.description:
Tenant-wide guardrail **backend** config — the classifier deployment shared
by every guardrail profile in the tenant. Backed by `system_settings.guardrail`.
Never per-workspace: one classifier endpoint, one alert producer. Combined
with a per-profile [`GuardrailPolicy`] via [`GuardrailSettings::resolve`].

max_windows.description:
Maximum bounded sliding windows a single long **prose** input (inbound
prompt / model response) is split into. `0`→`1`.

max_windows_content.description:
Same cap for gateway-fetched **third-party content** (web results, peer
agent replies) — the P0 surface, so it gets more coverage. `0`→`1`.

notify_on_detection.description:
Emit a daily notification when verdicts are flagged in observe mode.
Tenant-wide (the alert producer is leader-elected and tenant-scoped), not
per-profile.

positive_label.description:
Label that signals a positive (injection) classification for
`hf_text_classification`. Ignored by `openai_moderations`.

spotlight.description: Wrap each fetched tool-result in spotlight datamarking delimiters.

GuardrailCategory.description: Category of a guardrail finding. Append-only — never rename a variant.

GuardrailFailMode.description: How a detector failure (timeout / transport / parse error) is handled.

GuardrailMode.description: Posture applied to a flagged verdict.

GuardrailPolicy.description:
Per-profile guardrail **policy** — the posture a workspace's selected profile
applies. Backed by `system_settings.guardrail_profiles` keyed by profile id;
an absent entry resolves to [`GuardrailPolicy::default()`]. Combined with the
tenant [`GuardrailBackendSettings`] via [`GuardrailSettings::resolve`].

enabled.description:
Master toggle. Default **on** (still inert without a resolved backend
`classifier_url`, mirroring [`GuardrailSettings::is_active`]).

pii.description: In-process PII detection / redaction (no backend — fully per-profile).

scan_inbound.description: Also screen the inbound prompt (P1/P2). Opt-in.

threshold.description: Confidence at or above which a verdict counts as flagged.

pii_entity_types.description:
The closed set of PII entity types the in-process detector recognizes —
the options the UI offers in the PII entity allowlist. Server-owned.

GuardrailPolicyResponse.description:
Response for `GET /api/v1/admin/profiles/{id}/guardrail`. The profile's
policy plus the closed PII entity-type set the editor offers.

GuardrailStepDiff.description:
One guardrail classifier finding on a fetched/searched web tool-result,
anchored to the `ConversationEvent::ToolResult` it scanned via `tool_use_id`
(the same join `BlockedToolInfo` uses). Surfaces as a numbered step in the
session trace beside transforms and policy. Severity is rendered bucketed
(Low/Med/High) in the UI; the raw `confidence` here is audit-only.

call_id.description:
On the inbound surface, a finding about a tool output the conversation
holds inside an assistant turn (a Responses built-in tool's output): the
call it answers, naming which of that turn's results it is about. `None`
on every other step.

oneOf.description:
Finding category as classified (prompt-injection on the web surface).
`None` on a no-verdict step (a detector `Error` / incomplete scan) — there
is no classification to report; the paired `error` reason describes why.

confidence.description:
Raw positive-class confidence in `[0, 1]`. Audit-only — the UI renders a
Low/Med/High bucket, never this number. `None` on a no-verdict step
(paired with `category: None` and a set `error`).

error.description:
Sanitized, body-free reason token present on any step that was *not* a
clean classifier verdict — a fail-open `Error` (content passed) or a
fail-closed `Blocked` withhold driven by a detector error / incomplete
scan. On such a step `category`/`confidence` are `None` (no verdict) and
this reason is the discriminator the UI keys on. Absent on a
verdict-driven `Flagged`/`Blocked` step (where `category`/`confidence` are
`Some`).

name.description: Stable step name shown in the trace (`guardrail:classifier`).

outcome.description: What the guardrail did with the finding.

phase.description: Pipeline phase the scan ran in (the web fold-back is `response`).

target.description:
What was scanned — the fetched URL or the search query, truncated; on a
response PII step, the answer it is in when not the first
(`choices[1]`, `candidates[1]`).

tool_use_id.description:
Anchor tying the finding to the event it scanned. On the response/web
surface this is the `tool_use_id` of the scanned tool-result (`response`
for the model's reply); on the inbound surface it is a **reverse**
message index (distance from the end of the domain message list, as a
string) of the flagged user message, folded tool-result, or assistant
turn holding a built-in tool's output (`call_id` names which), resolved
against the rendered message count in `build_events` (reverse so it
survives the session view's dedup filter).

GuardrailStepOutcome.description:
What the inline guardrail did with one classifier finding on a web
tool-result. Only a finding or a coverage gap produces a step — a clean,
fully-screened scan leaves no entry (its absence is the all-clear), keeping
the trace focused.

Held.description: A resource the edge holds, and the digest of the body it applied.

HostVersion.description: A release: the project version at a package revision.

ImpactCheck.description: Returned on `?dry_run=true` — preview of how many users/keys are affected.

instance.description:
The edge instance: an id created with the edge's durable store and kept
in it, the `instance_key` of its `edge_instances` row under the
authenticated edge.

oneOf.description: Sent when due (every heartbeat interval).

shares.description:
Each written in its tenant's own transaction; answered index-aligned
in [`IngestResponse::shares`].

oneOf.description: Sent when due (every usage-sync interval).

one_shots_settled.description:
The request's one-shot events are stored (or need never be): the edge
may forget them. False when the request carried none, or when applying
them failed for some tenant — the edge then restates them.

shares.description: One outcome per request share, in request order.

oneOf.description:
Present when the request carried usage from the instance's current
epoch.

InheritedDefaults.description:
Read-only effective values after layering tenant override over the SYSTEM
default. The keys mirror SYSTEM-defaulted entries on `TenantSettings`. A
`None` entry means *neither* layer is configured — the dependent surface
fails closed for this tenant. Generic carrier: any future
SYSTEM-defaulted setting lands here too.

InjectionBlock.description:
Structured record of what a specific transform step changed.
Captured at execution time in the proxy — no downstream diffing needed.

InstanceState.description:
One instance's state, restated every heartbeat interval. The stated parts
apply only when `(process_epoch, seq)` is newer than what admin-api applied
for the instance (per tenant for the tenant-scoped parts), and never from
an epoch older than the instance's current one. The one-shot parts
(`health`, `model_missing`) apply once per [`OneShot::id`] instead, whatever
report carries them.

model_missing.description: "Model not found" answers from endpoints, not yet answered.

seq.description: Increases with every report within one process epoch.

InterceptBinding.description:
Record of a tool definition rewritten by a `Substitute` / `InterceptOnly`
rule at the `Request × ToolDefinitions` phase. The bindings list is the
contract between the request-phase rule walker and the response-phase
agent loop: every `tool_use` echo whose `name` matches `replaced_name`
MUST be routed through the bound `intercept` handler instead of being
forwarded to the client.

`original_name` is the tool name the client declared on the wire (which
may have been renamed or substituted away); `replaced_name` is the name
the upstream sees and is the join key used by the response side.

action.description:
Action variant that produced the binding: `"substitute"` (definition
rewritten) or `"intercept_only"` (definition unchanged, only the
response-side handler is bound).

original_server_type.description:
`Some(server_type)` when the substituted/intercepted tool was a native
server-tool on the wire (Anthropic `web_search_20250305`, Responses
`web_search_preview`, Gemini `google_search`); `None` for client
function-tools. Acts as the visible-mode discriminator for the
substitution agent loop: `Some` ⇒ render synthesised
`server_tool_use` / `web_search_tool_result` blocks back to the
client; `None` ⇒ fully invisible (Decision #1).

rule_id.description:
