Stable identifier (e.g. `WS-SUB-CC-WEBSEARCH`) of the rule that bound
the intercept.

oneOf.description:
Execute via the built-in `WebService` (phase-1 executor). The
only intercept currently supported; agent-loop wiring lands in a
follow-up PR.

InterceptedToolCall.description:
One model tool call the gateway intercepted and ran server-side (a
`substitute`/`intercept_only` rule with a web-executor binding). The agent
loop absorbs the call — it never reaches the client and is not in the turn's
`response_tool_calls` — so this record is the only audit of *what the model
asked for* and *which rule diverted it*. The admin event builder replays it
as a visible `ToolCall` carrying an "intercepted by policy" banner, and
`tool_use_id` is the join key to the server-side `web_audit` row and the
`guardrail_steps` finding for the same dispatch.

arguments.description: Arguments the model emitted for the call.

name.description: Tool name the model called (the client-declared name, e.g. `web_search`).

replaced_name.description: Name the upstream saw after the definition was rewritten.

rule_id.description: Id of the substitution rule that diverted the call.

server_type.description:
Native server-tool type when the intercepted tool was a server-tool on the
wire (visible-mode); `None` for client function-tools.

tool_use_id.description:
Id of the dispatched call — correlates to `web_audit.tool_use_id` and the
matching `guardrail_steps[].tool_use_id` for this dispatch.

InterceptionInfo.description:
Rule-identity payload attached to a `ConversationEvent::ToolCall` when a
substitution rule intercepted the call and ran it server-side (the model's
call was diverted to the gateway's web executor, never reaching the client).
The call is rendered with this banner so operators see *which rule* diverted
it; the server-side execution + guardrail surface on the following
`web_call` event.

replaced_name.description: Name the upstream saw after the tool definition was rewritten.

rule_id.description: Stable rule identifier of the substitution rule.

rule_title.description: Human-readable rule title, resolved from the rule id when available.

server_type.description:
Native server-tool type when the intercepted tool was a server-tool on
the wire (visible-mode); `None` for client function-tools.

token.description: Plaintext token — shown once, never stored.

IssuedTokenRow.description:
One row in the `/mcp/issued-tokens` list. Joins display fields (user
email + display_name, client name, endpoint slug) so the UI can render
without secondary lookups.

IssuedTokensListResponse.description:
Tokens-tab list payload: page of rows + the same-scope status counts
rendered above the table. One round trip for both.

oneOf.description:
[`AUTO_ITL_TARGET_RATIO`] times the engine's own time per token at low
load, as the window has learned it by now
([`AdaptiveWindow::low_load_itl`]); no target until it has.
The operator's own figure, in milliseconds between two tokens.
No target: the limit grows as far as the engine's memory holds.

ItlTarget.description:
The token-latency target a learned limit keeps its engine within (its
server's setting), in seconds once applied
([`AdaptiveWindow::set_latency_target`]).

JsonWebKey.description:
One public key in the set published at `jwks_uri`.

Only the shape we actually publish: a P-256 verification key. Every field is
mandatory on the wire because every field is one a verifier needs to select
and use the key, so `Option` would only describe documents we never emit.

kid.description:
Matches the `kid` header of the tokens this key verifies, so a client
selects by header rather than by trying each key in turn.

use.description: Always `sig` — these keys verify signatures and nothing else.

JsonWebKeySet.description:
Body of the `jwks_uri` document (RFC 7517 §5).

Carries the active signing key **and** any verify-only secondary, which is
what makes an `AUTH_SECRET` rotation invisible to clients: a token minted
before the rotation still names a key the set publishes, so a verifier that
re-fetches finds it rather than failing every signature for the overlap.

KeyBudget.description:
Optional per-key budget ceiling. Enforced as a third "stricter wins" bucket
(workspace, per-user, key) keyed by the key id — budget only, no RPM/TPM.
Settable by tenant admins and workspace managers; not self-service.

daily_budget.description: Daily budget in the tenant's accounting currency. `null` = no daily cap.

monthly_budget.description: Monthly budget in the tenant's accounting currency. `null` = no monthly cap.

KeyDelivery.description:
How the gateway key reaches the user for a given template.

`Config` is the ordinary case: the key must be reachable from what a render
hands over — the rendered body, the rendered instructions (for
`kind = instructions`, where the prose IS the deliverable), or one of the
template's companions; a print-only snippet may also lean on an
LLM-bearing sibling template, but a template that writes a file may not.

`Environment` states that the tool reads the key ONLY from a process
environment variable the user exports, and loads no file we could write
(Zed). Nothing can deliver it but the portal showing the plaintext once at
render time, so declaring it here is what turns that from an accident into
a stated claim — and it is the only thing that exempts a template from the
key-deliverability check.

budget_mode.description:
`enforce` | `alert_only` — gateway keys only, meaningful when a budget is
set.

daily_budget.description:
Per-key daily budget in the tenant's accounting currency (`null` = no
per-key daily cap; always `null` for automation keys, which carry no
budget).

daily_spent.description:
Current fleet-estimate spend, in the tenant's accounting currency,
against this key's per-key budget in
the active daily / monthly windows. Filled from `usage_counters`, not a
stored column; `0` when the key carries no budget.

key_prefix.description: Masked display of key hash prefix.

kind.description:
`sk` (gateway) | `vk` (gateway BYOK) | `ak_admin` (admin control plane)
| `ak_portal` (portal control plane). The single discriminator — BYOK is
`kind == "vk"`, not a separate flag.

monthly_budget.description:
Per-key monthly budget in the tenant's accounting currency (`null` = no
per-key monthly cap).

qos_class_elevated.description:
Whether that class is more important than the workspace's — granted by
a tenant admin. `null` for automation keys.

qos_class_id.description:
The key's own priority class under load (`null` = the workspace's
class; always `null` for automation keys, which carry none).

user_id.description: The owning principal (a human user or a service account).

KeySpec.description:
The gateway key a render embeds. Exactly one mode: mint a fresh key
(`name` or `name_prefix` auto-suffix), reuse an existing one
(`reuse_key_id`), or render against a key the caller holds out-of-band
(`external`). In reuse/external mode the snippet still renders the api-key
placeholder (the gateway keeps only the hash, so the plaintext can't be
recovered) and the caller splices the value it saved at creation time.

expires_at.description: Expiry for a freshly-minted key. Ignored when `reuse_key_id` is set.

external.description:
The caller already holds a gateway key out-of-band and splices it
itself (the CLI's `STREAMSCOPE_GATEWAY_KEY` escape hatch): nothing is
minted or reused, templates render with the api-key sentinel, and
`forward_auth` must state the key's mode (it decides the URL shape).
Mutually exclusive with every other field.

forward_auth.description:
`true` mints a `vk-` BYOK forward-auth key (the client forwards its own
upstream credential via `/fwd/{key}/...`). Ignored when `reuse_key_id`
is set — the reused key's own mode is used.

name.description:
Name for a freshly-minted key. `None` (and no `reuse_key_id`) → the
backend derives the next free `<name_prefix>` / `<name_prefix>-N` name.
Mutually exclusive with `name_prefix` and `reuse_key_id`.

name_prefix.description:
Prefix for a backend-derived name (next free `<prefix>` /
`<prefix>-N`) instead of the default derived from the selected
client(s) — the CLI's CI mode mints under `ci`. Mutually exclusive
with `name` and `reuse_key_id`.

reuse_key_id.description:
Reuse this existing key instead of minting. Mutually exclusive with
`name`. The key must belong to the caller and be bound to `workspace_id`.

oneOf.description:
What this key spent over the window, and in which currency. `null`
when the window straddles a change of the tenant's accounting currency
— the rows are then in different denominations and no single figure
states them.

KnownServerToolType.description:
One known native server-tool wire tag — surfaced through the admin API so
the UI's `server_type` autocomplete tracks the canonical Rust source of
truth instead of a hard-coded copy. Operators can still author profiles
for unlisted providers; this is a suggestion list, not a closed set.

label.description: Human-readable provider name for UI display.

server_type.description:
The wire-protocol tag stamped on `DomainTool.server_type` for this
native server-tool.

LimitBucket.description:
Which limit refused a request — the typed `bucket` of a 429 and of its
audit row. Clients and the UI branch on this, never on the message text.

LimitLayer.description: One bucket of the effective-limit stack.

binding.description:
This is the layer that will stop the member first (at most one layer
of a stack — two key layers share a bucket, so the bucket alone cannot
say which).

budget_mode.description: `enforce` | `alert_only` — how this layer's budgets act at the cap.

key_id.description:
The key this layer is — set on a `key` layer only, with its name and
its prefix (what names an unnamed key).

source.description:
Where this layer's limits come from: `own` (set on this scope),
`tenant_default` (a workspace whose every cap is the tenant default
budget), `member_default` (the workspace's default member limit),
`exception` (the member's own exception, replacing the default). A
layer mixing its own caps with its default's is `own` / `exception`,
and each metric's `inherited` says which caps are the default's.

LimitMeter.description:
One metric of one bucket: its cap (`None` = no cap) and the fleet-estimate
use in the current window.

inherited.description:
The cap is not set on this scope but taken from its default: the
tenant default budget on a `workspace` layer, the workspace's default
member limit on a `member` layer. Never true without a cap.

used.description:
Use in the current window; null where the viewer may not see it —
another person's spend (the viewer rules are `StackViewer`'s).

LinkedSessions.description: Response for GET /sessions/{id}/linked — returns parent + children.

tenant_slug.description: Tenant slug (default: "system"). Routes login to the correct tenant.

changelog_pending.description: True when the admin has not yet seen the changelog for the current version.

value.description:
String for `glob` / `regex` / `equals`; array of strings for
`contains_any` / `contains_word_any` / `in`.

McpAuditLogEntry.description:
MCP-side audit row exposed at `/audit?kind=mcp`. Per-call shape with the
joined virtual-server slug + user email + protocol_version so the audit
UI can render rows without an extra fan-out fetch. Operators correlate
across calls in the same JSON-RPC session by pasting `mcp_session_id`
into the audit list `search` box (substring match).

app_id.description:
Three-tier app id resolved by `extract_attribution` from `X-App-Id` /
`Referer` / `User-Agent` (mirrors LLM rows). `None` when no pattern
matched. Stored on `gateway_audit.app_id`.

badges.description:
Typed audit badges — same `AuditBadge` enum as LLM rows. Codes are
append-only; UI consumer is the shared `BADGE_REGISTRY`. DB column
is `NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` so this is always present.

mcp_session_id.description:
Raw `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the call. Distinct from
`session_id` above (which is hashed).

params.description:
JSON-RPC `params` payload as the agent sent it (for `tools/call`
this is the `{name, arguments}` envelope; for `resources/read` the
`{uri}`; for `prompts/get` the `{name, arguments}`). Mirrors the
LLM trace's `messages` field — surfaced so the audit drawer + the
session-view MCP bubble can render the actual request body
without an extra fetch.

protocol_version.description:
MCP protocol version negotiated at `initialize` and pinned for the
remainder of the session. `None` for the rare row that lands before
`initialize` completes (`mcp_sessions.protocol_version` defaults to
`"unknown"`).

result.description:
JSON-RPC `result` payload returned by the upstream (success path
only — error responses populate `error_code` / `error_message`).

session_id.description:
Hashed session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — same shape the
LLM `AuditLogEntry` carries. Cross-protocol correlation pivots on
this when an MCP `sampling/createMessage` was intercepted by the
gateway and answered through the LLM pipeline (the synthetic
`llm_audit` row shares this id).

oneOf.description:
Typed diff payload stamped by the MCP policy engine + multiplex pump.
Each field corresponds to a key the proxy may stamp on a given row.
Empty struct (`{}`) when nothing fired.

McpAuthMode.description:
How the client authenticates with the MCP gateway. Drives the MCP step
of the wizard: `static` binds a workspace key into `Authorization: Bearer …`;
`spec_oauth` issues no key and lets the client run the MCP-spec OAuth 2.1
dance against the gateway on first use.

McpCatalogEntry.description: A catalog entry as returned to the admin UI.

McpCatalogToolSchema.description:
OpenAPI projection of the JSONB `tools` element (the row type uses the
`sqlx::types::Json` wrapper, which isn't itself `ToSchema`).

McpDashboardPanel.description:
Wrapper response for the dashboard panels. `total_calls` lets the UI
render "N of M" alongside the top-K list without a second round trip.

live_tokens.description:
Snapshot count of MCP-surface `oauth_issued_tokens WHERE revoked_at IS
NULL AND expires_at > NOW()`. Not period-scoped — always "right now".

previous.description: Same metrics for the prior equivalent period (for delta UI).

unique_users.description: Distinct users with at least one call in the period.

top_error_code.description:
Most common JSON-RPC `error_code` for this method, when one exists.
Null when all errors came from the HTTP path (`g.status_code >= 400`)
without a JSON-RPC error code.

McpInvocationCount.description: One row in a top-N MCP dashboard panel.

error_count.description:
Calls that returned a JSON-RPC error (`mcp_audit.error_code IS NOT NULL`)
or HTTP 4xx/5xx (`gateway_audit.status_code >= 400`). Either side counts.

key.description:
Pivot value: `tool_id`, `prompt_id`, `resource_uri`, or a UUID/string
identifier (virtual_server_id, upstream_server_id, user_id, app_id).
Always cast to TEXT server-side so the UI can resolve display names.

p95_latency_ms.description:
P95 of `gateway_audit.latency_total_ms` for this group. Null when the
group has no rows with non-null latency.

user_count.description: Distinct users who invoked it. Always 1 when pivot is `g.user_id`.

user_email.description:
User email when pivot is `g.user_id` and the user has one on file.
Lets the UI build a `?user_email=…` deep-link that audit / sessions
match exactly, instead of relying on the rendered display-name `key`.

user_id.description:
User UUID when pivot is `g.user_id`. Fallback identifier the UI uses
when `user_email` is absent — pairs with `AuditQuery::user_id` /
`SessionListQuery::user_id` so deep-links still resolve for users
without an email on file.

virtual_server_count.description:
Distinct virtual servers that hosted this pivot value. Always 1 when
pivot is `virtual_server_id`.

McpPolicyClassification.description:
Mirrors `streamscope_core::config::tool_rules::RiskResult` as the proxy's MCP
audit writer stamps it into `transform_diff.policy_classification`.

rule_id.description:
Id of the rule that fired. `None` when no rule fired but the action is
non-allow.

token.description:
The token to revoke — either an access token or a refresh token. A
refresh token takes its paired access token down with it.

McpRouteFilterShape.description:
Allow/deny list filter applied per-route to tools / resources / prompts
surfaced from an upstream. JSONB-backed; both fields optional, mutually
exclusive in practice (allow wins if both are set). Storage uses
`sqlx::types::Json<McpRouteFilterShape>` so the wire schema, the OpenAPI
projection, and the row type are all the same struct — no opaque
`serde_json::Value` newtype on the public surface.

McpSamplingInterceptOutcome.description:
Mirrors `streamscope_core::audit::mcp::SamplingInterceptOutcome` for wire
transport. Two shapes:

- `Served` — synthetic LLM call succeeded; the linked llm_audit row
  carries the actual cost + token counts. Includes the resolved upstream
  model and the loopback latency for at-a-glance triage.
- `Failed` — interception attempted but could not be served (auth
  rejection, budget exceeded, capability mismatch). Reason is a stable
  short string for UI dispatch.

stream_bytes.description:
Total bytes streamed from upstream during the call. Wire shape is the
proxy's `usize` → JSON number; we deserialize as `i64` to leave
headroom past the current 8 MiB `MCP_STREAM_MAX_BYTES` cap.

by_method.description: Calls per JSON-RPC method in this bucket (e.g. `{"tools/call": 42}`).

upstream_p50_ms.description:
Upstream-only latency percentiles (`mcp_audit.upstream_latency_ms`).
Gap between gateway and upstream P95 = proxy overhead.

interval.description: Bucket interval: `"hour"` when the window ≤ 1 day, else `"day"`.

McpTransformDiff.description:
Typed shape of `mcp_audit.transform_diff`. The MCP proxy stamps a finite
set of well-known keys — surfacing them as named optional fields keeps the
admin UI off untyped JSONB grovel and lets `openapi-typescript` generate
strict TS types. Adding a key here requires bumping the proxy and the UI
in lockstep; the keys are append-only.

oneOf.description: Stamped on rows that represent a `notifications/elicitation/complete`.

Stamped on rows that represent a `notifications/{tools,resources,prompts}/list_changed`
passthrough.

Stamped on rows that represent a server-initiated round-trip (the
agent's reply to an upstream `sampling/createMessage` or
`elicitation/create`). The `method` is the upstream's request method;
`rpc_id` is opaque (JSON-RPC id can be string / number / null).

Per-call multiplex summary for streaming `tools/call` / `prompts/get`.
Counters are non-zero only when the upstream emitted SSE events of
the corresponding kind during the call.

Set when the unified policy engine fired a rule on this RPC. Mirrors
`streamscope_core::config::tool_rules::RiskResult` — same shape used by the
LLM tool-policy path so the UI banner is shared.

Stamped on `mcp_audit` rows for `sampling/createMessage` calls that
were intercepted by the gateway. The matching `llm_audit` row is
linked by shared `gateway_audit.session_id`.

transport.description:
`"sse"` when the upstream still uses the legacy `text/event-stream`
GET transport instead of Streamable HTTP. Operator-visible signal.

built_in.description:
`true` for synthetic gateway-managed rows (e.g. `builtin-web` for the
built-in web-search virtual server). The admin UI surfaces a
`<SystemRowBadge>` and disables Edit/Delete for these — operators
configure them through the matching settings tab, not the upstream
CRUD form.

has_credential.description:
Presence-only signal. `true` iff `encrypted_credential`
IS NOT NULL on the underlying row. The plaintext is never echoed.

has_oauth_client_secret.description:
Presence-only signal for the encrypted client secret. `true` iff the
underlying row has a non-NULL `encrypted_oauth_client_secret`.

has_session.description: True when a `mcp_user_credentials` row exists for this (user, upstream).

last_used_at.description: Bumped on each successful upstream call. Null when never used or not connected.

scope.description: Granted OAuth scope (space-separated). Null when not connected.

display_title.description:
MCP 2025-11-25 `serverInfo.title` — display-friendly variant of
`name`. Clients show this in their UI; when null, falls back to
`name`. Surfaced in the `initialize` response.

oauth_enabled.description:
When true, the proxy advertises spec-compliant OAuth on this
virtual server. Unauthenticated requests return RFC 9728-compliant
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` headers, and
proxy-issued JWT bearers (audience-bound to the slug) are accepted.

oauth_incomplete.description:
`true` when this endpoint routes a `per_user_oauth` upstream whose
shared OAuth-App client is incomplete (missing client_id, secret,
authorization_url, or token_url). Such an endpoint can't be granted to
a workspace or connected from the portal until the client is set, so
the admin UI marks it not-grantable. Required-field set mirrors
`oauth_client_missing_fields` / `ensure_endpoint_oauth_grantable`.

sampling_credential_set.description:
Presence-only signal. `true` iff `sampling_credential` is set in DB.
The plaintext bearer is never returned over the wire.

sampling_intercept_enabled.description:
When true, server-initiated `sampling/createMessage` calls on this
virtual server are intercepted by the gateway and answered through
the standard LLM pipeline instead of being forwarded to the agent.

sampling_model_alias.description:
Model alias the synthetic LLM call requests (e.g. `claude-default`).
`None` when not yet configured.

website_url.description:
MCP 2025-11-25 `serverInfo.websiteUrl` — optional URL the client
may surface to users (e.g. linking to the product's docs).

appliance.description:
True when this deployment is the Kairos VM appliance (the host daemon is
configured) — gates the super-admin Appliance surface in the UI. Always
false on Kubernetes / dev.

MeResponse.description: Response for /auth/me — includes optional JWT when using header auth.

MediaAnalyticsResponse.description:
Direction-aware media analytics: each media type has sub-directions
(e.g. image has generation=text→image and vision=image→text).

users.description: Top users with per-type request counts

total_refs.description: References to stored blobs from live audit rows.

oneOf.description:
What this direction cost, and in which currency. `null` when the
window straddles a change of the tenant's accounting currency.

MediaUserStat.description:
One user of the media spend ranking, ordered by the shared spend rule
(see `TopUserEntry`).

oneOf.description:
`null` when this user's window straddles a change of the accounting
currency.

MemberLimitDefaults.description:
The default limit applied to every member of a workspace, one field per
metric. `null` = no default for that metric (members are limited only by
the workspace pool); a positive value applies to each member separately. A
member exception replaces it per metric.

context_window.description: The context window this endpoint reported for the model.

identity.description: What the engine says it serves under this name (vLLM `root`).

model_missing_reports.description:
The endpoint answered "model not found" for this model since its last
discovery answer: this many reports, the last at `model_missing_at`.

cells.description: One cell per endpoint, in the endpoint order of the response.

context_window.description: The window the gateway advertises: the smallest any member reported.

identity_mismatch.description:
Members report different identities — possibly different weights under
one name; the operator decides.

parent.description: The base model when this is an adapter (vLLM `parent`).

MembershipState.description: One cell of the membership matrix.

MessageContent.description: A conversation message, keyed by its content hash within the tenant.

message.description: One conversation message in its client protocol's wire shape.

oneOf.description:
Optional per-key budget ceiling (omitted ⇒ no per-key cap). A manager may
cap the keys they provision for a member.

downstream_provider_id.description:
Optional BYOK downstream binding for a `vk-` key (LLM pass-through). Must
be a `byok` downstream granted to this workspace; ignored for a standard
key. Mirrors the self-service key path.

forward_auth.description: When true, mint a `vk-` BYOK (forward-auth) key.

qos_class_id.description:
The key's priority class under load. Omitted takes the workspace's own
default for a person's tool; a class more important than the workspace's
is refused — a manager cannot hand out what the workspace does not have.

oneOf.description: Optional per-key budget (gateway keys only).

forward_auth.description: When `type=gateway` and true, mint a `vk-` BYOK key; else `sk-`.

workspace_id.description: Required when `type=gateway`: the workspace the key binds to.

api_base_url.description:
Admin/portal `ak-` scripting origin (`api_public_url`) — the FQDN the
admin-API is served on, which the reveal-once example targets. `None`
for gateway keys or when the API origin isn't configured (the UI then
falls back to the console origin, correct for co-resident installs).

key.description: The plaintext key — returned ONCE, never again.

proxy_base_url.description: Gateway BYOK (`vk-`) connection origin; `None` for admin/portal keys.

api_base_url.description:
Portal `ak-` scripting origin (`api_public_url`) — the FQDN the
admin-API is served on, which the reveal-once example targets. `None`
when the API origin isn't configured (the UI then falls back to the
console origin, correct for co-resident installs).

key.description: The plaintext `ak-` key — returned ONCE, never again.

MintedKey.description:
A key created during a render — surfaced so the UI can show the resolved
(auto-suffixed) name and refresh `/portal/keys` without a round-trip.

api_key.description:
Plaintext gateway key when this render minted one. Substituted into the
clipboard at copy-time only. `None` when the render reused an existing
key (or the template mints nothing, e.g. spec-OAuth MCP).

catalog_model_id.description: Explicit catalog link (NULL = auto-match by canonical name).

healing_enabled.description: Per-model self-healing override (NULL = inherit the tenant `healing_enabled`).

oneOf.description: Stored price override (null = inherit the catalog's map whole).

resolved_catalog_model_id.description: Catalog entry actually used to resolve this model (link or auto-match).

resolved_rates.description:
Price actually in force: this model's own map, else the map of the
catalog row for the SAME provider, else empty (no price known).

sources.description: Per-field provenance of the resolved value, keyed by field name.

user_overridden_fields.description: Fields the operator has explicitly pinned (caps + pricing + token limits).

endpoints.description: What each enabled endpoint answered, primary first.

unattended_refuses.description:
"Sync now" would not make some of `removed`, or would refuse the sync
whole: it judges an answer implausibly short (under half of what the
server, or the endpoint, listed before). The review still offers them — a server
can really shrink — and this says to check the server is fully up
before accepting them.

MutationResult.description: Returned after a destructive operation — how many keys were revoked.

Nack.description:
A body the edge refused to apply. The admin does not send that digest to
this instance again; a later body for the resource is sent as usual.

Normalizer.description:
Hardcoded normaliser kinds. Adding one requires a new variant here and a
new arm in [`apply_forms`], and an entry in [`Normalizer::ALL`]; the
console's two normaliser lists (the profile editor's picker and the
Field Profiles filter) are kept by hand beside it.

NotificationItem.description: One notification row for the feed.

redirect_uris.description:
Always returned as a JSON array of strings. Empty arrays are rejected
at write time, but a corrupted DB row could surface as `null` — the
handler treats that as `[]` for forward compat.

OauthErrorCode.description:
The `error` values this authorization server emits.

A subset of what RFC 6749 §5.2, RFC 8628 §3.5 and RFC 7591 §3.2.2 define —
the codes for conditions we can actually reach. The vocabulary is the RFCs',
not ours, so widening it is adding a variant, never inventing a value: a code
outside the specified set is one no client is required to understand.

oneOf.description: The gateway's server-derived OAuth redirect/callback URI (copyable).
The gateway's public homepage URL (copyable).
A fixed suggested value, e.g. an app name (copyable).
A non-copyable instruction, e.g. "leave unchecked".

OauthFieldValue.description:
How a provider-form field's value is produced when the OAuth-setup guide
renders. `redirect`/`homepage` are resolved client-side from tenant settings
(they can't be baked into a static seed); `literal`/`note` carry their text.

OauthProviderField.description: One row in a provider's OAuth-app registration form.

hint.description: Optional short clarifier shown under the field.

label.description: The label the provider's console uses for this field.

OauthProviderRecipe.description:
A provider-specific recipe for hand-registering a per-user-OAuth MCP
upstream: which console to open, the fields it asks for and the value to
paste into each, ordered steps, and suggested scopes. Static help content
shipped in `seeds/mcp_servers/oauth_provider_recipes.json`.

console_url.description: Deep link to the provider page that creates an OAuth app.

host_patterns.description:
Hostname needles matched (as suffixes) against the upstream/issuer host
to auto-detect the provider. Empty for the generic fallback recipe.

supports_dcr.description:
Whether the provider advertises RFC 7591 dynamic client registration
(i.e. whether "Register client automatically" is expected to work).

OauthProviderRecipesResponse.description: Static per-provider OAuth-setup guides for the upstream-server modal.

OffsetPage_AdminAuditRow.description:
Default pagination shape — no `total`, cheap on partitioned/hot tables.
Handlers select `limit + 1` rows; `has_more` is `true` when the extra row existed.

items.description: One row in `GET /api/v1/admin/admin-audit`.

actor_key_id.description:
The `ak-` key id when `actor_kind='admin_key'`; `null` for humans.
Answers "which automation did this?" independently of the owning account.

change_diff.description:
Structured before/after snapshot stamped by handlers that pre-load
the row they're about to mutate. Shape: `{ "before": <row>, "after":
<row> }`, or `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n> }` when it was too
large to keep. NULL for handlers that haven't opted in (most creates /
deletes) or when nothing actually changed.

request_body.description:
Redacted request body. `null` when the inbound body was empty or
non-JSON. The middleware redacts known secret-shaped keys (password,
api_key, token, …) before insert.

response_error.description:
Typed error body (`{code, message}`) the handler returned on a non-2xx
status. NULL on success. Lets the log show WHY a call failed, not just
its status_code.

scan_cut.description:
`true` when a text search stopped at its scan budget before it could
fill the page: more matches may exist past what was scanned, and
`has_more` says nothing about them — narrow the window or the term.
Always `false` for a list without a search.

OffsetPage_AuditLogRow.description:
Default pagination shape — no `total`, cheap on partitioned/hot tables.
Handlers select `limit + 1` rows; `has_more` is `true` when the extra row existed.

badges.description:
Typed audit badges (`streamscope_core::audit::AuditBadge`, codes
append-only): the LLM row's own, plus a `session_alert` read from its session's
current alert (the agent writes the alert on the session, never on the
audit row).

billed_units.description:
Per-unit decomposition of `cost`: what was charged for each thing the
request consumed. Counts are what was CHARGED — a provider's reported
count less anything that partitions out of it, each of which carries its
own line — so the lines sum to `cost` less `embedding_cost`.

catchall_path.description:
Path/method of the catch-all hit (only populated when the request fell
to the catch-all handler).

chat_media_summary.description:
Extracted media references for chat requests. Typed shape mirrors
`streamscope_core::audit::ChatMediaSummaryEntry`.

client_ip.description:
Forwarded end-client identity, present only for Inline AI traffic where a
trusted inline key relayed it (`X-Client-IP` / `X-Authenticated-User` /
`X-Authenticated-Groups`). Absent/empty for direct clients.

conversation_session_id.description:
Content-derived conversation id from `conversation_turns.session_id`.
`None` when no `conversation_turns` row exists for this request
(MCP/web audit rows, LLM rows captured before content
logging was on). Use this — not `session_id` — for any UI link to
`/sessions/{id}`.

cost.description:
The row's total, in `cost_currency` — the tenant's accounting currency
as it was when the row was written, not as it is now. Stamped per row so
changing the setting cannot restate spend that was already reported.

embedding_cost.description:
Portion of `cost` spent on the response cache's own embedding call,
with the tokens it consumed. Non-zero only on a Semantic-cached alias.
Present so the row's total still decomposes: without it `cost`
exceeds the completion's own cost with nothing to explain the gap.

endpoint_url.description:
The replica endpoint of the server that answered, as its URL was when
it did. Null on a row with no upstream call, or from a release before
endpoints.

latency_total_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the moment the gateway started forwarding — after its
own checks and transforms — to the end of the answer: any hold for
capacity (`queue_wait_ms`) and any earlier attempt it moved on from
included.

latency_ttft_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the moment the gateway started forwarding — after its
own checks and transforms — to the first token: any hold for capacity
(`queue_wait_ms`) and any earlier attempt it moved on from included.

limit_bucket.description:
On a limit refusal: which limit refused it — `organisation`,
`workspace`, `member` or `key`. The UI explains a refusal from this.

oneOf.description:
Canonical media RPC shape — source of truth for embeddings / audio /
images / video endpoint turns. `None` for chat/text routes.

pipeline_path.description:
Internal pipeline-path tag (`fastpath` | `buffered`). Analytics-only,
not user-facing.

qos_class_id.description:
The QoS class the request ran as. The name is resolved by the reader
against the tenant's class list — an audit row must not hold a class
back from being renamed or deleted.

queue_wait_ms.description:
Milliseconds the request waited for upstream capacity before it was
dispatched. Part of `latency_ttft_ms` and `latency_total_ms`: the time
the upstream that answered took is the latency less this and less any
earlier attempt it moved on from.

session_id.description:
Raw client-facing session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — the
hashed X-Session-Id value used for cross-stream correlation in the
session detection layer. This is NOT the conversation id used by
the session-detail UI: that's the separate content-derived
`conversation_session_id` below, populated only when there's an
LLM turn linked via `conversation_turns.session_id`. UI callers
building "View Session" links MUST use `conversation_session_id`,
not this field — the two diverge for any session that didn't go
through the LLM pipeline (MCP-only, web-only, etc).

source_cost.description:
What the provider charges, in the currency it quotes, and the multiplier
that took one to the other. Equal to `cost` with an `fx_rate` of 1 when
the model is priced in the accounting currency.

oneOf.description:
Transform diff captured on `conversation_turns` — mirrors the shape in
`GET /api/v1/admin/traces/{request_id}`. Present when the request had
transforms applied with `capture_diffs` enabled. `None` otherwise (e.g.,
media requests, non-text requests, or transforms without diff capture).

allOf.description:
MCP-side audit row exposed at `/audit?kind=mcp`. Per-call shape with the
joined virtual-server slug + user email + protocol_version so the audit
UI can render rows without an extra fan-out fetch. Operators correlate
across calls in the same JSON-RPC session by pasting `mcp_session_id`
into the audit list `search` box (substring match).

app_id.description:
Three-tier app id resolved by `extract_attribution` from `X-App-Id` /
`Referer` / `User-Agent` (mirrors LLM rows). `None` when no pattern
matched. Stored on `gateway_audit.app_id`.

badges.description:
Typed audit badges — same `AuditBadge` enum as LLM rows. Codes are
append-only; UI consumer is the shared `BADGE_REGISTRY`. DB column
is `NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` so this is always present.

mcp_session_id.description:
Raw `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the call. Distinct from
`session_id` above (which is hashed).

params.description:
JSON-RPC `params` payload as the agent sent it (for `tools/call`
this is the `{name, arguments}` envelope; for `resources/read` the
`{uri}`; for `prompts/get` the `{name, arguments}`). Mirrors the
LLM trace's `messages` field — surfaced so the audit drawer + the
session-view MCP bubble can render the actual request body
without an extra fetch.

protocol_version.description:
MCP protocol version negotiated at `initialize` and pinned for the
remainder of the session. `None` for the rare row that lands before
`initialize` completes (`mcp_sessions.protocol_version` defaults to
`"unknown"`).

result.description:
JSON-RPC `result` payload returned by the upstream (success path
only — error responses populate `error_code` / `error_message`).

session_id.description:
Hashed session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — same shape the
LLM `AuditLogEntry` carries. Cross-protocol correlation pivots on
this when an MCP `sampling/createMessage` was intercepted by the
gateway and answered through the LLM pipeline (the synthetic
`llm_audit` row shares this id).

oneOf.description:
Typed diff payload stamped by the MCP policy engine + multiplex pump.
Each field corresponds to a key the proxy may stamp on a given row.
Empty struct (`{}`) when nothing fired.

survives the account), and counting users would silently drop exactly

items.description:
One `ssai login` — the machine, not the token.

A login is a **chain** of token rows: each pair is access + refresh, and
every refresh rotation retires the pair and mints another onto the same
chain. This row aggregates one chain, which is why its id is the chain and
not a jti — the operator revokes a machine, and the tokens are an
implementation detail of how that machine holds its access.

device_name.description:
Self-reported by the CLI at login (device-grant logins name the host).
Absent for a login that reported none — never treat it as an identifier.

expires_at.description: How long the machine can keep refreshing before it must sign in again.

id.description: The login chain. Also the revoke handle.

last_used_at.description:
When the machine last called, across the whole chain — a rotation mints
a new generation, but the last call belongs to the machine rather than
to whichever generation was holding its access at the time.

`None` means it has not called yet. It is stamped at
roughly one write a minute, so read it as "active around then", never
as an exact last-request time.

revoked_at.description:
When the machine was deliberately cut off — by an operator here, or by
its own `ssai logout`. Read from the chain's NEWEST generation,
never from "some row is revoked": rotation revokes the generation it
replaces, so the latter would report every rotated-then-expired chain as
revoked, stamped with the time of a rotation.

signed_in_at.description:
When the machine signed in, from the oldest generation still on record.
The sweeper eventually purges long-expired generations, so on a chain
older than the retention window this walks forward rather than pinning
the original login.

items.description:
Maps a raw `(tool_name, app_id|mcp_server)` to a canonical `tool_id`,
and per-arg `field` to the wire field + normaliser. Operators register
these per-client so a single rule (`tool_id = read_file`,
`arg.path glob /etc/*`) catches every client's variant of the same
conceptual tool, and so obfuscation tricks (whitespace, percent-encoding,
case) are defeated by the normaliser before matching.

Disambiguation: `server_type`, `mcp_server`, and `app_filter` are mutually
exclusive on a given profile. A profile sets exactly one (or none, for a
generic fallback). Lookup precedence is:
  1. `server_type` matches an inbound `DomainTool.server_type` (Anthropic
     `web_search_20250305`, OpenAI Responses `web_search_preview`, Gemini
     `google_search`, …)
  2. `mcp_server` matches the parsed MCP namespace
  3. `app_filter` matches the request's app_id
  4. Generic (none set)

Then by `priority` ASC, then by load position.

app_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the request's `app_id`. Mutually
exclusive with `mcp_server` — a profile is either app-scoped or
MCP-server-scoped, never both.

description.description: Human-readable description ("Claude Code Bash tool — shell command").

field.description:
Canonical arg field name (e.g. `command`, `url`, `path`). Rules
reference this in `arg.<field>` conditions. The engine maps this to
`wire_field` (or `field` when `wire_field` is unset) when fetching
the value from `arguments`.

id.description:
Stable operator-visible identifier (e.g. `TFP-claude-Bash-command`).
Surfaces in the discovery/registration UI and audit-style logs so
reviewers can trace why a field was canonicalised a specific way.

is_builtin.description:
Server-managed: `true` on initial seed, `false` after the first PATCH/PUT.
Mirrors [`Rule::is_builtin`]. Ignored on incoming client payloads.

mcp_server.description:
Optional MCP server identifier. When set, this profile only matches
when the wire tool name is `mcp__<server>__<local>` and `<server>`
equals (case-insensitively) this value, OR when the engine was given
an out-of-band `mcp_server` hint matching this value.

normalizer.description:
Which normaliser to apply. Hardcoded set; unknown values fail
deserialisation.

priority.description:
Lower wins on overlapping `(tool_pattern, field)` matches. Default 100.
Stable-sorted with array position as the tiebreaker so manual order
still controls equal-priority entries.

server_type.description:
Optional server-side server-tool discriminator. When set, this
profile matches only when the inbound `DomainTool.server_type`
equals this value (case-insensitively) — covers Anthropic
`web_search_20250305`, OpenAI Responses `web_search_preview`,
Gemini `google_search`, and any future native server-tool. The
`ServerType` precedence tier outranks `mcp_server`, `app_filter`,
and generic; consult `lookup_with_server_type` /
`resolve_tool_id_for_definition` to drive the lookup with a
`server_type` hint.

source.description:
Provenance tag, e.g. `"claude-code:builtin"`, `"mcp-registry:filesystem@1.0"`.
Display-only — the engine doesn't read it.

tool_id.description:
Canonical concept identifier (e.g. `shell_exec`, `read_file`). Rules
pivot on this id rather than tool-name globs. Free-form string —
`tool_ids.json` is documentation, not an enforced enum.

tool_pattern.description:
Pipe-separated case-insensitive glob over tool names. Same syntax as
`Rule.match[].value` for `glob` conditions. For MCP-namespaced tools
(`mcp__<server>__<tool>`), this matches the unprefixed local name —
`mcp_server` carries the server identity separately.

wire_field.description:
Optional actual arg key on the wire. Defaults to `field` when null.
Use this when the client emits a different name than the canonical:
`field: "path"`, `wire_field: "target_file"` for Cursor, etc.

a2a_agent_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the A2A upstream agent's slug
(`a2a_upstream_agents.slug`, e.g. `research-prod`, `partner-*`). The
agent is the pivot of the `agent_calls` scope the way the upstream is
the pivot of MCP rules. Non-A2A traffic never matches a rule with this
filter set; `None` means "any agent".

Optional pipe-separated glob over the request's `app_id` (client
identity, e.g. `claude-code`, `cursor-*`). When set, the rule only
fires for matching apps. `None` means "any app".

enabled.description: Inert when false; preserved in storage. `extract_for` skips disabled rules.

forked_from.description:
Copy-on-write link: when set on a `Some(P)` rule, this is a per-profile
**fork** of the shared rule with this id — it *suppresses* that shared rule
inside P (an override). Deleting the fork reverts P to the shared rule.

id.description:
Stable operator-visible identifier (e.g. `ASI02-06`). Surfaces on
blocked-tool banners and transform diffs so reviewers know which rule
fired without parsing the description. Every rule carries one: a seed

match.description: AND-of-conditions. Empty means "every item in scope" (catch-all).

"any upstream". Non-MCP traffic (LLM tool calls without an MCP
namespace) never matches a rule with this filter set — pairs
naturally with `(request, resource_reads | prompt_invocations)`
rules. Use this to keep per-upstream policies (and per-test rules)
from spilling onto other servers in the same tenant.

priority.description:

profile_id.description:

baseline; builtins live here). `Some(P)` → **specific** to profile P. The
