OidcExchangeRequest.description: Request body for the internal OIDC exchange.

enabled.description:
Take the endpoint out of traffic (false) or put it back (true). The last
enabled endpoint of a server cannot be disabled.

force.description: Skip the reachability probe of a new URL.

max_in_flight.description:
This replica's own capacity, overriding its server's. Present and
`null` goes back to the server's value; absent leaves it unchanged.
Replicas of one server are rarely identical machines, which is why the
override exists at all.

url.description:
A new base URL. The endpoint then starts over as never answered: it is
assumed to serve every model until discovery answers from the new host.

PatchServerRequest.description:
A partial update to one upstream server.

Every field is optional and an omitted one keeps whatever is stored.

The two nullable columns are three-state: absent = unchanged, `null` (or an
empty string) = cleared, falling back to the provider default, a value = set.
On every other field a blank value is refused — see [`require_non_blank`].

adaptive_concurrency.description:
Learn each endpoint's in-flight limit from its engine's readings (or
stop). Refused while the server or any endpoint of it declares a
waiting-queue bound: the learned limit replaces that bound.

oneOf.description:
The learned limit's token-latency target: `auto`, `off`, or `fixed`
with `ms` from 1 to 60 000. Absent leaves it unchanged. Kept while the
limit is fixed, and applied whenever it is learned.

api_key.description:
New credential. Absent or empty keeps the stored one — there is no way to
read a credential back, so it can never be round-tripped by a caller
echoing the current server.

chat_endpoint_path.description:
New chat-endpoint-path override. Explicit `null` clears it back to the
provider default.

clear_endpoint_bounds.description:
Also clear every endpoint's own `max_in_flight` / `waiting_threshold`
— disabled endpoints included, since enabling one would otherwise bring
its bound back — in the same transaction as the server's scheduling
fields. What a switch to a mode that holds nothing needs: an endpoint's
bound gates on its own, whatever the server says.

enabled.description:
Turn the server on or off. A disabled server is not sent to the
gateways: its routes serve nothing, and a pass-through (BYOK) provider
linked to it reaches nothing. The built-in pass-through servers are
seeded off.

engine_metrics.description: Read this server's engines' own metrics for the dashboards (or stop).

force.description: Skip the write-time liveness probe. Absent = probe, as on create.

max_in_flight.description:
Capacity the gateway may use at each endpoint of this server. Present
and `null` clears the knob (unbounded); absent leaves it unchanged.

scheduling_dialect.description:
How this engine expresses a priority class: `none` or `vllm_priority`.
An explicit opt-in, because it has to match how the engine was started.

upstream_url.description:
New URL of the primary endpoint. Explicit `null` clears it back to the
provider default.

PiiSettings.description:
Per-tenant configuration for the in-process PII detector. Lives under
`system_settings.guardrail.pii`; synced through the same config-sync path as
the rest of [`GuardrailSettings`]. Defaults to **observe** on the inbound
request — like the injection classifier, detection is on out of the box, but
observe mode only badges/audits and never mutates content (enforce and
response scanning are the opt-ins).

Unlike the injection classifier, the PII detector is purely in-process, so it
has no transport / endpoint / timeout and cannot "fail" as a unit — a
recognizer-script error fails safe per-candidate (the candidate is dropped).

enabled.description: Master toggle. Default **on** (observe) — like the injection classifier.

entities.description:
Entity types to detect. Defaults to all of [`PII_ENTITY_TYPES`]. An entity
not in this list is never flagged.

fail_mode.description:
Reserved for parity with the injection guardrail's fail-mode. The
in-process detector cannot fail as a unit (script errors fail safe
per-candidate), so this is currently unused; kept so the wire shape and
admin surface match the classifier's.

mode.description:
Observe (default) vs enforce. See [`GuardrailMode`]. Enforce masks each
finding in place (`[REDACTED:US_SSN]`).

redaction_placeholder.description:
Replacement for a masked finding in enforce mode. `{entity}` is
substituted with the entity type.

scan_request.description:
Scan the **inbound** request — the user's own latest message (P5: DLP
egress, stopping PII from leaving for the upstream model). Default **on**.

scan_response.description:
Scan the **model response** (P3: leakage — PII the model emitted). Opt-in
(the default-on observe covers the inbound request surface only).

threshold.description:
Score at or above which a finding surfaces. Native-validated entities
(card/SSN/IBAN) score high; pattern-only entities lean on a context
boost to clear this.

PiiSettingsUpdate.description: Partial update for the PII detector sub-block. All fields optional.

PlaceholderRef.description:
One placeholder an author may use in a template or companion body, with
the value save-time validation resolves it to.

item_keys.description: For a `list`, the keys available inside its `{{#each}}` block.

kind.description:
`string` | `bool` | `int` | `list` — a `list` is iterated with
`{{#each <name>}}`, and its per-item keys are in `item_keys`.

sample.description: Sample value, or `None` for a list.

used_pct.description: Percent of the persistent partition in use.

PortalAuditFilterOptions.description:
The audit filter options a member may pick from: configuration only, never
a scan of the traffic. Apps and QoS classes are the tenant's; MCP servers,
MCP upstreams and A2A agents are those the caller's workspaces are granted
(a portal `ak-` key: its one workspace).

a2a_agents.description: A2A agents by slug (the filter's key).

apps.description: Apps by `app_id` (the key an audit row records).

mcp_upstream_servers.description: Upstream servers reachable through those virtual servers, by id.

qos_classes.description: QoS classes by id, to name the class an audit row records.

actor_id.description:
Portal user (the `users` row) that performed the action. For a
`portal_key` actor this is the owning service account.

change_diff.description: `{ "before": <row>, "after": <row> }` for the resource the call changed, or `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n> }` when it was too large to keep; `null` when nothing was captured or nothing changed.

request_body.description: Redacted request body (secret-shaped keys removed); `null` when the body was empty or not JSON; `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n>, …identity fields }` when it was too large to keep.

response_error.description: The error body the call answered with (`{code, message}` for a current release, any stored JSON for an older one); `null` on success.

target_user_id.description:
The member a manager operated on (mint/revoke a key for someone else).
NULL for self-service mutations.

workspace_id.description:
Workspace the mutation acted within, when one was in scope (key
creation, quickstart render carry it). NULL otherwise.

pending_id.description: `mcp_pending_authorizations.id` — the portal can poll status by this id.

status.description:
One of: `connected` (credential present, not expired), `expired`
(credential present but `expires_at < now`), `not_connected` (no
credential row).

virtual_servers.description:
Virtual servers this upstream is reachable through (the agent calls
`/mcp/<slug>` per virtual server). Useful for the portal to show
"this connection unlocks tools on N virtual servers".

PortalFilterOption.description: One option of a member's audit filter: its id and display name.

PortalHome.description:
The portal Home: what needs doing, the caller's spend, their team (managers),
and their latest sessions.

expiring_keys.description:
The caller's unrevoked keys that expire within 7 days or expired in the
last 7 (at most 5): those still working first, soonest first — a key
about to stop is never pushed out by keys that already have. A key created to live 7 days or less
(a per-run CI key) is not one.

has_active_key.description: The caller holds at least one live (unrevoked, unexpired) key.

last_7_days.description: The caller's own LLM traffic over the last 7 days.

limit_warnings.description:
Budgets in the header workspace at 80 % of their cap or more, as the
caller may see them (a manager sees the pool's use, a member only when
the workspace shares it).

mcp_sign_in.description: MCP servers the caller may use that wait for their sign-in (at most 5).

oneOf.description: The header workspace's pool — answered to its managers only.

today.description: The caller's own LLM traffic since 00:00 UTC.

currency.description: The accounting currency the pool figures are in.

daily.description:
The pool's spend in the current UTC day and 30-day period, with its
caps (`null` = no cap).

daily_budget.description: Per-key budget ceiling (read-only here; settable by admin/manager only).

daily_spent.description:
Current fleet-estimate spend, in the tenant's accounting currency,
against this key's per-key budget in
the active daily / monthly windows. Filled from `usage_counters`, not a
stored column; `0` when the key carries no budget.

qos_class_id.description: The key's own priority class under load (`null` = the workspace's).

currency.description: The accounting currency `used` and `cap` are in.

key_name.description:
The key, on a `key` warning: its name, and the prefix that names it
when it has none.

tenant_slug.description:
The tenant these credentials belong to.

Required, and the only thing that decides which `users` row is
consulted. An email is unique within a tenant and nowhere else, so
without it a login can only guess — and a guess authenticates the
password against one tenant's hash while the caller believes it signed
in to another.

The organization the session is for. Under header auth the gateway
decides it, so the console follows this rather than its own URL.

PortalMcpBuiltinStatus.description:
Configuration summary for gateway-internal MCP upstreams (only built-in
upstreams populate this — regular HTTP upstreams leave it absent).

has_credential.description:
`true` iff an encrypted backend credential is stored on the
synthetic `builtin-web` row. False is non-fatal (some backends like
public SearXNG don't need one) but worth surfacing for operators.

PortalMcpSignInNeeded.description: A virtual server waiting for the caller's sign-in.

total_tools.description: Aggregated tool count across all reachable routes (post-namespacing).

oneOf.description:
Populated only for gateway-internal upstreams (e.g. `internal://web`).
Exposes admin-side configuration state the portal user can't observe
directly (does the operator have a backend selected? a credential
stored?), so the user can tell whether their agent calls will
actually succeed at runtime.

error.description: Human-readable detail when `status != ok`. None on success.

tools.description: Namespaced tool names (`<prefix>__<name>` when prefix is set).

built_in.description:
`true` when at least one of this virtual server's routes points at a
built-in upstream (e.g. the synthetic `builtin-web` row that backs
`/mcp/web`). Lets the portal badge the built-in web server and sort
it first in the quickstart MCP picker, regardless of its slug.

connection_status.description:
Aggregate per-user-OAuth connection state for the **current user**:
- `none` — no `per_user_oauth` upstreams (nothing to connect).
- `connected` — every `per_user_oauth` upstream has a present, unexpired
  credential for this user.
- `needs_connection` — at least one `per_user_oauth` upstream is missing
  a credential or its credential has expired. The config is still valid
  to write; the user connects in the portal to make it live.

Both the web quickstart and the `ssai` CLI surface this so a
user is warned to connect first; keep the two in sync.

requires_connection.description:
`true` when at least one of this virtual server's routes points at a
`per_user_oauth` upstream — i.e. the calling user must link their own
account in the portal before requests through this server succeed.

accounting_currency.description:
Currency this tenant keeps its books in — every budget cap and spend
figure the portal shows is expressed in it. Sent here so the portal has
one authoritative source, the way the console reads it from the settings
endpoint it is not allowed to call.

byok.description:
`true` when this is a BYOK pass-through downstream — provision a `vk-`
(BYOK) key against it; the client forwards its own upstream credential
and unconfigured models pass through. `false` for a normal gateway
provider (provision an `sk-` key + curated routes).

upstream_protocol.description:
For a BYOK pass-through, the protocol its server speaks
(`chat_completions` · `responses` · `anthropic_messages` ·
`google_gemini`) — the one a forwarded credential works on, so the
client template speaking it is the default. `None` for a gateway
provider, which translates, or a pass-through with no server.

oneOf.description: `null` when the window straddles a change of the accounting currency.

What the window spent, and in which currency. `null` when the window
straddles a change of the tenant's accounting currency — its rows are
then in different denominations and no single figure states them. The
same holds for every `spend` below.

shares_with_members.description:
True when this workspace shares members' usage, sessions and audit with
one another. The portal offers the workspace-wide view only here — the
server refuses to widen elsewhere regardless, so this is what the client
shows, not what enforces it.

settings.description: Native partial request body in the model's protocol vocabulary.

PreviewModelStatus.description: How a model an endpoint listed relates to the server's current models.

PreviewedFile.description: One rendered template (or companion) in a preview.

allOf.description: One rendered template (or companion) in a preview.

PricingSettings.description:
Tenant-wide accounting settings: the currency the books are kept in, and the
table for converting a provider's quote into it.

One struct rather than two loose values because they are only ever meaningful
together — a conversion table without a target currency converts to nothing,
and a target currency without a table can only be honoured for models already
quoted in it.

accounting_currency.description:
Currency every budget cap, spend aggregate and audit total is expressed
in.
Currency every budget cap, spend figure and audit total is expressed in.

currencies_in_use.description:
Currencies this tenant's own models are priced in, from its catalog and
its per-model overrides. Any entry other than `accounting_currency` needs
a rate, or requests against those models record no spend.

fx.description:
Operator-maintained conversion rates, `{from: {to: multiplier}}`. A pair
configured in one direction serves both — the inverse is exact.

unconvertible.description:
Currencies from `currencies_in_use` that cannot currently be converted
into the accounting currency. Non-empty means some traffic is being
billed as unstated and badged.

ProbeEmbeddingRequest.description:
Body for `POST /api/v1/admin/settings/cache/actions/probe-embedding`.

The alias is passed explicitly rather than read from the stored settings so
the UI can check a candidate before committing it.

ProbeEmbeddingResponse.description: Result of probing an embedding alias.

classified.description: Set when a successful probe reclassified a model as an embedding model.

ok.description: True only when **every** target the runtime can pick succeeded.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal problems worth showing: unpriced model, load-balanced alias,
non-standard endpoint paths.

model.description:
Judge model, `kind='expert'` only: the model the profile's experts
analyze with. `null` on a non-default profile = inherit the Default
expert profile's model. Always set on the Default; other kinds carry
`null`.

rule_count.description: Number of profile-specific content items (tool rules) for this profile.

Profile.description:
List/detail shape: the profile row plus the count of content items assigned
to it (tool rules for `kind='tools'`; `0` for kinds whose content isn't a
rule list, e.g. guardrail, which is a single policy blob).

oneOf.description: Inherit the tenant default (clear any explicit assignment).
Turn the kind fully off for this workspace.
Select a specific profile.

ProfileAssignmentChoice.description:
A workspace's tri-state choice for one profile kind, sent in
[`UpdateWorkspaceRequest::profiles`]. Tagged discriminated union (`mode`):
- `{"mode":"inherit"}` → delete any explicit row → fall back to the tenant
  default for that kind;
- `{"mode":"off"}` → upsert a NULL-profile row → the kind's policy is **fully
  disabled** for this workspace (the proxy resolves [`EffectiveProfile::Off`]);
- `{"mode":"profile","id":<uuid>}` → upsert that profile id.

ProfileCoverage.description:
Headline Stage-C metric: how many tool calls in the window resolved to a
canonical `tool_id` via the field-profile registry, and which wire names
dominate the unresolved tail.

top_unprofiled.description: Top 10 wire tool names by call count where `tool_id` resolution failed.

total_calls.description:
Equals `summary.total_calls` — duplicated here for self-contained
rendering of the coverage panel.

model.description:
Judge model, `kind='expert'` only: the model the profile's experts
analyze with. `null` on a non-default profile = inherit the Default
expert profile's model. Always set on the Default; other kinds carry
`null`.

oneOf.description: Inherits the Default; its own rows are the diff layered on top.
Owns its full content; ignores the Default.

ProfileStartChoice.description:
New-profile inheritance mode × initial content. `mode` is the tagged
discriminator; `content` seeds the profile's own rows.

profile_id.description:
Transform profile scope. `None` → shared (the baseline); `Some` →
specific to that transform profile.

PromptSnippet.description:
Expert prompt snippet — stored one row per snippet in the `prompt_snippets`
table (keyed `(tenant_id, snippet_key)`). Shape matches the markdown
frontmatter loader at `seed_loader::SnippetEntry`.

content.description: Markdown content rendered into the agent prompt.

is_builtin.description:
True for built-in snippets that re-seed on startup; user-created snippets
(and user-edited builtins) set this false so seeds don't overwrite them.

key.description: Stable key used in expert `prompt_snippets` arrays (e.g. `memory`, `session`).

label.description: Human-readable label shown in the admin UI.

ProtectedResourceMetadata.description:
Body of `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<resource_path>`.

The MCP handler returns 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
resource_metadata="<this URL>"` when an unauthenticated request hits an
OAuth-enabled virtual server. The client fetches this document to learn
which authorization server can mint a valid bearer.

We populate only the fields the spec mandates. The client is free to ignore
fields it doesn't recognize.

authorization_servers.description:
Authorization servers that can mint bearers for this resource. We
return exactly one — the proxy's per-tenant AS.

bearer_methods_supported.description: We accept the bearer in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

resource.description:
Canonical resource URI — exactly the audience the client must request
in its `resource` parameter (RFC 8707) and that we'll mint into the
`aud` claim.

resource_signing_alg_values_supported.description:
We sign access tokens for this resource with ES256. A holder that wants
to verify one locally fetches the authorization server's `jwks_uri` and
selects the key by the token's `kid`.

scopes_supported.description:
Every scope a client may request for this resource. A client following
least privilege picks the narrowest entry that covers what it intends to
do; one that asks for nothing receives full access.

inbound_count.description: Requests that arrived in this protocol — the client's inbound wire format.

outbound_count.description: Requests sent upstream in this protocol, after any protocol translation.

oneOf.description:
What this protocol's requests cost, and in which currency. `null` when
the window straddles a change of the tenant's accounting currency.

default_chat_endpoint_path.description:
Provider seed's chat-completions endpoint path override (null = canonical
`/v1/chat/completions`). Lets the UI prefill the field when a provider is
picked.

icon.description: 24x24 fill SVG path for the provider's brand glyph.

byok.description:
`true` for a BYOK pass-through downstream (keyless upstream; clients
forward their own credential, unconfigured models pass through). Granting
one to a workspace lets its members provision `vk-` keys against it.

enabled.description:
Its linked upstream server's on/off state (`true` when linked to none).
For a pass-through it is the live-grant rule: one that is not enabled
reaches nothing and is not offered for grants.

granted_workspaces.description: The workspaces whose allowlist holds this provider, by name.

is_builtin.description:
A seed-shipped pass-through: switched on and off from its server and
granted per workspace, never edited or deleted here (both answer
`409 BuiltinProviderProtected`).

workspace_count.description:
Number of workspaces whose allowlist includes this provider. Keys are no
longer provider-bound, so this measures provider reach across workspaces.

clients.description: Templates to bundle — at least one.

oneOf.description:
ONE gateway key shared by every selected client (mint or reuse).
Required when any selected template embeds a key.

llm_provider_id.description:
Provider the LLM sections render against. Required when any selected
template has an LLM section.

mcp_servers.description: MCP virtual servers to wire into every MCP-capable selected template.

workspace_id.description:
Workspace every rendered config draws on; the shared key is bound to
it and the chosen provider + MCP servers must be granted by it.

bundle_etag.description:
Content hash over (selections, templates, placeholders, key id). A
later `ssai sync` re-requests the bundle with `reuse_key_id`
and treats an unchanged etag as "nothing to rewrite".

client_access.description:
What the workspace is offered: its clients, and what its developers'
sandbox may reach besides the gateway.

oneOf.description:
The shared gateway key the bundle embeds; `None` when no selected
template needed one (spec-OAuth MCP-only).

minted_keys.description:
Key created by this call (empty on reuse). Same contract as the web
quickstart render.

label.description: Display label of the client profile.

launch_command.description: Command that launches the tool (e.g. `claude`). `None` for GUI clients.

placeholders.description:
The values the server rendered with, by placeholder name — strings,
flags and lists, as the template engine reads them. Never contains key
plaintext — `api_key` resolves to the same sentinel as the body.

rendered_body.description:
Server-rendered body (sentinel intact) — the CLI cross-checks its
local render against this to catch engine drift.

template.description: The RAW template — the CLI re-renders it locally on later syncs.

key_count.description: Live keys that name this class themselves.

route_target_count.description: Route targets that accept this class explicitly.

workspace_count.description: Workspaces whose keys default to this class.

QosClass.description: A class plus what currently points at it — the counts the delete flow needs.

is_default.description: The class every workspace without one of its own resolves to.

mint_default_for.description:
`interactive` or `automation`: the class a key minted by that kind of
principal gets. `null` on every other class.

queue_ttl_ms.description:
How long a request of this class may be held, in milliseconds. `null`
uses the deployment's default hold.

rank.description:
Lower is served first. Ties are broken by the fairness order between
users, never by arrival.

sheddable.description: Refused at once at saturation instead of being held.

QosDeploymentLimits.description:
The operator's hold limits every class resolves against. Read-only here:
they bound a gateway's memory and shutdown, so only the operator sets them.

oneOf.description:
What a class that names no wait of its own is held for: the default,
capped by the maximum, per gateway.

How long a request is held when its class names no wait of its own.
`null` (as are the two below) when no gateway states a readable
number: a value it could not parse is not a limit to state as zero.

gateway_replicas.description:
Gateway replicas connected now. Holds, and a server's in-flight limit,
apply per replica.

oneOf.description: The longest hold any class gets: a class asking for more is held this long.

QuickstartKey.description:
One existing key the caller can reuse instead of minting a fresh one. The
plaintext is never returned — reuse renders the snippet with the api-key
placeholder and the user pastes the value they saved at creation time.

key_prefix.description: First few characters of the key — a recognition hint, not the secret.

oneOf.description: One price, whatever the request size.
A base price plus thresholds on the request's prompt size.

tiers.description: Thresholds, applied by the highest one the basis exceeds.

Rate.description:
What one unit costs, in the rate map's currency and the unit's natural scale.

Tiering is the only case that needs more than a scalar, and it is a step
table rather than an expression: keeping it declarative is what lets a price
change ship as a seed refresh instead of a release.

Rates.description:
Prices for one model, and the currency they are quoted in.

Deliberately has no `Default`: an empty rate map means *no price is known*,
while a request the client funded elsewhere is *known to be free*, and the
two must never be reachable by the same expression. Construct through
[`Rates::unknown`] or [`Rates::free`].

currency.description:
Currency every rate above is quoted in. Travels inside the rate map so
prices and their currency are inherited as one atom — a row can never
take its numbers from the catalog and its currency from somewhere else.

units.description:
Price per unit, in `currency`, at each unit's natural scale. Keys are
pricing-unit wire names; an unrecognised one is dropped rather than
rejected, so a rate map written by a newer build still loads.

added_from.description: How many leading messages of this turn's history its parent carried.

messages.description:
The messages this turn added, each in the client protocol's wire shape —
its whole history when `whole_history`.

parent_request_id.description:
The turn this one continues — its parent, which need not be the turn
just before it in the list. When `whole_history` is false, the turn's whole
history is the parent's first `added_from` messages followed by
`messages`.

request_id.description: The turn's request — what a later turn's `parent_request_id` names.

response_tool_calls.description: The tool calls the answer carried, in the client protocol's shape; `null` when none.

whole_history.description:
`messages` is the turn's whole history: the session's first turn, a
turn that starts a new baseline, or one whose parent is not a turn
listed before it (unknown, not recorded, or expired).

RcloneConfigFrom.description: Who saved the rclone config, as the daemon knows it.

Record.description: `{ "kind": <RecordKind>, "body": <the record> }` — the body is the proxy's audit / MCP / A2A / web audit record, MCP SSE event row or rotated MCP credential

RecordKind.description:
The record kinds a share carries. The string form is the `kind` tag on
the wire and the outbox's `records.kind`.

RedactedToolResultInfo.description:
Info about a tool_result redacted by request-phase policy — mirrors
`BlockedToolInfo` for the result side. Captures both the original and
redacted content so the audit UI can surface the diff.

rule_id.description:
Stable identifier (e.g. `ASI02-02`) of the rule that redacted the
result.

tool_name.description:
Resolved by scanning the prior tool_use block with the matching id;
None when the pairing can't be located (rare — logged).

reason.description:
Why the gate gave no capacity: `shed`, `queue_timeout`,
`gateway_saturated`, `shutting_down` or `superseded` (the same request
was sent again while this copy waited). Counted at the pool that
refused, including the refusals a request then moved on from.

default_scopes.description:
Scopes to record on the registered client (RFC 7591 `scope`, space-
delimited). Defaults to none; many servers ignore it at registration.

issuer_url.description:
Optional explicit issuer URL. When supplied, the PRM step is skipped and
the authorization-server metadata is fetched directly from it.

upstream_url.description:
The MCP upstream server URL — the same value as the upstream row's
`upstream_url`. Used to discover the authorization server (and thus its
registration endpoint) when `issuer_url` is not supplied.

client_id.description:
The client identifier the authorization server issued — store as the
upstream's OAuth client ID.

oneOf.description:
The gateway key to embed. One unified key serves both the LLM and MCP
sections — the route grammar (`/v1/*` vs `/mcp/<slug>`) implies the
protocol and the workspace allowlist gates each target at request time.
Required for every static template; `spec_oauth` MCP-only templates mint
nothing and may omit it.

llm_provider_id.description:
Downstream provider to render the LLM snippet against. Required for
`kind = llm | combined | instructions`. Must be granted by the
workspace. The snippet renders against every enabled route under this
provider; single-model templates resolve `{{model_alias}}` to the
default route, `{{#each routes}}` templates get the full list.

mcp_servers.description:
MCP virtual servers to wire up. A `kind = mcp` template requires at
least one; `kind = combined` accepts 0..N (its body wraps the MCP
section in `{{#if mcp_servers}}`). Each must be granted by the workspace.

template_index.description:
Index into `ClientProfile.templates`. The wizard picks one template
up front (e.g. anthropic-messages variant) before calling render.

workspace_id.description:
Workspace the snippet draws on. The minted (or reused) key is bound to
it, and the chosen provider + MCP servers must be granted by it. The
caller must be a member.

companions.description:
Files the client needs ALONGSIDE `template` — a credential the tool
reads from its own env/secrets file rather than from the config the
profile templates. Same sentinel contract as `template.body`: the UI
substitutes the plaintext at copy-time. Empty for every client whose
template already carries its key.

minted_keys.description:
Keys created during this render. Empty when the render reused an
existing key or minted nothing.

body.description:
Body with the api-key placeholder (`<paste-your-api-key-here>`) left
intact — the same sentinel appears in the LLM section and in every MCP
server entry, since one key serves both. Safe to render to the DOM. The
UI substitutes the real key at copy-time using `MintedSecrets`.

endpoint_ids.description:
Every endpoint of the server, in the new order. The first enabled one
becomes the primary.

event_data.description: The SSE wire bytes, standard base64, to forward verbatim.

Resource.description:
A resource body, already canonical (see [`crate::digest`]); the edge
applies it as received and records `digest` as held.

body.description:
A [`crate::config::ConfigResponse`] for a tenant, a
[`crate::config::GlobalConfig`] for `global` — the canonical bytes
themselves, carried verbatim.

counter.description:
The resource's change counter the body was built at. Larger means
newer for one resource; the edge applies by digest and does not read it.

client_id.description: The `client_id` exactly as it appears in the inventory.

confirm.description: The release the operator confirmed going back to (from `GET …/rollback`).

RotateInlineAiKeyResponse.description:
The rotated inline-AI key, revealed ONCE so the operator can configure the
external analyzer (the mint-key reveal contract).

key.description:
The new plaintext key — returned ONCE, never again (rotate again for a
fresh one).

cache_preset_id.description: Bound response-cache preset (NULL = the alias is uncached).

cache_preset_name.description: Name of the bound cache preset, for display without a second lookup.

client_slots.description: The client model slots this route fills.

disabled_reason.description:
Why the route is disabled, if it is: `upstream_model_vanished` (soft —
model gone from the provider, reinstated if it returns) or
`upstream_model_deleted` (orphan — operator deleted the model/server).

model_id.description:
Null when the route is **orphaned** — its upstream model (or server) was
deleted. The row is kept (disabled, flagged) for cleanup; see `disabled_reason`.

preset_id.description: Bound invocation preset (NULL = the model's default preset).

preset_name.description:
Resolved preset name (the route's preset, else the model's default).
NULL when the route is orphaned (no model).

qos_class_ids.description: Priority classes this target accepts; empty = every class.

resolved_context_window.description:
Resolved window/output (COALESCE'd: upstream model → catalog).
NULL = the bound model declares no value (unknown). This is the honest
real window the proxy/`GET /v1/models` advertise — distinct from
`client_context_window` (token-scaling).

RowRef.description: Names one record of a share: what [`ShareOutcome::Rejected`] lists.

a2a_agent_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the A2A upstream agent's slug
(`a2a_upstream_agents.slug`, e.g. `research-prod`, `partner-*`). The
agent is the pivot of the `agent_calls` scope the way the upstream is
the pivot of MCP rules. Non-A2A traffic never matches a rule with this
filter set; `None` means "any agent".

app_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the request's `app_id` (client
identity, e.g. `claude-code`, `cursor-*`). When set, the rule only
fires for matching apps. `None` means "any app".

enabled.description: Inert when false; preserved in storage. `extract_for` skips disabled rules.

forked_from.description:
Copy-on-write link: when set on a `Some(P)` rule, this is a per-profile
**fork** of the shared rule with this id — it *suppresses* that shared rule
inside P (an override). Deleting the fork reverts P to the shared rule.

id.description:
Stable operator-visible identifier (e.g. `ASI02-06`). Surfaces on
blocked-tool banners and transform diffs so reviewers know which rule
fired without parsing the description. Every rule carries one: a seed
names it, and a rule created through the API is given one.

is_builtin.description:
Server-managed: `true` on initial seed and on `actions/reset`, `false`
after the first PATCH/PUT. Ignored on incoming client payloads.

match.description: AND-of-conditions. Empty means "every item in scope" (catch-all).

mcp_server_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the MCP upstream server name
(`mcp_upstream_servers.name`, e.g. `notion-prod`, `internal-*`).
When set, the rule only fires for matching upstreams; `None` means
"any upstream". Non-MCP traffic (LLM tool calls without an MCP
namespace) never matches a rule with this filter set — pairs
naturally with `(request, resource_reads | prompt_invocations)`
rules. Use this to keep per-upstream policies (and per-test rules)
from spilling onto other servers in the same tenant.

model_filter.description: Optional pipe-separated glob over the resolved upstream model name.

priority.description:
Lower wins. Default 100. Stable-sorted with original list position as
the tiebreaker so manual ordering still controls equal-priority rules.

profile_id.description:
Profile scope. `None` → **shared**: the rule applies to every profile (the
baseline; builtins live here). `Some(P)` → **specific** to profile P. The
snapshot bucketer fans shared rules into every profile's bucket.

risk.description:
`"safe"` | `"caution"` | `"danger"` | `"unknown"` — the rule's classification
for matching items, regardless of which action kind is configured.

oneOf.description: Annotate the matched item with `risk` + rule id; no mutation.
Drop the matched item (definition removed from request, tool_call/result suppressed elsewhere).

Rewrite the scoped content. With `regex`: per-match capture-aware rewrite (`with` may use $1..).
Without `regex`: wholesale replace with `with`. With `drop: true`: rewrite to "" (drop wins
over `regex`/`with` when combined). `with` defaults to "[redacted]".

Replace the matched tool definition wholesale and bind an intercept
handler that fires on response-side `tool_use` echoes for the new
name. The load-bearing primitive for cross-protocol web-search /
web-fetch substitution. Valid only on `Request × ToolDefinitions`.

Bind an intercept handler against the matched tool's name without
rewriting the definition — the upstream sees the tool unchanged but
any `tool_use` for it is routed through the intercept handler.
Valid only on `Request × ToolDefinitions`.

RuleActivity.description: Per-rule activity aggregated over the request's time window.

call_count_window.description: Calls that fired this rule (first-match-wins, per the unified evaluator).

last_seen.description:
Most recent matching call timestamp; `None` when the rule never fired
in the window.

tool_count_window.description: Distinct wire tool names with at least one matching call.

RuntimeConfigResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/admin/global/runtime-config` response — the catalog plus
desired (override) and actual (per-edge) state.

admin_values.description: admin-api process effective values, keyed by token (Admin-group only).

catalog.description: Every catalog entry, with its current desired override (if set).

secrets_present.description:
Secret / bootstrap token → whether it is set in the admin-api process.
The value itself is never serialized.

SandboxPolicy.description:
What the sandbox of a workspace's developers may reach, flattened from
the attached lists: the provision bundle's `sandbox` section and the
portal's sandbox policy. The gateway is always reachable and is not listed.

allow.description: Canonical entries of every list attached as allow.

block.description: Canonical entries of every list attached as block — a block wins.

revision.description: Content hash of the three fields above: unchanged = nothing to rewrite.

SandboxSettings.description: The sandbox settings, resolved (an unset setting reads its default).

SandboxSettingsPatch.description: The sandbox settings to change; a field absent is unchanged.

SearchHit.description: One ranked hit from the search backend, post URL-filter chain.

SearchResult.description:
Result returned to the caller. `total_filtered` counts hits dropped by
the URL-filter chain so the model can reason about coverage.

backend.description: Echo of the configured backend that ran the call.

total_filtered.description:
Hits the backend returned that the URL-filter chain denied. Always
`0` when no filter denied anything.

actor_identity.description:
Attempted identity — the login email or OAuth client_id. NULL when the
request carried none (e.g. the body-less OAuth callback).

request_body.description: Redacted request body (secret-shaped keys removed); `null` when the body was empty or not JSON; `{ "_truncated": true, "_bytes": <n>, …identity fields }` when it was too large to keep.

response_error.description: The error body the call answered with (`{code, message}` for a current release, any stored JSON for an older one); `null` on success.

SecurityFramework.description:
A single entry in `seeds/tool-policy/frameworks.json` — a reference to an
external security framework category (OWASP LLM Top-10, MITRE ATLAS, CWE)
that the framework-aware expert cites when proposing rules, and that the
UI uses to render context when an operator clicks a framework chip.

id.description:
Stable id, prefixed by framework family
(`OWASP-LLM01`, `MITRE-ATLAS-AML-T0048`, `CWE-78`, …).

tool_risk_hints.description:
Short bullet-list of tool-risk patterns that typically map to this
framework entry. Surfaced to the agent + the UI side-panel.

qos_class_id.description: `null` for requests of a tenant with no classes.

class_held_series.description:
Requests held at the gateway, per class (holds a gateway reported with
no class breakdown as their own series). Empty when nothing was held.

endpoints.description: Per endpoint that answered in the window or reports live load.

interval.description:
`"hour"` for a window up to 8 days, `"day"` beyond
([`server_bucket_interval`]).

load_series.description:
Live load per endpoint over the window (the part of it within
`live_history_days`).

top_waiters.description: The users whose requests waited longest in total.

adaptive_concurrency.description:
Whether the gateways LEARN each endpoint's in-flight limit from its
engine's readings (KV-cache use, preemptions, prefix-cache hit rate),
`max_in_flight` being the ceiling. Excludes a waiting-queue bound; the
engines are read whatever `engine_metrics` says.

adaptive_itl_target.description:
The token-latency target the learned limit keeps each engine within:
no raise while the engine's inter-token latency is above it, and a step
down when it stays above it. `auto` (the default) is a multiple of each
engine's own time per token at low load, as the gateways learn it;
`fixed` is `ms`; `off` grows the limit as far as the engine's memory
holds.

auto_sync_enabled.description:
When on, the autosync worker periodically re-discovers this server's
models and mirrors them downstream (add + refresh + remove).

byok.description:
True when a `byok = true` pass-through downstream is linked to this
keyless upstream. Set-once at create — an update derives it solely
from the linked downstream and never flips it.

chat_endpoint_path.description:
Override for the appended chat-completions endpoint path (null = the
canonical `/v1/chat/completions`).

endpoint_count.description: How many endpoints (replicas) the server has.

endpoints_down.description:
Endpoints a connected gateway currently has out of rotation (breaker
open).

engine_metrics.description:
Whether the gateways read this server's engines' own metrics
(`/metrics`) for the dashboards. On by default for vLLM. An endpoint
with a waiting-queue bound is read whatever this says.

gated.description:
Whether the dispatch gate applies here: the server, or any enabled
endpoint of it, declares an in-flight or a waiting-queue bound. Only a
gated server has live load to report.

health.description: Whether the server can serve traffic now, from the same counts.

is_builtin.description:
A seed-shipped pass-through: it is switched on and off and repointed,
never deleted (the delete answers `409 BuiltinProviderProtected`).

last_auto_sync_at.description: Timestamp of the last autosync (or "sync now") run, if any.

oneOf.description: Outcome of the last run. Null until the first run.

max_in_flight.description:
How many requests the gateway may have in flight at one endpoint of this
server, and how long that engine's own queue may grow before it is sent
no more. Both null = the dispatch gate does not apply to this server.

scheduling_dialect.description:
How this engine expresses a request's priority class: `none` (the
default — the gateway keeps the decision to itself) or `vllm_priority`.

transport.description:
How requests are carried to this server: `default`, `azure_openai`,
`azure_openai_entra`, `aws_bedrock` or `google_vertex`.

upstream_url.description: The primary endpoint's URL: the first enabled endpoint of the server.

auto_itl_target_ms.description:
What an automatic token-latency target is now, in milliseconds:
`AUTO_ITL_TARGET_RATIO` times the slowest engine's time per token at
low load, as the connected gateways report it
(`ServerLive::auto_itl_target_ms`; each engine is held to its own
figure's). `null` while the limit is not learned, or no engine has
taught one yet — an automatic target is then still learning. Reported
whatever the setting.

vllm_engine.description:
The provider is vLLM, read as every other provider check reads it:
the QoS tab shows that engine's settings.

url.description:
A URL the rows recorded for this endpoint — what names an endpoint
since removed. A current endpoint is named by its own resource.

oneOf.description:
`null` when no replica has reported a reading lately — the server is
not gated, or no gateway is connected.

interval.description: `"hour"` for a window up to 48 hours, `"day"` beyond.

live_history_days.description:
How far back live load readings reach for this tenant: seven days, or
its retention window if that is shorter.

servers.description:
Every existing server with traffic in the window or a live reading now.
A server absent here had neither, or has been deleted.

ServerHealth.description:
Whether an upstream server can serve traffic right now, as the connected
gateways report it.

ServerLive.description:
The live load of a server, from the newest reading each gateway replica
sent for each of its gated endpoints.

auto_itl_target_ms.description:
The largest automatic token-latency target among the server's engines
(`AdaptiveLive::auto_itl_target_ms`), in milliseconds — the slowest
engine's. `null` until an engine has taught one.

capacity.description:
How many the replicas may have in flight there — `null` unless every
reported endpoint declares an in-flight bound.

engines_silent.description:
Endpoints whose engine gauges the gateway reads that declare a queue
bound (or learn their limit) and that some replica has stopped hearing
from — that replica is not applying the bound, whatever the others see.
An engine read only for the dashboards and gone quiet is not counted
here: nothing depends on it but its charts (see
`EndpointLive::queue_bounded`).

gated.description:
Whether any of the server's endpoints is gated. Only a gated endpoint's
requests are counted; one read only for its engine metrics is not.

held.description: Requests the replicas are holding for want of capacity.

held_by_class.description:
The same, per priority class, most held first. Empty from a gateway
that does not report classes.

in_flight.description: Requests in flight at the server's gated endpoints, across replicas.

sampled_at.description: When the newest reading was taken.

ServerMembershipResponse.description: Which endpoint serves which model of a server.

ServerRecentLoadResponse.description:
One server's gauges over the last few minutes, one bucket per TWO
heartbeats ([`recent_bucket_secs`]), each beat carrying its interval's peak. The
same figures as the dashboard's load series (peak and mean per bucket),
whatever the dashboard's period.

class_held_series.description: Requests held at the gateway, per class, as on the dashboard.

oneOf.description:
The server's load now — the same as the dashboard's `live` — so a figure
labelled "now" beside these charts moves with them.

load_series.description:
Each endpoint's gauges, and the rates derived from its engine's
counters and its learned limit's decisions, per bucket — the
dashboard's load series at this grain.

window_secs.description: Seconds the window covers, ending now.

adaptive_concurrency.description:
Whether the gateways LEARN each endpoint's in-flight limit from its
engine's readings (KV-cache use, preemptions, prefix-cache hit rate),
`max_in_flight` being the ceiling. Excludes a waiting-queue bound; the
engines are read whatever `engine_metrics` says.

adaptive_itl_target.description:
The token-latency target the learned limit keeps each engine within:
no raise while the engine's inter-token latency is above it, and a step
down when it stays above it. `auto` (the default) is a multiple of each
engine's own time per token at low load, as the gateways learn it;
`fixed` is `ms`; `off` grows the limit as far as the engine's memory
holds.

When on, the autosync worker periodically re-discovers this server's
models and mirrors them downstream (add + refresh + remove).

byok.description:
True when a `byok = true` pass-through downstream is linked to this
keyless upstream. Set-once at create — an update derives it solely
from the linked downstream and never flips it.

chat_endpoint_path.description:
Override for the appended chat-completions endpoint path (null = the
canonical `/v1/chat/completions`).

endpoint_count.description: How many endpoints (replicas) the server has.

endpoints_down.description:
Endpoints a connected gateway currently has out of rotation (breaker
open).

engine_metrics.description:
Whether the gateways read this server's engines' own metrics
(`/metrics`) for the dashboards. On by default for vLLM. An endpoint
with a waiting-queue bound is read whatever this says.

gated.description:
Whether the dispatch gate applies here: the server, or any enabled
endpoint of it, declares an in-flight or a waiting-queue bound. Only a
gated server has live load to report.

health.description: Whether the server can serve traffic now, from the same counts.

is_builtin.description:
A seed-shipped pass-through: it is switched on and off and repointed,
never deleted (the delete answers `409 BuiltinProviderProtected`).

last_auto_sync_at.description: Timestamp of the last autosync (or "sync now") run, if any.

oneOf.description: Outcome of the last run. Null until the first run.

max_in_flight.description:
How many requests the gateway may have in flight at one endpoint of this
server, and how long that engine's own queue may grow before it is sent
no more. Both null = the dispatch gate does not apply to this server.

scheduling_dialect.description:
How this engine expresses a request's priority class: `none` (the
default — the gateway keeps the decision to itself) or `vllm_priority`.

transport.description:
How requests are carried to this server: `default`, `azure_openai`,
`azure_openai_entra`, `aws_bedrock` or `google_vertex`.

upstream_url.description: The primary endpoint's URL: the first enabled endpoint of the server.

ServerTraffic.description:
What a server — or one endpoint, class or time bucket of it — handled,
counted over ATTEMPTS: the attempt each request ended with, and each one it
moved on from (refused by this server's pool, or sent here and failed, then
tried elsewhere). A server that fails every request a fallback then answers
is failing, and says so here.

errors.description:
Attempts sent here that the server failed — no answer, an error answer,
a stream that broke or went quiet — the request's last, or one it moved
on from (`failed_over`). Neither a refusal nor a failure that is not the
server's (the client hanging up, the gateway's own fault) is one: the
share failed is `errors / (requests - refusals)`, over what was sent.

failed_over.description:
Of `errors`, the ones the request moved on from, to another replica or
another target.

latency_p50_ms.description:
Upstream latency of the requests served here, excluding any wait for
capacity and the time spent on the attempts before this one. `null`
when none was.

passed_on.description: Of `refusals`, the ones the request moved on from.

queue_wait_p50_ms.description:
The wait at this server's pool of the attempts that waited and were
sent to it. `null` when none did.

queued.description:
Attempts that waited for capacity at this server's pool and were then
sent to it. One that waited and was refused is a refusal
(`queue_timeout`), not counted here.

refusals.description:
Attempts this server's pool refused — for want of capacity, or a
waiting copy replaced by the same request sent again (`superseded`) —
the request's last, or one it moved on from (`passed_on`).

requests.description:
Attempts at this server: requests sent to it or refused by its pool,
once per attempt. A request that moved on counts here and at the
target it moved to.

spilled.description:
Requests moved to another replica of the server because theirs had no
room. Per endpoint: the ones moved TO it.

ttft_p95_ms.description:
Time to first token of the CHAT requests served here, excluding any
wait. A media or pass-through call records its whole duration there,
which is no first token of anything.

wait_ms_total.description:
Everything the attempts spent waiting at this server's pool — the
refused ones' waits included: that time was spent all the same.

label.description: Display name, else email, else the id.

queue_wait_p95_ms.description: The wait of the attempts that waited and were then sent.

queued.description: Attempts that waited and were then sent.

requests.description: This user's attempts at this server (see [`ServerTraffic::requests`]).

wait_ms_total.description:
Everything this user's requests spent waiting at this server's pool, in
total — including a wait that ended in a refusal here, or in an attempt
the request then moved on from: that time was spent all the same.

ServiceAccountKeyItem.description:
A key owned by a service account — unified across the automation (`ak-`) and
gateway (`sk-`/`vk-`) tables. `plane` discriminates; the per-plane fields are
populated only where they apply.

plane.description:
`admin` (ak-, admin control plane) | `portal` (ak-, portal control plane)
| `gateway` (sk-/vk-, data plane).

active_keys.description:
Count of live (non-revoked, non-expired) keys the account owns, across
both the admin and gateway key tables.

is_builtin.description: True for the built-in agent service account (read-only in the UI).

SessionLinkage.description: How a session sits in a cross-session relation.

SessionSort.description:
The order of a session list. A text search pages through its matches by
`updated_at`, so under a search term only `newest` and `oldest` exist.

linkage_spawn_tool_call_id.description:
Tool-call id of the spawn call in the parent this session was spawned from
(a CHILD only). The UI anchors the child card to the composite
`(linkage_spawn_turn, linkage_spawn_tool_call_id)` on the parent's stream.

oneOf.description:
What the session's turns cost, in the accounting currency they were
booked in. `null` when no single figure can be stated: the turns span
a change of the accounting currency.

SessionTurnSummary.description: Summary of a turn within a session timeline.

response_tool_calls.description: The tool calls the turn's answer carried, in the client protocol's shape; `null` when none.

oneOf.description:
What the turn cost, and in which currency — one audit row, so the
currency is the one the ledger stamped when the row was written.

from.description:
Analyze sessions with activity after this instant. Absent or `null` = now,
which drops the backlog. Earlier than the current position analyzes again what
was already analyzed. A future instant is refused.

oneOf.description: New per-key budget. Null caps clear the cap; omitted budget clears it too.

kind.description: `interactive`, `automation`, or `null` to take the star off this class.

SettingDescriptor.description: A catalog entry plus its current desired override — the API wire shape.

override_value.description: The desired central override, if one is set.

SettingGroup.description:
Which process a setting configures. `Secret` covers secrets and bootstrap
variables — reference-only entries with no backing settings struct.

SettingKind.description: A setting's value type — drives override validation and the UI input.

single_tenant_slug.description:
Slug of the only active organisation (a tenant other than `system`)
when exactly one exists, else null. Lets the landings and login pages
skip the unanswerable "organization" prompt on a single-organisation
install.

oneOf.description: Every row is stored (or already was).

The share committed without these rows, which the database refused for
their data — every resend would be refused the same way.
The tenant no longer exists; nothing of the share can be stored.

ShareOutcome.description: What became of one share. Only `Retry` keeps it at the edge.

SourceFilter.description:
List filter on a row's origin: shipped with the product (`builtin`) or
written by the tenant (`custom`).

SpendBreakdown.description:
A spend total decomposed per pricing unit.

Carries the same currency contract as [`SpendTotal`], and names its figure
`amount` for the same reason — one accessor renders either. `amount` is the
whole charge: the `units` costs summed, plus `embedding`.

embedding.description:
Response-cache embedding calls, charged to the requests that triggered
them. Outside `units` because they price a different model.

media.description:
The part of `amount` the media endpoints accounted for. Cuts across the
units rather than adding to them — a transcription's `audio_second`
line is media, an ordinary completion's `input_token` line is not.

units.description:
Per-pricing-unit decomposition of `amount`, in unit declaration order.
A unit nothing consumed is omitted rather than reported as a zero line.

SpendTotal.description:
A spend total and the accounting currency it is stated in.

Every audit row stamps the currency in force when it was written, because
changing the tenant's accounting currency must not restate spend already
reported. An aggregate is therefore only a figure when every row behind it
shares one currency — wherever this type appears as an `Option`, `None`
means the rows straddle a change of that setting, and adding their amounts
would state a total in no currency at all.

SpendUnit.description: One pricing unit's contribution to an aggregate.

cost.description: What that count cost, in the enclosing figure's currency.

count.description:
Units charged, summed over the aggregate. The provider's reported count
less anything charged on a line of its own, so the lines never double
count.

StartContent.description:
Initial content for a new profile. `blank` = empty; `seed` = a fresh copy of
the kind's built-in defaults; `copy` = a deep copy of another profile's own
content.

size_bytes.description: Wire bytes of the upstream response (raw HTTP body length).

stripped.description:
Discriminator for `#[serde(untagged)]` deserialize. Always `true`
when emitted by the cap path.

content_hash.description:
Hash of every field an approval installs; send it back on approve so
the approval installs exactly what was reviewed.

proposed_trigger_regex.description: Optional fast-find / span-finder regex carried onto the promoted program.

endpoints.description:
What each enabled endpoint answered, primary first — an endpoint that
did not answer changed nothing, which is why a sync can change less than
expected.

held.description:
The full held set — only when the previous response set
[`SyncResponse::send_held`].

instance.description:
The edge instance: an id created with the edge's durable store and kept
in it (`edge_instances.instance_key`).

outbox_pending.description: Rows still buffered for ingest, the async audit queue included.

wait_ms.description:
How long admin-api may hold an answer that would carry nothing, waiting
for a body or an event to send instead. 0 answers at once.

events_cursor.description:
What the edge sends as its next `events_after`: the last event of a
full page, else the newest event id when the answer was read — every
event for this instance up to it is in `events` — and never beyond it
(a cursor past the newest id, after a restore, comes back down).

more.description:
Resources whose body differs but did not fit this answer; they come on
the next poll. While true, the edge does not hold the current config.

send_held.description:
The admin could not tell what this instance holds: the next request
carries the full [`SyncRequest::held`]. Nothing else is set.

SyntheticSourceTag.description:
Marker stamped on `llm_audit` rows whose request was synthesized by an
MCP `sampling/createMessage` interception. `source` is a stable string
the UI dispatches on; today the only producer is `"mcp_sampling"`.

SystemPromptContent.description:
A system prompt, keyed by its
[`system_prompt_hash`](streamscope_core::audit::system_prompt_hash) within
the tenant.

TemplateFormat.description:
Lexical format of a client-config template body. Drives both the
syntax-highlight hint on the UI side and the per-format escape mode the
renderer applies to substituted values.

TemplateKind.description:
What kind of credential the template uses. Drives wizard step gating: a
`combined` template needs both an LLM key and an MCP key; a `mcp` template
only an MCP key; an `instructions` template carries no secrets.

mcp_oauth_delegate_to_oidc.description:
When true, the spec-OAuth `/authorize` consent step
delegates user authentication to the tenant's OIDC IdP. The portal
consent page reads this to decide whether to redirect to OIDC begin
instead of rendering the credential-based session check.

is_connected.description:
Some replica of this edge has synced recently. `all_synced` counts only
these, so an edge that never connected cannot read as lagging.

synced.description: Every live replica holds the tenant's current config.

TenantSettings.description:
Typed per-tenant settings surface. Every field is `Option<T>` with `#[serde(default)]`
so PATCH requests can carry partial updates and GET responses remain stable when new
fields land.

Wire shape for both `GET /api/v1/admin/settings` and `PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings`.
Partial updates are the norm — send only the fields you want to change.

admin_public_url.description:
Public URL of the admin/portal UI for this tenant. Used by login
links, invite/email URLs, OIDC RP-initiated-logout post-redirect,
MCP OAuth admin redirect, admin/portal CORS allow-list. Same layering
rules as `proxy_public_url`.

agent_run_window_enabled.description:
When true, the agent only runs analysis cycles whose current UTC
hour falls inside `[agent_run_window_start_hour_utc,
agent_run_window_end_hour_utc)`. Outside the window, cycles are
skipped with a log line. Lets operators reserve agent load for
off-hours on shared on-premise LLMs.

agent_run_window_end_hour_utc.description:
Window end hour in UTC (0..=23 inclusive, exclusive bound). See
`agent_run_window_start_hour_utc` for wrap-around semantics.

agent_run_window_start_hour_utc.description:
Window start hour in UTC (0..=23 inclusive). When `start < end` the
window is `[start, end)`; when `start > end` it wraps past midnight
(`[start, 24) ∪ [0, end)`). `start == end` disables the window
(treated as empty).

api_public_url.description:
Public URL of the admin-API for external scripting / CLI access.
Caddy serves the admin-API at this FQDN; operators set this value
so the UI can display the canonical script-callable URL (copy-out
for `curl` / SDKs). Not in any CORS allowlist — scripts aren't
browsers, and the UI calls the admin-API same-origin through the
SvelteKit proxy at `admin_public_url`. Same layering rules as
`proxy_public_url` (per-tenant override over SYSTEM default).

app_registry.description:
App registry — client detection patterns for incoming requests. The only
apps-edit surface: a full-array replace written to the `apps` table.

proxy_public_url.description:
Public URL of the proxy gateway (scheme + host[:port], no trailing
slash, no path). Used by Quickstart snippets, MCP OAuth audience,
and MCP CORS allowlist. Empty/unset on a non-SYSTEM tenant means
"inherit the SYSTEM default"; unset on SYSTEM means dependent
surfaces fail closed for every tenant that doesn't override.

tenant_daily_budget.description:
Daily ceiling across every workspace in the tenant, in the tenant's
accounting currency. `0` = uncapped.
Distinct from `default_daily_budget`, which is only the value a
workspace inherits when it sets none: this one caps the organisation.

tenant_monthly_budget.description:
Monthly ceiling across every workspace in the tenant, in the tenant's
accounting currency. `0` = uncapped.

oneOf.description: Tool risk classification rules — stored as `{ rules: [ToolRule...] }`.

TenantShare.description:
One tenant's records and the content they reference, written together.

Every body a record names ([`Record::content_keys`]) is carried in
`content`, left out (this edge delivered it earlier — in a share admin-api
committed, or a blob that went up by itself), or named in `unavailable`
(the edge cannot deliver it). Admin-api checks every key a record names
that the share does not carry: one it does not hold is asked for in
[`ShareOutcome::Retry`] and nothing is written — unless the share names it
`unavailable`, when the records naming it are stored badged
`content_unavailable`.

unavailable.description:
Bodies the records name that the edge does not have to send: refused
when buffered (too large for any request), or lost since.

all_synced.description:
Every live replica of every edge holds this tenant's current config
and the current global config, read from the database now; false when
no replica is live.

TenantUsage.description: Per-tenant usage row returned by the global usage query.

oneOf.description:
What the tenant spent, in its accounting currency. `null` when the
window straddles a change of that currency.

reason.description:
Human-readable reason when match/no-match is non-obvious
(e.g. "name matched but arg_patterns did not").

context.description: The context object the program runs against; free-form, read by the script as written.

match_mode.description:
Execution mode for the preview. `"span"` runs the script once per
`trigger_regex` match over the sample context's text; anything else runs
the full-context script once.

result.description: What the program returned for the test context — whatever value the script produced; `null` when it returned nothing.

TestToolRule.description:
Body of POST /tool-rules/actions/test. Carries a draft rule (the create
body: its id may be omitted) and a list of sample tool names + optional
sample args; returns one match result per sample. The rule isn't persisted —
used by the modal sandbox to preview matching.

sample_args.description: The tool-call arguments to test the rule against, as a tool would send them.

sample_content.description:
Optional sample tool_result content body — only relevant for
`phase=request, scope=tool_results` rules. Ignored otherwise.

Tier.description: A price threshold: above `above` units of the tiering basis, `rate` applies.

above.description: Basis count this tier takes effect strictly above.

rate.description: Rate for the whole request once the basis exceeds `above`.

oneOf.description:
What this bucket spent, and in which currency. `null` when the bucket
straddles a change of the tenant's accounting currency — its rows are
then in different denominations and no single figure states them.

code_verifier.description:
Required when `grant_type=authorization_code` (PKCE). Ignored for
`refresh_token` — the refresh-token JWT signature itself is the
proof-of-possession.

device_code.description:
Required when `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`
(RFC 8628). Ignored for the other grants.

resource.description:
RFC 8707 §2.2: the protected resource this token is being requested for.

The metadata document advertises `resource_parameter_supported`, so a
conforming client sends it and is entitled to have it honoured — a
value that disagrees with the audience the grant was issued for is
refused rather than quietly ignored, which is the difference between a
token scoped where the client believes it is and one that is not.

refresh_token.description:
Issued alongside the access token. Long-lived (30d). Present a
refresh token to `POST /token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` to
rotate to a fresh access + refresh token pair without re-consent.

refresh_token_expires_in.description: TTL of the issued refresh token, in seconds.

TokenStatusBreakdown.description:
Counts of tokens by status, scoped to the same filters as the list
(excluding the `status` filter itself). Powers the Tokens-tab header.

issued.description: Total tokens in scope (active + revoked + expired).

TokenStatusFilter.description: Status filter for the issued-tokens list.

ToolArgModification.description:
Per-argument modification a response-phase `replace` rule applied to a tool
call. Attached to `ConversationEvent::ToolCall.modifications` so the UI can
render "arg X changed from A to B" alongside the effective payload.

field.description: Name of the mutated argument key (e.g. `command`, `file_path`).

original.description: Original value as received from the model.

rule_id.description: Id of the rule that made the change.

ToolCallBlock.description:
Rule-identity payload attached to a `ConversationEvent::ToolCall` when a
policy rule rejected the call. The call is still rendered in the stream
(the model actually emitted it); this struct lets the UI overlay *which
rule* fired and *why*.

phase.description:
Where the block fired: `request` (tool stripped before LLM) or
`response` (LLM emitted an arg-based-blocked call). Today only
`response`-phase blocks attach to a `ToolCall` event — request-phase
blocks surface only on the turn header.

reason.description:
Full rule description carried through from the seed rule — UI uses
this for tooltip / expanded detail. May contain a legacy `[ASI02]`
prefix for older rules.

rule_id.description:
Stable rule identifier (e.g. `ASI02-06`), read from the persisted
`transform_diff` JSONB — never parsed back out of the description text.
`None` only for an agent-call block whose finding names no rule
(`A2aPolicyFinding::rule_id` is optional on its record).

ToolCallKind.description:
The row families of the tool-calls feed: a tool call is made over LLM
tool use, MCP or the built-in Web tool. An agent call (A2A) is not a tool
call, so `a2a` is not a value here — the audit list carries those.

ToolCallOutcome.description: The `outcome` a tool-call feed can narrow to.

call_event.description:
Canonical `ConversationEvent::ToolCall` event — rendered by the UI with
the same component the session view uses.

latency_total_ms.description:
Call-side `gateway_audit.latency_total_ms`. Surfaced on the unified
tool-call row card's header strip so LLM rows align visually with
MCP / web rows. `None` for synthetic blocked invocations whose call
turn was suppressed before the latency was stamped.

oneOf.description: Canonical `ConversationEvent::ToolResult` event when paired.

user_email.description:
Raw email of the row's user (when resolved). Distinct from
`user_display` (which falls back to display name or id). Drives the
row-card "filter by user" button so the click reapplies a precise
email filter, not the display-name fallback.

allOf.description:
MCP-side audit row exposed at `/audit?kind=mcp`. Per-call shape with the
joined virtual-server slug + user email + protocol_version so the audit
UI can render rows without an extra fan-out fetch. Operators correlate
across calls in the same JSON-RPC session by pasting `mcp_session_id`
into the audit list `search` box (substring match).

app_id.description:
Three-tier app id resolved by `extract_attribution` from `X-App-Id` /
`Referer` / `User-Agent` (mirrors LLM rows). `None` when no pattern
matched. Stored on `gateway_audit.app_id`.

badges.description:
Typed audit badges — same `AuditBadge` enum as LLM rows. Codes are
append-only; UI consumer is the shared `BADGE_REGISTRY`. DB column
is `NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` so this is always present.

mcp_session_id.description:
Raw `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the call. Distinct from
`session_id` above (which is hashed).

params.description:
JSON-RPC `params` payload as the agent sent it (for `tools/call`
this is the `{name, arguments}` envelope; for `resources/read` the
`{uri}`; for `prompts/get` the `{name, arguments}`). Mirrors the
LLM trace's `messages` field — surfaced so the audit drawer + the
session-view MCP bubble can render the actual request body
without an extra fetch.

protocol_version.description:
MCP protocol version negotiated at `initialize` and pinned for the
remainder of the session. `None` for the rare row that lands before
`initialize` completes (`mcp_sessions.protocol_version` defaults to
`"unknown"`).

result.description:
JSON-RPC `result` payload returned by the upstream (success path
only — error responses populate `error_code` / `error_message`).

session_id.description:
Hashed session id from `gateway_audit.session_id` — same shape the
LLM `AuditLogEntry` carries. Cross-protocol correlation pivots on
this when an MCP `sampling/createMessage` was intercepted by the
gateway and answered through the LLM pipeline (the synthetic
`llm_audit` row shares this id).

oneOf.description:
Typed diff payload stamped by the MCP policy engine + multiplex pump.
Each field corresponds to a key the proxy may stamp on a given row.
Empty struct (`{}`) when nothing fired.

allOf.description:
Web audit row exposed at `/audit?kind=web`. One row per
dispatched call (both direct `/mcp/web` traffic with `surface='mcp'` and
substitution-loop children with `surface='substitution'`). `parent_request_id`
links substitution rows back to the orchestrating LLM `gateway_audit`
row; the dedicated `GET /api/v1/admin/audit/{request_id}/web`
endpoint queries by it.

fetch_content_summary.description: For fetch operations: blob hashes/MIMEs into audit_media_blobs.

filter_chain.description: Ordered filter ids that ran in the chain.

parent_request_id.description:
Orchestrating LLM `request_id` when `surface == "substitution"`;
`None` for direct MCP traffic.

oneOf.description:
Provider's raw response, typed as the cap-aware
[`streamscope_core::web::audit::WebProviderResponse`]
enum. UI branches on the `Stripped` variant for the oversized
callout.

response_summary.description: Response shape returned to the caller.

result_count.description: search → hits returned to caller (post-filter); fetch → 1 on success.

oneOf.description: Per-rule diff payload (same shape the LLM/MCP rows carry).

url_results.description: Per-URL filter verdicts on every search hit / fetch target.

ToolCallRow.description:
`kind`-discriminated row family for the unified tool-calls feed. UI
branches on `row.kind` and dispatches to the matching detail component.
Boxed variants because `WebAuditLogEntry` is wide (~1 KB of optional
JSON columns) and the size mismatch with the LLM shape would blow up
per-row allocation in the `kind=all` merge.

parameters.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 input schema for the tool's arguments.

ToolDefinitionBlobResponse.description:
Lazy-fetch a single deduplicated tool-definition blob by hash. Mirrors
`get_media_blob` shape, but returns JSON (tool definitions are JSON, not
binary). The UI uses this when expanding a `tools_changed` event banner so
it can render the diff between the previous and current tool sets without
inlining the blobs on every turn.

definition.description: The tools array as the client declared it, in its own protocol's shape.

ToolDefinitionContent.description: A tool-definition set, keyed by its content hash within the tenant.

definition.description: A tools array in its client protocol's wire shape.

risk_level.description:
Highest-severity risk seen across all calls to this tool in the window.
Drives the card's border accent and the `?risk=` row filter; the UI
renders the per-risk breakdown via the *_count fields below.

tool_id.description:
Canonical tool concept resolved through the field-profile registry.
`None` when no profile matched `(tool_name, app_id, mcp_server)`.

unknown_count.description: Calls that matched no risk rule.

ToolIdEntry.description:
One entry in the canonical `tool_id` taxonomy shipped with the engine.
`seeds/tool-policy/tool_ids.json` is documentation + UI hint, not an
enforced enum — operators can introduce custom ids via the modal.

call_event.description:
Canonical `ConversationEvent::ToolCall` event — rendered by the UI with
the same component the session view uses.

latency_total_ms.description:
Call-side `gateway_audit.latency_total_ms`. Surfaced on the unified
tool-call row card's header strip so LLM rows align visually with
MCP / web rows. `None` for synthetic blocked invocations whose call
turn was suppressed before the latency was stamped.

oneOf.description: Canonical `ConversationEvent::ToolResult` event when paired.

user_email.description:
Raw email of the row's user (when resolved). Distinct from
`user_display` (which falls back to display name or id). Drives the
row-card "filter by user" button so the click reapplies a precise
email filter, not the display-name fallback.

ToolRiskFilter.description: The `risk` a tool-inventory list can narrow to.

ToolRuleDetector.description: One entry of the detector registry, as the rule editor renders it.

label.description: Operator-facing name for the option list.

name.description: Wire value for a condition's `value` when `op` is `detector`.

summary.description: One line describing what the detector recognises.

a2a_agent_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the A2A upstream agent's slug
(`a2a_upstream_agents.slug`, e.g. `research-prod`, `partner-*`). The
agent is the pivot of the `agent_calls` scope the way the upstream is
the pivot of MCP rules. Non-A2A traffic never matches a rule with this
filter set; `None` means "any agent".

app_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the request's `app_id` (client
identity, e.g. `claude-code`, `cursor-*`). When set, the rule only
fires for matching apps. `None` means "any app".

enabled.description: Inert when false; preserved in storage. `extract_for` skips disabled rules.

forked_from.description:
Copy-on-write link: when set on a `Some(P)` rule, this is a per-profile
**fork** of the shared rule with this id — it *suppresses* that shared rule
inside P (an override). Deleting the fork reverts P to the shared rule.

id.description:
Stable operator-visible identifier (e.g. `ASI02-06`). Surfaces on
blocked-tool banners and transform diffs so reviewers know which rule
fired without parsing the description. Every rule carries one: a seed
names it, and a rule created through the API is given one.

is_builtin.description:
Server-managed: `true` on initial seed and on `actions/reset`, `false`
after the first PATCH/PUT. Ignored on incoming client payloads.

match.description: AND-of-conditions. Empty means "every item in scope" (catch-all).

mcp_server_filter.description:
Optional pipe-separated glob over the MCP upstream server name
(`mcp_upstream_servers.name`, e.g. `notion-prod`, `internal-*`).
When set, the rule only fires for matching upstreams; `None` means
"any upstream". Non-MCP traffic (LLM tool calls without an MCP
namespace) never matches a rule with this filter set — pairs
naturally with `(request, resource_reads | prompt_invocations)`
rules. Use this to keep per-upstream policies (and per-test rules)
from spilling onto other servers in the same tenant.

model_filter.description: Optional pipe-separated glob over the resolved upstream model name.

priority.description:
Lower wins. Default 100. Stable-sorted with original list position as
the tiebreaker so manual ordering still controls equal-priority rules.

profile_id.description:
Profile scope. `None` → **shared**: the rule applies to every profile (the
baseline; builtins live here). `Some(P)` → **specific** to profile P. The
snapshot bucketer fans shared rules into every profile's bucket.

risk.description:
